name: Egg Omelet
description: A quick and fluffy 2-egg omelet, simply seasoned and cooked in butter.
instructions: Beat 2 eggs in a bowl and season with salt and pepper.
Heat butter in a pan over medium heat, pour in the eggs and cook until set.
Fold the omelet and serve hot.

name: Chicken Soup
description: A comforting, hearty broth-based soup with tender chicken and vegetables.
instructions: Place chicken, carrots, celery, and onions in a pot with water and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Add noodles if desired and cook until tender.

name: Spaghetti Bolognese
description: A classic Italian pasta dish with a rich, slow-simmered beef and tomato sauce.
instructions: Brown 400g minced beef in a pan with chopped onion and 2 garlic cloves.
Add crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, salt, pepper, and dried oregano. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook spaghetti according to package instructions until al dente, then drain.
Serve the spaghetti topped with the sauce and grated Parmesan.

name: Tomato Basil Soup
description: A creamy, blended tomato soup infused with fresh basil, perfect with crusty bread.
instructions: Sauté chopped onion and 2 garlic cloves in olive oil until soft.
Add 600g chopped tomatoes and 400ml vegetable broth. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Blend until smooth, then stir in fresh basil, salt, and pepper. Serve with crusty bread.

name: Banana Pancakes
description: Soft, fluffy pancakes made with ripe mashed bananas, great for breakfast.
instructions: Mash 2 ripe bananas in a bowl. Mix in 2 eggs, 1/2 cup flour, 1/2 cup milk, and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Heat a lightly buttered pan over medium heat. Pour small ladles of batter and cook until bubbles form, then flip.
Cook until golden on both sides. Serve with honey or maple syrup.

name: Grilled Cheese Sandwich
description: A golden, crispy buttered sandwich oozing with melted cheese.
instructions: Butter one side of each of 2 bread slices. Place one slice butter-side-down in a pan over medium heat.
Layer with 2 slices of cheese and top with the second slice butter-side-up. Cook 3 minutes per side until golden and the cheese has melted. Serve immediately.

name: Chicken Stir-Fry
description: A quick, colorful stir-fry of chicken and crisp vegetables in a savory soy-sesame sauce.
instructions: Slice 500g chicken breast thin. Heat oil in a wok over high heat and cook chicken for 5 minutes.
Add sliced bell peppers, carrots, and broccoli. Stir-fry for 4 minutes.
Mix 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, and 1 tsp sesame oil; pour over vegetables. Toss well and serve over steamed rice.

name: Apple Cinnamon Oatmeal
description: Warm, creamy oatmeal sweetened with honey and spiced with cinnamon and fresh apple.
instructions: Bring 2 cups of milk to a gentle simmer. Stir in 1 cup rolled oats and cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Dice 1 apple and add it along with 1 tsp cinnamon and a pinch of salt. Cook 2 more minutes.
Sweeten with honey and serve warm.

name: Vegetable Stew
description: A hearty, slow-simmered stew loaded with root vegetables in a savory tomato broth.
instructions: Dice and sauté an onion and 2 garlic cloves in olive oil until soft.
Add diced potatoes, carrots, celery, and zucchini. Pour in 600ml vegetable broth and a can of diced tomatoes.
Season with thyme, rosemary, salt, and pepper. Simmer 30 minutes until vegetables are tender.

name: Caprese Salad
description: A fresh Italian salad of tomatoes, mozzarella, and basil drizzled with olive oil and balsamic.
instructions: Slice 3 large tomatoes and 200g fresh mozzarella into rounds.
Alternate tomato and mozzarella slices on a plate. Tuck fresh basil leaves between slices.
Drizzle with extra-virgin olive oil and balsamic glaze. Season with salt and freshly ground black pepper.

name: Pasta Carbonara
description: A creamy Italian pasta with crispy bacon, eggs, and Parmesan.
instructions: Boil spaghetti in salted water according to package instructions.
Meanwhile, cook bacon in a pan until lightly browned. In a bowl, whisk eggs with sour cream and grated Parmesan.
Drain pasta and immediately toss with the bacon and egg mixture. Season with salt and pepper. Finish with extra Parmesan.

name: Pasta with Tomato and Mushroom Sauce
description: A comforting pasta tossed in a savory tomato and mushroom sauce.
instructions: Boil pasta in salted water according to package instructions.
Sauté a chopped onion in oil, then add mushrooms and cook until tender. Stir in tomato sauce and simmer until creamy.
Drain pasta and mix with the sauce. Sprinkle with grated Parmesan to serve.

name: Green Salad with Tuna and Corn
description: A light, refreshing salad with lettuce, tuna, and sweet corn.
instructions: Wash and tear lettuce leaves into a bowl. Drain the canned tuna and corn, then add them to the salad.
Drizzle with olive oil and freshly squeezed lemon juice. Season with salt and toss gently to combine.

name: Cheese and Herb Omelet
description: A fluffy omelet packed with melted cheese and fresh herbs.
instructions: Beat 3–4 eggs in a deep bowl. Stir in grated cheese and finely chopped fresh herbs (spring onion, green garlic, or dill). Season with salt.
Heat a drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil in a pan, pour in the mixture, and cook over medium heat for about 15 minutes until set.

name: Asian-Style Rice with Chicken
description: Fragrant rice paired with grilled chicken and a splash of soy sauce.
instructions: Cook rice in a rice cooker with 2 tbsp oil and water according to package directions.
Meanwhile, grill chicken breast on a grill pan until cooked through. Dice the chicken into small cubes.
When rice is done, mix with the chicken and drizzle soy sauce to taste.

name: Turkey Breast on a Bed of Vegetables
description: Oven-baked turkey breast served over a bed of roasted vegetables.
instructions: Line a baking tray with parchment paper. Spread frozen vegetables over it and drizzle with olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Lay turkey breast slices on top and season with salt. Bake in a preheated oven until the turkey is golden and cooked through.

name: Cream of Mushroom Soup
description: A smooth, velvety mushroom soup blended with cream.
instructions: Clean 1 kg of champignon mushrooms and boil them in water until tender. Finely chop one large onion.
Drain the mushrooms and place them in a blender together with the onion and cooking cream. Blend until smooth and creamy.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.

name: Chicken and Cheese Puff Pastry Braid
description: A golden, flaky pastry braid filled with chicken, mushrooms, and cheese.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into small cubes and lightly brown in a pan. Roll out puff pastry dough.
Place the chicken, canned mushrooms, and grated cheese down the center. Season with salt and pepper.
Fold the dough over in a braid shape, brush the top with beaten egg, and bake until golden and crispy.

name: Flatbread Pizza
description: Quick and crispy flatbread pizzas topped with cheese and savory toppings.
instructions: Place flatbreads on a parchment-lined baking tray. Spread tomato sauce over each one.
Top with bacon, mushrooms, olives, and corn to taste. Sprinkle generously with grated cheese. Bake in a preheated oven until the cheese is melted and bubbly.

name: Chicken Skewers in a Pan
description: Juicy chicken and vegetable skewers pan-grilled to perfection.
instructions: Thread cubed chicken breast, red bell pepper, mushrooms, cherry tomatoes, olives, and onion onto skewer sticks. Season with a pinch of salt.
Cook the skewers in a grill pan, turning occasionally, until the chicken is browned and cooked through.

name: Crispy Sandwich
description: A toasted, oven-baked sandwich stuffed with ham, cheese, and fresh veggies.
instructions: Toast 2 slices of bread, then spread with butter. Layer with pressed ham and plenty of cheese slices.
Add fresh lettuce and sliced cucumber for freshness. Top with grated cheese and bake in the oven on a flat tray for about 10 minutes until the cheese has melted.

name: French Potato Pudding
description: A baked potato and cheese casserole enriched with eggs and butter.
instructions: Wash and dice potatoes into small cubes; boil until tender.
Transfer to an oven-safe dish and mix with grated telemea cheese, well-beaten eggs, butter, and a pinch of salt. Bake in the oven until the top is nicely browned.

name: Rice with Mexican Vegetables
description: Fluffy rice tossed with buttery sautéed mixed vegetables.
instructions: Boil long-grain rice in salted water until cooked. Meanwhile, sauté fresh or frozen mixed vegetables in a pan with a knob of butter until tender.
Combine the cooked rice and vegetables, season with salt and pepper, and serve hot.

name: Chicken with Mushrooms in Cream Sauce
description: Tender chicken and mushrooms simmered in a rich, creamy sauce.
instructions: Cut the chicken breast into cubes. In a pan with oil, brown the meat over medium heat, stirring frequently. Remove the chicken to a plate.
In the same pan, sauté the finely chopped onion for 2-3 minutes. Add the sliced mushrooms, season with salt and pepper, and cook until golden.
Pour in 400 ml of heavy cream and cook for a few minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Add the chicken back and stir well. Sprinkle with freshly chopped parsley, cover with a lid, and leave for 2-3 minutes. Serve warm.

name: Pork and Potato Stew
description: A slow-cooked stew of pork, bacon, and potatoes in a savory tomato broth.
instructions: Cut the pork neck into cubes and coat them in flour. Place in a pot together with the diced smoked bacon and a little oil. Brown the meat well on all sides, then set aside.
In the same oil, sauté the diced onion for 2 minutes. Add the minced garlic and sliced carrot, and sauté for another 1-2 minutes.

Add the tomato sauce, browned meat, and 500 ml of clear broth or water. Season with salt, pepper, and a bay leaf. Cover and cook over low heat for 1 hour. Add the diced potatoes and cook for another 20 minutes or until tender. Serve warm.

name: Oven-Baked Chicken with Potatoes
description: Chicken thighs roasted over seasoned potatoes with a garlicky, creamy sauce.
instructions: Peel and slice the potatoes (≈0.5 cm thick). Toss in a bowl with olive oil, salt, and thyme.
Pour 2-3 tbsp of olive oil into a baking tray. Slice the 4 onions and spread them evenly in the tray. Layer the seasoned potatoes on top.
Blend the garlic (5 cloves), milk, sunflower oil, tomato paste, paprika, thyme, salt, and pepper until you get a smooth sauce.
Place the chicken thighs over the potatoes, pour the sauce over the meat, and tuck in the asparagus and the whole garlic head. Bake at 220°C for 60 minutes. Serve immediately.

name: Penne Quattro Formaggi
description: A rich, cheesy penne pasta made with four kinds of melted cheese.
instructions: Boil 250g penne according to package instructions, about 8 minutes until al dente.

Separately, prepare the sauce. Melt butter in a pan and add cream, salt and pepper to taste. Cut the cheeses into small pieces if not already grated, and when the cream starts to boil, add them to the pan. Mix everything for 5 minutes until all ingredients have melted and combined perfectly.
Let the sauce thicken for 2-3 more minutes on low heat. Add the penne using two spatulas and mix well. Sprinkle with oregano before serving.

name: Pasta Arrabiata
description: A spicy Italian pasta with a fiery tomato and hot pepper sauce.
instructions: Boil spaghetti in salted water for about 8 minutes until al dente, then rinse under cold water.

Separately, prepare the sauce. Clean the hot peppers from seeds, slice them into 2-3 cm pieces and put them in a pan with 4-5 tbsp oil. Add finely chopped garlic and let everything sauté for 3 minutes. Deglaze with a little water and add the tomato sauce.
In 10 minutes the arrabiata sauce is almost ready. Add lemon juice, parmesan and 2 tbsp olive oil. Mix the pasta with the sauce and serve with grated parmesan on top.

name: Pasta with Chicken and Pesto
description: Pasta tossed with grilled chicken, homemade basil pesto, and cherry tomatoes.
instructions: Remove chicken from refrigerator 30 minutes before cooking to reach room temperature. Boil the pasta and prepare the pesto sauce. Using a blender, blend raw basil, cashews, garlic, parmesan, 2 tbsp olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper to taste.

When the pesto sauce is ready, lightly brush the chicken breast pieces with it and let them reach room temperature for 20-30 minutes. Using a suitable pan, heat 2 tbsp olive oil and cook the meat until fully fried. Add cherry tomatoes and sauté for 5 minutes.
When the chicken breast is ready, cut it into thin pieces and mix with the pasta, sauce, and cherry tomatoes. Serve with grated parmesan on top.

name: Pasta with Shrimp
description: A garlicky shrimp pasta finished with lemon and white wine flavors.
instructions: Boil water and when it starts to boil, add the pasta. Separately, peel the shrimp by first removing the head, then the shell and intestine. Don't throw away the remains; boil them in a little water just to cover them. Let them boil for a few minutes, then strain the broth into a glass as you will need it later.

While the shrimp broth is cooking, heat oil, butter, garlic, and finely chopped hot pepper in a pan. Mix gently for 3 minutes. Add the shrimp and let them sauté for 2 minutes. When the shrimp turn pink, add a glass of the broth and let everything boil for 3-4 minutes.
Add lemon juice, salt and pepper. Mix well and finally add the pasta and parsley to the pan. Serve with grated parmesan on top and a glass of white wine.

name: Pasta with Garlic and Hot Pepper
description: A simple, spicy pasta tossed in garlic, hot pepper, and olive oil.
instructions: Boil the spaghetti according to package instructions. Meanwhile, slice the pepper and garlic, and finely chop the parsley. Sauté the garlic and pepper in olive oil for a few minutes.

Add 2 ladles of the pasta cooking water, then add the finely chopped parsley. Leave the pan on the heat for a few minutes and finally add the cooked pasta to the pan. Season with salt and basil. Mix everything well and serve with grated parmesan on top.

name: Baked Salmon with Asparagus
description: Oven-baked salmon fillets with a garlicky lemon-herb sauce and roasted asparagus.
instructions: Preheat the oven and grease a baking tray with olive oil. Place the salmon fillets and season with salt and pepper.
Mix olive oil, garlic, herbs, and juice from half a lemon. Pour this sauce over the salmon fillets, ensuring it covers all surfaces.

Wash the asparagus and cut off the woody stems. Arrange asparagus around the edges with salmon in the center and drizzle with olive oil. Slice the remaining lemon thinly and cover each piece of salmon with a slice.
Bake for 12-15 minutes or until the fish is opaque and flaky when tested with a fork. Garnish with fresh thyme or parsley and serve alongside the asparagus.

name: Baked Salmon with Vegetables
description: Buttery baked salmon served alongside a medley of roasted vegetables.
instructions: Remove salmon from refrigerator and let it reach room temperature for about 15 minutes. Preheat the oven. In a small bowl, mix melted butter and lemon juice.
Using a brush, apply the butter mixture over the salmon fillets in a baking dish. Sprinkle with chopped garlic, salt, and pepper. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes.

Meanwhile, cut the vegetables according to their density so they cook evenly. Cauliflower can remain medium-sized florets, while broccoli should be separated into smaller florets. Place vegetables with cut side down in another baking tray and drizzle with olive oil. Bake vegetables for 30 minutes. When done, sprinkle with fresh parsley and dill. Serve the salmon alongside the roasted vegetables.

name: Classic Beef Soup
description: A traditional, hearty beef and vegetable soup simmered until tender.
instructions: Wash and clean the vegetables, then cut the carrots into rounds, and dice the celery, bell pepper, and potatoes. Finely chop the onion.

Put approximately 4 liters of water in a pot and add the diced beef. Let the meat boil until foam forms on top (approximately 20 minutes), which you will remove with a skimmer. Let the meat boil for another 20-30 minutes, removing foam occasionally.
Once no more foam forms, add the onion, carrots, and celery and let them boil for another 20-30 minutes. Then add the bell pepper, peas, and potatoes and let them boil for 15 minutes.
Once cooked, add the tomato juice, a little salt and olive oil, and let the soup boil for another 15 minutes. When the soup is ready, add the chopped parsley and serve.

name: Sour Beef Soup
description: A tangy Romanian-style beef soup soured with bors and topped with sour cream.
instructions: Start by putting the beef on the bone to boil in cold water with salt. Boil the meat over low heat while removing the foam that forms on the surface. Meanwhile, prepare the root vegetables. Clean, wash and finely chop the onion, and cut the carrots, celery, and parsley root into cubes.

Once no more foam forms, pierce the meat with a fork to see if it's cooked more than halfway. Then add the root vegetables. Let the soup boil over low heat while you prepare the remaining vegetables. Cut the pepper into cubes, peel and cube the potatoes.

Once the root vegetables start to soften, add the pepper, peas, and finely chopped white cabbage. Check if the meat is cooked. When the fork goes in easily, remove it from the pot, let it cool slightly, then cut into cubes. Put the meat back in the pot.
When the vegetables are almost cooked, add the potatoes. Once they're cooked, add the tomatoes that you've previously scalded, peeled, and cubed.

Boil the bors separately and add it to the soup. Let the contents come to two boils and remove the pot from heat. Add salt and pepper to taste, as well as finely chopped lovage. Serve with a little sour cream.

name: Transylvanian Veal Soup with Sour Cream
description: A rich veal soup finished with an egg yolk and sour cream mixture.
instructions: Start by putting the veal to boil together with the veal bones in a pot with cold water, salt, and a few peppercorns. Let the meat boil for approximately 45 minutes, during which you will skim constantly until the broth remains clear.

Meanwhile, wash and clean the vegetables. Cut the potatoes into cubes, carrots into rounds, parsnip, parsley root, and celery into cubes, and finely chop the onion. Add two tablespoons of oil to a pan and briefly sauté the carrots.

When the meat is almost cooked, remove it from the pot and cut into cubes. Strain the soup separately into another pot, add the veal and prepared vegetables. Let everything boil and add celery and parsley leaves. When the veal soup boils, add the thyme sprig, bay leaf, pepper, and a little ground cumin. Then add two level tablespoons of sweet paprika and tomato juice. Let everything boil until the vegetables are soft.

When the veal soup is cooked, remove the celery leaves and thyme sprig. Prepare the egg yolk and sour cream mixture: Mix the sour cream with the egg yolks and 2 tablespoons of soup until the mixture thins, then add it to the soup and mix well. Optionally, add a little lemon juice to taste.

name: Country-Style Beef Soup
description: A rustic, vegetable-packed beef soup with a tangy tomato and bors broth.
instructions: Remove the meat from the bone and wash it well, then cut it into cubes. Put the cubed meat and bones to boil in a pot with water and salt for approximately one hour. Skim constantly until the broth remains clear. The meat should be soft when pierced with a fork.

Meanwhile, prepare the vegetables and remove the bones from the pot. Wash, clean, and cut the carrots, onion, potatoes, bell pepper, parsnip root, and celery. Finely chop the white cabbage. Add the cut vegetables to the pot where the meat is boiling (without potatoes), along with the peas and green beans. Let the soup boil over low heat.

When the vegetables and meat are tender, add the potatoes and let them boil for approximately 20 minutes. Then add the tomatoes in broth and bors to taste. Let it come to a few boils and add salt to taste. When ready, remove the pot from heat and add finely chopped lovage and parsley.

name: Classic Tomato Soup
description: A traditional Romanian tomato soup made with fresh tomatoes and root vegetables.
instructions: Blanch the tomatoes in boiling water for 2-3 minutes, then peel them and remove the woody part near the stem. Put the tomatoes in a pot with water to cover, bay leaves, thyme sprigs, and basil sprigs, and boil for 15-20 minutes.

Meanwhile, peel and finely dice the carrots, onions, celery, parsnip, both bell peppers, and garlic. In a large pot, sauté all the diced vegetables over low heat until softened, then add 250 ml of water.

Once the tomatoes have finished boiling, remove them, discard the herbs, and blend the tomatoes into a smooth paste. Add the tomato paste to the sautéed vegetables and top up with water. Simmer until the soup reaches the desired consistency, then season with salt and pepper. Serve with sour cream and chopped fresh herbs on top.

name: Tomato Soup with Homemade Noodles
description: A hearty tomato soup made even more satisfying with fresh, hand-cut egg noodles.
instructions: First prepare the noodle dough: beat the egg in a bowl, then pour it into the center of the flour mixed with a pinch of salt. Combine and knead into a dough, adding a splash of warm water if it's too stiff. Let the dough rest for 30 minutes.

While it rests, peel and dice the carrots, bell pepper, onion, celery, and parsnip, then sauté them in oil for a few minutes until soft and add water to cover. Meanwhile, boil the tomatoes in water for 2-3 minutes, peel them, and blend into a smooth paste, then add it to the simmering vegetables.
Roll the rested dough into a thin sheet, let it dry for 30 minutes, then roll it up and slice into thin strips to make the noodles.
Sprinkle the noodles into the simmering soup like rain, stirring so they don't stick together, and cook for 10 minutes. Season with salt, pepper, and chopped fresh parsley before serving.

name: Tomato Soup with Semolina Dumplings
description: A well-known meatless Romanian soup, tangy and filling thanks to fluffy semolina dumplings.
instructions: Finely chop the onion and sauté it in oil for 2-3 minutes until soft. Dice the carrots and add them to the pot along with 3 liters of water, letting everything boil over high heat. Thinly slice the garlic and add it along with the chopped parsley, then let it all boil for 15-20 minutes. Pour in the tomato juice and let the soup continue simmering.
Meanwhile, prepare the dumplings: in a separate bowl, beat the eggs, season with salt and pepper, then sift in the semolina, mixing well so no lumps form. Let the mixture rest for 4-5 minutes.

Turn off the heat under the soup and drop spoonfuls of the dumpling mixture into it. Once all the dumplings are added, bring the soup back to a gentle simmer until the dumplings have puffed up and the vegetables are fully cooked. Season with salt and pepper to taste before serving.

name: Cream of Tomato Soup
description: A tangy, velvety blended tomato soup packed with root vegetables and potatoes.
instructions: Wash and peel the vegetables for the soup base (carrots, onion, garlic, bell pepper, parsnip, and celery), then dice them finely. Sauté the diced vegetables in a large pot for 3-4 minutes, then add about 4 liters of water. Cube the potatoes and zucchini and add them to the pot to boil along with the other vegetables.
Meanwhile, boil the tomatoes for 5-6 minutes so they're easy to peel. Once cooled and peeled, blend them with a hand blender or grate them into a smooth paste.
When the vegetables are fully cooked, remove them from the broth and blend them into a fine paste as well. Mix this vegetable paste back into the broth, then stir in the tomato paste.
Let the cream soup simmer for a few minutes, then season with salt, pepper, and other spices to taste. Serve with a few croutons, sour cream, and chopped parsley.

name: Tomato Soup with Garlic
description: A fragrant tomato soup infused with plenty of garlic, basil, and thyme.
instructions: Wash the tomatoes and cut them in half, then boil them for a few minutes until they soften well. Once they start to peel easily, pass them through a fine sieve to obtain a smooth paste.

In a separate pot, heat the oil for 1-2 minutes, then sauté the finely chopped garlic and onion for 5 minutes. Add the tomato paste along with the dried thyme and basil sprigs, and let everything simmer for 15 minutes. Add water and salt depending on how thick you want the soup, and let it come to a boil.

Cover the pot with a lid and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes. Finally, remove the basil sprigs and blend the whole soup with a mixer or hand blender until smooth. Serve with grated parmesan and croutons.

name: Gazpacho
description: A refreshing, chilled Spanish-style tomato and vegetable soup, perfect for hot summer days.
instructions: Soak the bread slices in water until soft. Meanwhile, wash, peel, and dice the tomatoes, cucumbers, bell pepper, onion, and garlic.

Place all the vegetables in a blender and blend until the mixture becomes a smooth paste. Add the soaked bread slices, lemon juice, olive oil, salt, and freshly ground pepper, then continue blending until fully combined.
Chill the gazpacho in the refrigerator for a few hours before serving with a few croutons or grated parmesan on top.

name: Turkish Tomato Soup
description: A simple, quick tomato soup thickened with a light flour roux and finished with milk.
instructions: Heat the oil in a suitably sized pot. Add the flour and let it brown lightly for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly. Pour the tomato juice over the flour and oil mixture and let it cook until it comes to a boil.

Once the juice starts boiling, add the salt, dried basil, and dried oregano. Lower the heat and slowly pour in the milk, stirring carefully with a wooden spoon. Let the soup cook for another 5-10 minutes, then serve with a few spoonfuls of grated cheese on top.

name: Mămăligă cu Brânză și Ou
description: Creamy Romanian polenta topped with crumbled telemea, a fried egg and a spoonful of sour cream.
instructions: Bring the water to a boil with the salt in a heavy pot.
Pour in the cornmeal in a thin stream while whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Reduce the heat and cook for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until thick and pulling away from the sides.
Melt the butter in a pan and fry the eggs sunny-side up until the whites are set.
Spoon the mămăligă onto plates, crumble the telemea on top and add the fried egg.
Finish with a dollop of sour cream and freshly ground black pepper.

name: Ouă Ochiuri Românești
description: Soft water-poached eggs with runny yolks, served the Romanian way with butter, telemea and fresh bread.
instructions: Fill a wide pan with water, add the vinegar and a pinch of salt, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Crack each egg into a small cup and slide it carefully into the barely simmering water.
Poach for 3 minutes until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.
Lift the eggs out with a slotted spoon and drain briefly on a paper towel.
Place on warm plates, top each egg with a sliver of butter and season with pepper.
Serve with slices of telemea, fresh bread and green onions.

name: Papară
description: Thrifty Romanian scramble of torn bread fried golden in butter, bound with eggs and finished with cheese.
instructions: Tear the bread into bite-sized pieces.
Melt the butter in a large pan and fry the bread over medium heat until golden and slightly crisp.
Beat the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper.
Pour the eggs over the bread and stir gently until just set.
Crumble the telemea on top, take off the heat and let it soften for a minute.
Serve hot with chopped green onions.

name: Clătite cu Gem
description: Thin, lacy Romanian crepes rolled around fruit jam and dusted with powdered sugar.
instructions: Whisk the eggs with the sugar, vanilla sugar and a pinch of salt.
Add the milk and sparkling water, then whisk in the flour until the batter is smooth and thin.
Stir in the melted butter and let the batter rest for 15 minutes.
Heat a lightly oiled non-stick pan and pour in a small ladle of batter, swirling to coat the base.
Cook for about 1 minute per side until golden, then stack the crepes on a plate.
Spread each crepe with jam, roll up and dust with powdered sugar before serving.

name: Clătite cu Brânză Dulce la Cuptor
description: Crepes filled with sweet vanilla cottage cheese and raisins, baked under a sour cream glaze until golden.
instructions: Whisk the eggs, milk, flour and a pinch of salt into a thin batter and cook 8 crepes in a lightly oiled pan.
Mix the cottage cheese with the sugar, vanilla extract, lemon zest, raisins and one egg yolk.
Place a spoonful of filling on each crepe and roll it up, tucking in the sides.
Arrange the rolls snugly in a buttered baking dish.
Whisk the sour cream with a tablespoon of sugar and spread it over the crepes.
Bake at 180°C for 20 minutes until lightly golden on top and serve warm.

name: Plăcintă cu Brânză Sărată
description: Flaky phyllo pie layered with salty telemea, eggs and dill, baked until crisp and golden.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C and brush a rectangular baking dish with melted butter.
Crumble the telemea and mix it with the cottage cheese, 3 eggs, chopped dill and pepper.
Layer half the phyllo sheets in the dish, brushing every second sheet with melted butter.
Spread the cheese filling evenly, then cover with the remaining sheets, buttering as you go.
Whisk the last egg with the yogurt and pour it over the top, letting it soak in.
Score into squares and bake for 40 minutes until deep golden. Cool slightly before cutting.

name: Plăcintă cu Mere
description: Crisp phyllo apple pie with grated apples, cinnamon and semolina, perfect warm with morning coffee.
instructions: Peel and coarsely grate the apples, then squeeze out the excess juice.
Cook the apples with the sugar and cinnamon in a pan for 8 minutes until softened. Stir in the semolina and cool.
Preheat the oven to 180°C and butter a baking dish.
Layer half the phyllo sheets in the dish, brushing each with melted butter.
Spread the apple filling evenly and cover with the remaining buttered sheets.
Bake for 35 minutes until golden, cool for 10 minutes and dust with powdered sugar.

name: Griș cu Lapte
description: Silky warm semolina pudding simmered in vanilla milk and swirled with fruit jam.
instructions: Bring the milk to a simmer with the sugar, vanilla sugar and a pinch of salt.
Pour the semolina in a thin stream while whisking constantly.
Cook over low heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy.
Take off the heat and stir in the butter.
Spoon into bowls and top each with a swirl of jam and a dusting of cinnamon.

name: Orez cu Lapte
description: Comforting Romanian rice pudding cooked slowly in milk with lemon zest and a cinnamon dusting.
instructions: Rinse the rice and simmer it in the water for 10 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Add the milk, sugar, lemon zest and a pinch of salt and bring back to a gentle simmer.
Cook uncovered over low heat for 25 minutes, stirring often, until creamy.
Stir in the vanilla sugar and butter and take off the heat.
Serve warm or chilled, dusted with cinnamon and topped with jam.

name: Papanași
description: Golden fried cottage cheese doughnuts, piled with sour cream and sour cherry jam.
instructions: Mix the cottage cheese with the egg, sugar, vanilla sugar, lemon zest and a pinch of salt.
Work in the flour and baking soda to get a soft dough that is just firm enough to shape.
With floured hands form 4 rings and 4 small balls from the dough.
Heat the oil to 170°C and fry the rings and balls in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels.
Stack each ring with a ball on top, spoon over sour cream and finish with jam.

name: Scrob cu Slănină Afumată
description: Country-style scrambled eggs cooked in the rendered fat of crispy smoked bacon, with green onions.
instructions: Dice the smoked bacon and fry it in a dry pan over medium heat until crisp and the fat has rendered.
Add the sliced green onions and cook for 1 minute.
Beat the eggs with a splash of milk, salt and pepper.
Pour the eggs into the pan and stir slowly with a spatula until soft curds form.
Remove from the heat while still slightly glossy and serve with bread and tomato wedges.

name: Bulz cu Brânză la Cuptor
description: Shepherd's polenta balls hiding a molten telemea centre, baked with butter and crisp smoked bacon.
instructions: Cook the cornmeal in salted boiling water for 20 minutes, stirring, until very thick. Cool until handleable.
Mix the telemea with the butter and half the sour cream into a soft paste.
With wet hands flatten a portion of polenta, place a spoonful of cheese in the middle and shape into a ball.
Arrange the balls in a buttered dish and scatter the diced smoked bacon around them.
Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until golden on top.
Serve hot with the remaining sour cream and a fried egg if you like.

name: Budincă de Pâine cu Mere
description: Stale bread turned into a custardy baked pudding with apples, raisins and cinnamon.
instructions: Cut the bread into cubes and spread them in a buttered baking dish.
Peel and dice the apples and scatter them with the raisins over the bread.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, sugar, vanilla extract and cinnamon.
Pour the custard over the bread and press down gently so everything soaks. Rest for 15 minutes.
Dot with butter and bake at 180°C for 40 minutes until puffed and golden.
Serve warm, dusted with powdered sugar.

name: Brânzoaice (Poale-n Brâu)
description: Soft yeasted Moldavian buns folded around a sweet cottage cheese and raisin filling.
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and a teaspoon of sugar in the warm milk and let it foam for 10 minutes.
Mix the flour, remaining sugar, 2 eggs, melted butter and salt with the yeast milk into a soft dough. Knead 10 minutes.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Mix the cottage cheese with 1 egg, sugar, vanilla sugar, lemon zest and raisins.
Roll the dough and cut into 12 squares. Put filling in the centre and fold the corners to the middle.
Brush with beaten egg and bake at 180°C for 25 minutes until golden.

name: Platou de Mic Dejun Românesc
description: No-cook country platter of telemea, tomatoes, cucumber, green onions, olives, ham and fresh bread.
instructions: Cut the telemea and cascaval into thick slices and arrange on a large board.
Slice the tomatoes and cucumber into wedges and add them alongside.
Trim the green onions and fold the ham slices beside the cheese.
Add a small bowl of olives and spoon the zacuscă into another.
Slice the bread and serve everything with butter, salt and pepper on the side.

name: Syrniki Cottage Cheese Pancakes
description: Thick, tender Eastern European cottage cheese pancakes, fried golden and served with sour cream and jam.
instructions: Press the cottage cheese through a sieve for a smooth texture.
Mix it with the egg, sugar, vanilla extract and a pinch of salt.
Add the flour and stir until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms.
Shape into 8 thick patties and dredge lightly in extra flour.
Fry in butter over medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Serve warm with sour cream and jam.

name: Buckwheat Porridge with Milk
description: Nutty toasted buckwheat simmered until tender, served warm with milk, butter and honey.
instructions: Toast the buckwheat groats in a dry pan for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Add the water and salt, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Take off the heat and let it steam, covered, for 5 minutes.
Stir in the butter.
Spoon into bowls, pour over warm milk and drizzle with honey.

name: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a spiced tomato and pepper sauce with cumin and paprika, served with crusty bread.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a wide pan and soften the diced onion and bell pepper for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, paprika and chili flakes and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes, season with salt and pepper and simmer for 10 minutes until thickened.
Make 4 wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook for 6 to 8 minutes until the whites are set but the yolks still soft.
Scatter with parsley and crumbled feta and serve straight from the pan with bread.

name: Green Shakshuka
description: A fresh twist on shakshuka: eggs baked into wilted spinach, leek and herbs with creamy feta.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pan and cook the sliced leek and garlic for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the spinach in handfuls and stir until wilted, then season with salt, pepper and cumin.
Stir in the chopped dill and parsley and a squeeze of lemon juice.
Make 4 wells in the greens and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook on low for 6 to 7 minutes until the whites are set.
Crumble the feta on top and serve with yogurt and warm pita.

name: Spinach and Feta Frittata
description: Fluffy oven-finished frittata packed with spinach, red onion, feta and fresh dill.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C.
Heat the olive oil in an ovenproof pan and soften the sliced red onion for 4 minutes.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted, then spread it evenly in the pan.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, dill, salt and pepper and pour over the vegetables.
Crumble the feta on top and cook on the stove for 3 minutes until the edges set.
Transfer to the oven for 12 minutes until puffed and just set in the centre. Slice into wedges.

name: Potato and Chorizo Frittata
description: Spanish-style frittata with crisp-edged potatoes, smoky chorizo and sweet onion, baked until golden.
instructions: Peel the potatoes, cut into 1 cm cubes and boil in salted water for 8 minutes. Drain well.
Fry the diced chorizo in an ovenproof pan for 3 minutes until the oil runs red, then add the sliced onion and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes and fry until lightly browned.
Whisk the eggs with the smoked paprika, parsley, salt and pepper and pour over the pan.
Cook on low for 5 minutes until the edges set, then bake at 190°C for 12 minutes.
Cool slightly, slice into wedges and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Baked Eggs in Avocado
description: Halved avocados baked with an egg nestled inside, finished with crispy bacon bits and chives.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Halve the avocados, remove the stones and scoop out a little flesh to make room for the eggs.
Set the halves in a small baking dish so they sit level.
Crack an egg into each half, season with salt, pepper and chili flakes.
Bake for 15 minutes until the whites are set.
Meanwhile fry the bacon until crisp, crumble it over the eggs and scatter with chives.

name: Smoked Salmon Scrambled Eggs
description: Slow-cooked creamy scrambled eggs folded with smoked salmon and chives, served on buttered toast.
instructions: Whisk the eggs with the cream, a pinch of salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a non-stick pan over low heat and pour in the eggs.
Stir slowly and constantly with a spatula until soft, glossy curds form, about 5 minutes.
Tear the smoked salmon into pieces and fold it in with the chives just before the eggs finish.
Toast and butter the bread and pile the eggs on top. Serve with lemon wedges.

name: Menemen
description: Turkish soft scrambled eggs cooked into sweet green peppers and juicy tomatoes with a hint of chili.
instructions: Heat the olive oil and butter in a pan and cook the diced green peppers for 5 minutes.
Grate the tomatoes and add them with the chili flakes, salt and pepper. Simmer 8 minutes until jammy.
Lightly beat the eggs and pour them into the pan.
Stir gently over low heat until the eggs are just set but still creamy.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve immediately with warm bread.

name: Huevos Rancheros
description: Crisp tortillas topped with black beans, fried eggs, a quick spicy tomato salsa, avocado and coriander.
instructions: Make the salsa: soften the onion and garlic in a little oil, add the crushed tomatoes, chili, cumin and salt and simmer 10 minutes.
Warm the drained beans in a small pan with a pinch of cumin, mashing lightly.
Fry the tortillas in a little oil for 1 minute per side until lightly crisp.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up.
Spread beans over each tortilla, add an egg and spoon over the salsa.
Top with sliced avocado, coriander and a squeeze of lime.

name: Garlic Mushroom Scramble on Toast
description: Buttery garlic and thyme mushrooms folded into soft scrambled eggs, piled onto toasted sourdough-style bread.
instructions: Slice the mushrooms and fry them in half the butter over high heat until golden, about 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and thyme leaves, season and cook 1 minute more. Set aside.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper.
Melt the remaining butter in the pan over low heat and scramble the eggs slowly until softly set.
Fold the mushrooms back in.
Toast the bread, spoon over the scramble and finish with grated parmesan and parsley.

name: Honey and Walnut Porridge
description: Creamy stovetop oat porridge finished with toasted walnuts, a drizzle of honey and sliced banana.
instructions: Combine the oats, milk, water and salt in a saucepan.
Bring to a simmer and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring, until thick and creamy.
Meanwhile toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes and roughly chop.
Stir the cinnamon into the porridge and divide between bowls.
Top with sliced banana, walnuts and a generous drizzle of honey.

name: Berry and Chia Overnight Oats
description: No-cook jar of oats, chia and yogurt soaked overnight, layered with juicy mixed berries.
instructions: Stir together the oats, chia seeds, milk, yogurt, honey and vanilla extract in a bowl.
Divide between two jars, cover and refrigerate overnight (at least 6 hours).
In the morning stir and loosen with a splash of milk if too thick.
Top with the berries and a sprinkle of almonds.

name: Peanut Butter Banana Overnight Oats
description: Thick, satisfying overnight oats with mashed banana, peanut butter and dark chocolate shavings.
instructions: Mash the banana in a bowl and whisk in the peanut butter, milk, yogurt and maple syrup.
Stir in the oats, chia seeds and a pinch of salt.
Spoon into a jar, cover and refrigerate overnight.
Serve topped with grated dark chocolate and a few extra banana slices.

name: Blueberry Baked Oatmeal
description: A sliceable tray of baked oats with bursting blueberries, cinnamon and maple syrup, great for meal prep.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C and butter a 20 cm baking dish.
Mix the oats, baking powder, cinnamon and salt in a bowl.
Whisk the eggs, milk, maple syrup, melted butter and vanilla extract in another bowl.
Combine wet and dry, fold in most of the blueberries and pour into the dish.
Scatter the remaining blueberries and the almonds on top.
Bake for 35 minutes until set and golden. Serve warm with yogurt.

name: Savoury Oat Porridge with Egg and Parmesan
description: Oats cooked risotto-style in broth with parmesan and butter, topped with a fried egg and green onions.
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan and toast the oats for 1 minute.
Add the broth and simmer for 6 minutes, stirring, until creamy.
Stir in the grated parmesan and season with pepper.
Fry the eggs in olive oil until the edges are crisp and the yolks runny.
Spoon the porridge into bowls, top with the eggs, sliced green onions and chili flakes.

name: Fluffy Buttermilk Pancakes
description: Tall, tender American-style pancakes with a buttermilk tang, stacked with butter and maple syrup.
instructions: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
In a jug whisk the buttermilk, eggs, melted butter and vanilla extract.
Pour the wet into the dry and stir until just combined; a few lumps are fine. Rest 5 minutes.
Heat a lightly buttered pan over medium heat and ladle in 80 ml of batter per pancake.
Cook until bubbles form and pop on the surface, about 2 minutes, then flip and cook 1 minute more.
Serve stacked with butter and maple syrup.

name: Belgian Waffles
description: Crisp, deep-pocketed waffles made light with whipped egg whites, topped with strawberries and cream.
instructions: Separate the eggs. Whisk the yolks with the milk, melted butter and vanilla extract.
Stir in the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt until smooth.
Beat the egg whites to soft peaks and fold them gently into the batter.
Preheat and lightly grease the waffle iron.
Cook each waffle for 4 to 5 minutes until golden and crisp.
Serve warm with sliced strawberries, whipped cream and a dusting of powdered sugar.

name: Cinnamon French Toast
description: Thick bread slices soaked in vanilla-cinnamon custard and fried in butter until caramelised and golden.
instructions: Whisk the eggs, milk, sugar, cinnamon and vanilla extract in a shallow dish.
Dip each slice of bread in the custard for 20 seconds per side.
Melt some butter in a large pan over medium heat.
Fry the slices for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden brown.
Serve warm with maple syrup and fresh berries.

name: Savoury French Toast with Ham and Cheese
description: Egg-soaked bread sandwiches with ham and melted cascaval, fried crisp and served with tomatoes.
instructions: Whisk the eggs with the milk, mustard, salt and pepper in a shallow dish.
Make 2 sandwiches with the bread, ham and sliced cascaval.
Dip each sandwich in the egg mixture, letting both sides soak for 20 seconds.
Fry in butter over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and the cheese melts.
Cut in half and serve with sliced tomatoes and chives.

name: Breakfast Burrito
description: Warm tortillas rolled around scrambled eggs, crispy potatoes, bacon, cheese and salsa-style tomatoes.
instructions: Dice the potatoes small and fry in oil for 12 minutes until crisp and golden. Season with paprika and salt.
Fry the bacon until crisp, then chop.
Scramble the eggs in butter until just set.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan.
Fill each tortilla with eggs, potatoes, bacon, grated cheese, diced tomato and a dash of hot sauce.
Fold in the sides and roll tightly. Toast the burritos seam-side down for 1 minute to seal.

name: Bacon, Egg and Cheese Breakfast Sandwich
description: Toasted bun with crispy bacon, a fried egg with a jammy yolk and melted cheddar — a diner classic.
instructions: Fry the bacon in a pan until crisp and set aside on paper towels.
Split and toast the buns in the bacon fat until golden.
Fry the eggs in butter, breaking the yolks lightly if you prefer them set, and lay a slice of cheese on each to melt.
Spread the bun bases with mayonnaise and ketchup.
Stack the bacon, cheesy egg and a few arugula leaves, close the sandwich and serve hot.

name: Avocado Toast with Poached Egg
description: Smashed lemony avocado on toasted whole wheat bread, crowned with a poached egg and chili flakes.
instructions: Bring a pan of water to a gentle simmer with the vinegar.
Mash the avocado with lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Toast the bread and spread thickly with the avocado.
Crack each egg into a cup, slide into the water and poach for 3 minutes.
Lift out, drain and place on the toast.
Finish with chili flakes, a drizzle of olive oil and cherry tomato halves.

name: Smoked Salmon and Cream Cheese Bagel
description: Toasted bagel with dill cream cheese, silky smoked salmon, red onion, capers and cucumber ribbons.
instructions: Mix the cream cheese with chopped dill, lemon zest and a little black pepper.
Split and toast the bagels.
Spread both halves generously with the dill cream cheese.
Layer on the smoked salmon, thin red onion rings and cucumber ribbons.
Scatter with capers, squeeze over lemon juice and close or serve open-faced.

name: Croque Monsieur
description: Parisian café classic: ham and gruyère sandwich under a blanket of nutmeg béchamel, grilled until bubbling.
instructions: Melt 20 g butter, stir in the flour and cook 1 minute. Whisk in the milk gradually and simmer until thick. Season with nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Lightly toast the bread and spread one side of each slice with mustard.
Layer ham and half the grated cheese on 2 slices and close with the other 2 slices.
Spread the béchamel over the tops and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.
Grill under a hot oven grill for 5 to 7 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Serve hot with a few salad leaves.

name: Greek Yogurt Bowl with Figs and Pistachios
description: Thick Greek yogurt with fresh figs, crushed pistachios, honey and a hint of cinnamon — no cooking needed.
instructions: Spoon the yogurt into two bowls and smooth the surface.
Quarter the figs and arrange them on top.
Roughly crush the pistachios and scatter over the figs.
Drizzle generously with honey and dust with cinnamon.
Add a sprinkle of granola for crunch and serve immediately.

name: Berry Smoothie Bowl
description: Thick blended frozen berries and banana topped with granola, fresh fruit, coconut and chia seeds.
instructions: Blend the frozen berries, frozen banana, yogurt and a splash of milk until thick and smooth, scraping down as needed.
Spoon the mixture into a bowl.
Arrange the sliced strawberries and kiwi on top.
Sprinkle with granola, desiccated coconut and chia seeds.
Drizzle with honey and eat right away.

name: Mango Coconut Smoothie Bowl
description: Tropical dairy-free bowl of blended mango, banana and coconut milk, topped with toasted coconut and lime.
instructions: Peel and dice the mango and freeze for at least 2 hours, or use pre-frozen.
Blend the frozen mango, banana, coconut milk and lime juice until thick and creamy.
Toast the desiccated coconut in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden.
Pour the smoothie into a bowl and top with toasted coconut, pumpkin seeds and extra mango.
Finish with a drizzle of agave syrup and mint leaves.

name: Homemade Honey Nut Granola
description: Crunchy oven-baked clusters of oats, almonds, walnuts and seeds glazed with honey and cinnamon.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C and line a tray with baking paper.
Mix the oats, chopped almonds and walnuts, sunflower seeds, cinnamon and salt in a large bowl.
Warm the honey, coconut oil and vanilla extract together until liquid and pour over the oats. Stir to coat.
Spread evenly on the tray and bake for 25 minutes, stirring once halfway, until golden.
Cool completely on the tray so clusters form, then stir in the dried cranberries.
Store in an airtight jar for up to 2 weeks and serve with yogurt or milk.

name: Blueberry Muffins
description: Bakery-style domed muffins bursting with blueberries and a crunchy sugar top.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C and line a 12-hole muffin tin with paper cases.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
In a jug whisk the eggs, milk, melted butter and vanilla extract.
Pour the wet into the dry and stir briefly until just combined, then fold in the blueberries.
Divide between the cases, sprinkle the tops with brown sugar.
Bake for 20 to 22 minutes until risen and golden. Cool 5 minutes before eating.

name: Banana Walnut Bread
description: Moist, deeply flavoured loaf made from overripe bananas and toasted walnuts — ideal for slicing all week.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 175°C and line a 25 cm loaf tin with baking paper.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl and mix in the melted butter, brown sugar, eggs and vanilla extract.
Stir in the flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt until just combined.
Fold in the chopped walnuts and pour into the tin.
Bake for 55 to 60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out and cool fully before slicing.

name: Coconut Chia Pudding
description: Creamy vegan chia pudding set overnight in coconut milk, topped with mango and toasted almonds.
instructions: Whisk the coconut milk, almond milk, maple syrup and vanilla extract in a bowl.
Stir in the chia seeds and whisk again after 5 minutes to break up clumps.
Cover and refrigerate overnight until thick and set.
Spoon into glasses and top with diced mango and toasted flaked almonds.

name: Full English Breakfast
description: The big weekend fry-up: sausages, bacon, fried eggs, baked beans, grilled tomatoes, mushrooms and toast.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 100°C to keep things warm. Fry the sausages in a little oil over medium heat for 12 minutes, turning, until browned.
Add the bacon to the pan and cook until crisp. Transfer both to the oven.
Halve the tomatoes and fry them cut-side down with the whole mushrooms in butter for 5 minutes.
Warm the baked beans in a small pan.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up in the remaining fat.
Toast and butter the bread and plate everything up with salt and pepper.

name: Dutch Baby Pancake
description: One giant puffed oven pancake with crisp golden edges, served with lemon, powdered sugar and berries.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C with a 25 cm ovenproof skillet inside.
Blend the eggs, milk, flour, sugar, vanilla extract and salt until completely smooth.
Carefully add the butter to the hot skillet and swirl until melted and foaming.
Pour in the batter immediately and return to the oven.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes without opening the door until dramatically puffed and golden.
Squeeze over lemon juice, dust with powdered sugar and top with raspberries. Serve at once.

name: Sweet Potato Hash with Eggs
description: Caramelised sweet potato, pepper and onion hash with smoked paprika, finished with eggs baked right in.
instructions: Peel and dice the sweet potatoes into 1 cm cubes.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan and fry the sweet potatoes for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until starting to brown.
Add the diced onion and bell pepper and cook 6 minutes more until tender.
Season with smoked paprika, cumin, salt and pepper.
Make 4 wells, crack in the eggs, cover and cook on low for 5 to 6 minutes until the whites set.
Scatter with green onions and coriander and serve with hot sauce.

name: Cozonac cu Nucă
description: Rich Romanian holiday sweet bread swirled with a walnut, cocoa and rum filling.
instructions: Dissolve the yeast in warm milk with a spoon of sugar and let it foam for 10 minutes.
Beat the egg yolks with the remaining sugar, salt, lemon zest and rum extract, then combine with the flour and yeast mixture.
Knead for 15 minutes, gradually working in the soft butter, until smooth and elastic; cover and let rise until doubled, about 1.5 hours.
Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks and fold in ground walnuts, cocoa, 50 g sugar and raisins for the filling.
Divide the dough in two, roll each into a rectangle, spread with filling and roll up tightly, then twist the two rolls together.
Place in a lined loaf tin, let rise 45 minutes, brush with beaten egg and bake at 170 C for 45 to 50 minutes.

name: Plăcintă cu Brânză Dulce
description: Crisp phyllo layers around a sweet vanilla cottage-cheese filling studded with raisins.
instructions: Mix cottage cheese with eggs, sugar, vanilla sugar, semolina, raisins and lemon zest until creamy.
Line a buttered tray with half the phyllo sheets, brushing each with melted butter.
Spread the cheese filling and cover with the remaining buttered sheets, tucking in the edges.
Whisk sour cream with one egg and pour over the top so it soaks into the layers.
Bake at 180 C for 40 minutes until puffed and golden; cool before slicing.

name: Clătite cu Dulceață
description: Thin Romanian crepes rolled around fruit jam and dusted with powdered sugar.
instructions: Whisk eggs with sugar and salt, then add milk, sparkling water, vanilla and flour to make a thin, lump-free batter; rest 20 minutes.
Heat a lightly oiled non-stick pan and pour in a small ladle of batter, swirling to coat thinly.
Cook 1 minute until the edges lift, flip and cook 30 seconds more; repeat with the rest.
Spread each crepe with jam, roll or fold into quarters.
Dust with powdered sugar and serve warm.

name: Gogoși Pufoase
description: Pillowy fried yeast doughnuts rolled in powdered sugar, best eaten warm.
instructions: Dissolve yeast and a teaspoon of sugar in warm milk and leave 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour, remaining sugar, salt, egg yolks, vanilla and the yeast milk; knead 10 minutes, adding the soft butter at the end.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Roll out to 1.5 cm thick, cut rounds with a glass and let them rest 20 minutes.
Fry in oil at 170 C for 2 minutes per side until golden, drain on paper and roll in powdered sugar.

name: Salam de Biscuiți
description: No-bake chocolate biscuit log with walnuts, raisins and Turkish delight, sliced like a salami.
instructions: Break the biscuits into small irregular pieces and dice the Turkish delight.
Melt butter with milk, sugar and cocoa in a saucepan, stirring until smooth; cool slightly and add rum extract.
Pour over the biscuits, walnuts, raisins and Turkish delight and mix until everything is coated.
Shape into a thick log on cling film, roll tightly and twist the ends.
Chill at least 4 hours, then dust with powdered sugar and cut into slices.

name: Negresă
description: Dense, moist Romanian cocoa cake with walnuts, cut into squares and dusted with sugar.
instructions: Whisk eggs with sugar until pale, then stir in oil, milk and vanilla.
Sift flour, cocoa, baking powder and salt and fold into the wet mixture.
Fold in the chopped walnuts and pour into a lined 25 cm square tin.
Bake at 180 C for 30 to 35 minutes until a skewer comes out with moist crumbs.
Cool in the tin, dust with powdered sugar and cut into squares.

name: Chec Marmorat cu Cacao
description: Classic Romanian marble loaf with swirls of vanilla and cocoa sponge, soft and buttery.
instructions: Separate the eggs and whisk the whites with a pinch of salt to stiff peaks.
Beat yolks with sugar until creamy, add oil, milk and vanilla, then fold in flour and baking powder.
Gently fold in the egg whites, then transfer one third of the batter to a bowl and mix in the cocoa.
Alternate spoonfuls of light and dark batter in a lined loaf tin and swirl once with a knife.
Bake at 170 C for 45 to 50 minutes until a skewer comes out clean; cool before slicing.

name: Cremșnit
description: Two crisp puff pastry sheets sandwiching a thick vanilla custard and whipped cream.
instructions: Bake the puff pastry sheets between two trays at 200 C for 20 minutes until golden; cool.
Whisk egg yolks with sugar, cornstarch and 100 ml of the milk until smooth.
Heat the remaining milk with vanilla, pour over the yolk mixture, return to the pan and cook, stirring, until very thick.
Stir in the butter, cover with cling film and cool completely, then fold in the whipped heavy cream.
Spread the cream over one pastry sheet, top with the second, chill 4 hours and dust with powdered sugar before cutting.

name: Savarină
description: Light yeast cakes soaked in rum syrup, split and filled with whipped cream and jam.
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm milk with a teaspoon of sugar; mix with flour, eggs, 30 g sugar, salt and soft butter into a sticky batter.
Spoon into buttered muffin or savarin moulds, let rise 40 minutes and bake at 180 C for 20 minutes.
Boil water with the remaining sugar for 5 minutes, remove from heat and add rum extract and lemon juice.
Dip the warm cakes in the hot syrup until fully soaked, then drain on a rack.
Whip the cream with powdered sugar, split each cake open, fill with cream and finish with a spoon of jam.

name: Budincă de Tăiței
description: Baked sweet noodle pudding with cottage cheese, raisins and lemon zest, golden on top.
instructions: Cook the noodles in lightly salted water until just tender, drain and toss with half the butter.
Beat eggs with sugar and vanilla sugar, then mix in cottage cheese, sour cream, raisins and lemon zest.
Fold the noodles into the cheese mixture and pour into a buttered baking dish.
Dot the top with the remaining butter and bake at 180 C for 35 to 40 minutes until set and golden.
Cool 10 minutes, dust with powdered sugar and serve warm.

name: Lapte de Pasăre
description: Romanian floating islands: soft meringue clouds poached in milk over a silky vanilla custard.
instructions: Separate the eggs and whisk the whites with 50 g sugar and a pinch of salt to firm, glossy peaks.
Bring the milk to a gentle simmer with the vanilla and drop in spoonfuls of meringue; poach 1 minute per side, then lift onto a plate.
Whisk the yolks with the remaining sugar, slowly pour in the hot milk and return to the pan.
Cook over low heat, stirring, until the custard coats the back of a spoon; do not let it boil.
Pour the custard into a serving dish, float the meringues on top and chill for 2 hours.

name: Cornulețe cu Gem
description: Tender crescent cookies made with sour cream dough, filled with jam and rolled in powdered sugar.
instructions: Rub the cold butter into the flour until crumbly, then mix in sour cream, egg yolks, yeast, vanilla sugar and salt to form a soft dough.
Wrap and chill for at least 1 hour.
Divide into 4 pieces, roll each into a thin circle and cut into 12 triangles.
Put half a teaspoon of thick jam at the wide end of each triangle and roll up towards the tip.
Bake at 180 C for 15 to 18 minutes until lightly golden, then roll in powdered sugar while warm.

name: Prăjitura Albinița
description: Thin honey sheets layered with a smooth semolina and butter cream, softened overnight.
instructions: Melt honey with butter and sugar, cool slightly, then mix in the egg, baking soda and enough flour to form a firm dough.
Divide into 3 pieces and roll each very thinly to fit a lined tray; bake each sheet at 180 C for 7 to 8 minutes.
Cook the semolina in the milk with the remaining sugar and lemon zest until thick, then cool completely.
Beat the soft butter until fluffy and gradually beat in the cooled semolina to make a smooth cream.
Spread half the cream on one sheet, add the second sheet and a thin layer of jam, then the rest of the cream and the top sheet.
Press lightly, refrigerate overnight and dust with powdered sugar before cutting into squares.

name: Baklava cu Nuci
description: Layers of buttery phyllo and spiced walnuts soaked in a lemon-honey syrup.
instructions: Pulse the walnuts with cinnamon and 50 g sugar until coarsely ground.
Butter a tray and layer 8 phyllo sheets, brushing each with melted butter; sprinkle with a third of the nuts.
Repeat twice more and finish with the remaining sheets, buttering each; cut into diamonds with a sharp knife.
Bake at 170 C for 45 to 50 minutes until crisp and golden.
Meanwhile boil water, remaining sugar, honey and lemon juice for 10 minutes; pour the hot syrup over the hot baklava.
Let it soak at room temperature for at least 6 hours before serving.

name: Tiramisu
description: Coffee-soaked ladyfingers layered with airy mascarpone cream and finished with cocoa.
instructions: Brew strong coffee, stir in the rum and let it cool.
Whisk egg yolks with sugar over a pan of simmering water for 5 minutes until pale and thick, then cool.
Beat the mascarpone into the yolks, whip the cream to soft peaks and fold it in.
Dip ladyfingers briefly in the coffee and line a dish; spread half the cream on top and repeat.
Chill at least 6 hours and dust thickly with cocoa before serving.

name: Panna Cotta with Raspberry Sauce
description: Wobbly vanilla cream set with gelatin and topped with a bright raspberry sauce.
instructions: Soak the gelatin in cold water for 5 minutes.
Heat cream, milk, 80 g sugar and vanilla until steaming, remove from heat and dissolve the squeezed gelatin in it.
Pour into 6 glasses or moulds and refrigerate at least 4 hours until set.
Simmer raspberries with the remaining sugar and lemon juice for 5 minutes, then press through a sieve and cool.
Unmould or serve in the glasses with the raspberry sauce spooned over.

name: Crème Brûlée
description: Rich vanilla custard with a crackling caramelised sugar crust you tap through with a spoon.
instructions: Heat the cream with vanilla until just steaming.
Whisk egg yolks with 80 g sugar and a pinch of salt, then slowly whisk in the hot cream.
Strain into 6 ramekins set in a deep tray; pour hot water around them halfway up.
Bake at 150 C for 35 to 40 minutes until just set with a slight wobble; chill 4 hours.
Sprinkle each with a thin layer of the remaining sugar and caramelise with a torch or under a very hot grill.

name: Dark Chocolate Mousse
description: Airy yet intense dark chocolate mousse made with whipped cream and whisked egg whites.
instructions: Melt the chocolate with the butter over a pan of barely simmering water; cool slightly.
Stir the egg yolks and vanilla into the warm chocolate one at a time.
Whisk the egg whites with salt to soft peaks, add the sugar and whisk until glossy.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold into the chocolate, then fold in the egg whites in two additions.
Spoon into glasses and chill for at least 3 hours.

name: Baked Vanilla Cheesecake
description: Creamy New York-style cheesecake on a buttery biscuit base, baked low and slow.
instructions: Crush the biscuits, mix with melted butter and press into a lined 23 cm springform tin; bake 10 minutes at 170 C.
Beat cream cheese with sugar and cornstarch until smooth, then beat in sour cream, vanilla and lemon zest.
Add the eggs one at a time on low speed, mixing just until combined.
Pour over the base and bake at 160 C for 60 to 70 minutes until the edges are set and the centre wobbles slightly.
Turn off the oven, leave the door ajar for 1 hour, then chill overnight before slicing.

name: No-Bake Strawberry Cheesecake
description: Chilled cream cheese and whipped cream filling on a biscuit base, crowned with fresh strawberries.
instructions: Crush biscuits, mix with melted butter and press firmly into a lined 23 cm springform tin; chill 20 minutes.
Soak gelatin in cold water, then dissolve it in 3 tablespoons of hot water.
Beat cream cheese with powdered sugar, vanilla and lemon juice until smooth, then whisk in the dissolved gelatin.
Whip the cream to soft peaks and fold into the cheese mixture; spread over the base.
Refrigerate at least 6 hours, then top with halved strawberries and a drizzle of warmed jam.

name: Fudgy Chocolate Brownies
description: Dense, glossy-topped brownies made with real dark chocolate and toasted walnuts.
instructions: Melt the chocolate and butter together, then cool for 5 minutes.
Whisk eggs with sugar and vanilla for 3 minutes until pale and thick.
Stir in the melted chocolate, then fold in flour, cocoa and salt until just combined; add the walnuts.
Pour into a lined 20 cm square tin and bake at 175 C for 25 to 28 minutes until the top is set but the centre is still soft.
Cool completely in the tin before cutting into squares.

name: Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Chewy brown-sugar cookies with crisp edges and pockets of melted chocolate chips.
instructions: Cream the soft butter with brown sugar and white sugar until fluffy.
Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Mix flour, baking soda and salt, stir into the butter mixture, then fold in the chocolate chips.
Scoop heaped tablespoons onto lined trays, spacing well apart, and chill 15 minutes.
Bake at 180 C for 10 to 12 minutes until golden at the edges; cool on the tray 5 minutes.

name: Lemon Bars
description: Buttery shortbread base topped with a tangy baked lemon curd and a snowy dusting of sugar.
instructions: Mix flour, 60 g powdered sugar and a pinch of salt, rub in the cold butter and press into a lined 20 cm square tin.
Bake the base at 180 C for 18 minutes until pale golden.
Whisk eggs with sugar, lemon zest, lemon juice and cornstarch until smooth.
Pour the filling over the hot base and bake 20 to 22 minutes more until just set.
Cool completely, chill 2 hours, dust with powdered sugar and cut into bars.

name: Apple Crumble
description: Soft cinnamon apples under a crunchy oat and brown sugar crumble, perfect with custard or ice cream.
instructions: Peel and chop the apples and toss with sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice in a baking dish.
Rub the cold butter into the flour until it looks like coarse crumbs, then stir in oats, brown sugar and salt.
Scatter the crumble evenly over the apples without pressing down.
Bake at 190 C for 35 to 40 minutes until the top is golden and the fruit bubbles.
Rest 10 minutes and serve warm with ice cream.

name: Banana Bread
description: Moist, tender loaf made with very ripe bananas, brown sugar and a handful of walnuts.
instructions: Mash the bananas thoroughly with a fork.
Whisk melted butter with brown sugar, eggs and vanilla, then stir in the bananas.
Fold in flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt until just combined; add the walnuts.
Pour into a lined loaf tin and bake at 175 C for 55 to 60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool in the tin 15 minutes before turning out.

name: Carrot Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting
description: Spiced carrot and walnut cake with a thick, tangy cream cheese frosting.
instructions: Whisk eggs with sugar and oil until smooth, then stir in the grated carrots and vanilla.
Mix flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg and salt and fold into the batter with the walnuts.
Divide between two lined 20 cm tins and bake at 175 C for 30 to 35 minutes; cool completely.
Beat cream cheese with soft butter and powdered sugar until smooth and fluffy.
Sandwich the layers with frosting, cover the top and sides and chill 1 hour before slicing.

name: Lemon Drizzle Cake
description: Light lemon sponge soaked while warm with a crunchy sugar and lemon juice drizzle.
instructions: Cream butter and sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time with the zest of both lemons.
Fold in flour, baking powder, salt and milk to make a soft batter.
Pour into a lined loaf tin and bake at 170 C for 45 to 50 minutes until golden and springy.
Mix the lemon juice with the powdered sugar and pour over the hot cake, pricking the top with a skewer first.
Cool completely in the tin so the drizzle sets into a crust.

name: Victoria Sponge
description: Two feather-light vanilla sponges filled with raspberry jam and softly whipped cream.
instructions: Cream butter and sugar until very pale and fluffy.
Add the eggs one at a time with a spoon of flour each, then fold in the remaining flour, baking powder, vanilla and milk.
Divide between two lined 20 cm tins and bake at 180 C for 22 to 25 minutes until golden and springy.
Cool on a rack, then whip the cream with 1 tablespoon powdered sugar.
Spread jam on one sponge, top with cream and the second sponge, and dust with powdered sugar.

name: Pavlova with Berries
description: Crisp-shelled meringue with a marshmallowy centre, piled with whipped cream and fresh berries.
instructions: Whisk the egg whites with salt to soft peaks, then add the sugar a spoon at a time until stiff and glossy.
Fold in cornstarch, vinegar and vanilla.
Spoon onto a lined tray in a 22 cm circle with a slight dip in the middle.
Bake at 120 C for 90 minutes, then turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside to cool completely.
Whip the cream with powdered sugar, spread over the meringue and top with strawberries, raspberries and blueberries.

name: Chocolate Lava Cakes
description: Individual dark chocolate cakes with a molten centre that flows out when cut.
instructions: Butter 4 ramekins and dust with cocoa powder.
Melt the chocolate and butter together and cool slightly.
Whisk eggs, egg yolks, sugar and vanilla until pale, then fold in the chocolate, followed by the flour and salt.
Divide between the ramekins and bake at 200 C for 11 to 12 minutes until the edges are set but the centres jiggle.
Rest 1 minute, run a knife around the edge, invert onto plates and serve immediately with ice cream.

name: Chocolate Layer Cake
description: Tall, moist cocoa sponge layered with a glossy dark chocolate ganache frosting.
instructions: Whisk flour, sugar, cocoa, baking powder, baking soda and salt in a large bowl.
Add eggs, milk, oil and vanilla and beat until smooth, then stir in the hot coffee; the batter will be thin.
Divide between two lined 20 cm tins and bake at 175 C for 30 to 35 minutes; cool completely.
Heat the cream until steaming, pour over the chopped chocolate, rest 2 minutes and stir smooth; chill until spreadable.
Fill and frost the cake with the ganache and let it set 30 minutes before slicing.

name: Sticky Toffee Pudding
description: Warm date sponge drenched in a buttery brown sugar toffee sauce.
instructions: Simmer the chopped dates in the water with baking soda for 3 minutes and set aside.
Cream 80 g butter with 150 g brown sugar, beat in the eggs and vanilla, then fold in the flour, baking powder and the date mixture.
Pour into a buttered baking dish and bake at 180 C for 30 to 35 minutes until springy.
Melt the remaining butter with the remaining brown sugar and the cream, simmer 3 minutes to a glossy sauce.
Prick the hot pudding, pour over half the sauce and serve with the rest and a scoop of ice cream.

name: Cinnamon Raisin Bread Pudding
description: Thrifty baked pudding of custard-soaked bread cubes with raisins and a crisp cinnamon-sugar top.
instructions: Cut the bread into cubes and spread in a buttered baking dish with the raisins.
Whisk eggs with milk, cream, 100 g sugar, vanilla and half the cinnamon.
Pour the custard over the bread, press down gently and soak for 20 minutes.
Dot with butter and sprinkle with the remaining sugar mixed with cinnamon.
Bake at 175 C for 40 to 45 minutes until puffed and golden; serve warm.

name: Fresh Fruit Tart
description: Crisp shortcrust shell filled with vanilla pastry cream and topped with glossy fresh fruit.
instructions: Line a 24 cm tart tin with the shortcrust pastry, prick the base, chill 15 minutes and blind bake at 180 C for 25 minutes until golden; cool.
Whisk egg yolks with sugar and cornstarch; heat the milk with vanilla and pour it over, whisking.
Return to the pan and cook, stirring, until thick; beat in the butter, cover and chill.
Spread the cold pastry cream in the tart shell and arrange sliced strawberries, kiwi and blueberries on top.
Warm the jam with a teaspoon of water and brush over the fruit to glaze; chill until serving.

name: Churros with Chocolate Sauce
description: Crisp ridged fried dough sticks rolled in cinnamon sugar, served with thick hot chocolate dip.
instructions: Bring water, butter, 1 tablespoon sugar and salt to a boil, add the flour all at once and stir into a smooth ball; cool 5 minutes.
Beat in the eggs one at a time until glossy, then transfer to a piping bag with a large star nozzle.
Pipe 10 cm lengths into oil heated to 180 C and fry 3 to 4 minutes until golden, turning once.
Drain and roll immediately in the remaining sugar mixed with cinnamon.
Heat the cream until steaming, pour over the chopped chocolate, stir smooth and serve alongside.

name: Caramel Flan
description: Silky baked custard that unmoulds under a pool of amber caramel sauce.
instructions: Melt 150 g sugar in a pan over medium heat without stirring until deep amber, then pour into a 20 cm round tin and swirl to coat the base.
Whisk eggs with the remaining sugar, then whisk in milk, condensed milk, vanilla and a pinch of salt.
Strain the custard over the caramel and set the tin in a deep tray of hot water.
Bake at 160 C for 50 to 60 minutes until set with a gentle wobble; cool and chill overnight.
Run a knife around the edge and invert onto a rimmed plate so the caramel flows over.

name: Baked Apples with Walnuts and Honey
description: Whole apples stuffed with walnuts, raisins and cinnamon, baked until tender and glazed with honey.
instructions: Core the apples from the top without cutting through the base and set them in a baking dish.
Mix chopped walnuts, raisins, brown sugar, cinnamon and soft butter and pack into the cavities.
Drizzle with honey and pour the water into the dish.
Bake at 180 C for 35 to 40 minutes, basting once, until the apples are soft but hold their shape.
Serve warm with the pan juices and a spoon of yogurt or ice cream.

name: Red Wine Poached Pears
description: Whole pears poached in spiced red wine until ruby red, served with the syrupy reduction.
instructions: Peel the pears, leaving the stalks on, and trim the bases so they stand upright.
Bring wine, sugar, orange zest and juice, cinnamon, star anise and cloves to a simmer in a pan that fits the pears snugly.
Add the pears and poach gently for 25 to 30 minutes, turning occasionally, until tender.
Lift out the pears and boil the liquid for 10 minutes until reduced to a syrup.
Serve the pears warm or chilled with the syrup and a spoon of mascarpone.

name: No-Churn Mango Lime Sorbet
description: Three-ingredient frozen mango sorbet blended smooth with lime and honey, no ice cream maker needed.
instructions: Peel and dice the mangoes, spread on a tray and freeze for at least 4 hours.
Blend the frozen mango with lime zest, lime juice, honey and a splash of water until completely smooth.
Serve immediately for a soft-serve texture, or freeze 1 hour more for firmer scoops.
Garnish with fresh mint leaves.

name: No-Churn Vanilla Ice Cream
description: Creamy vanilla ice cream from whipped cream and condensed milk, frozen without a machine.
instructions: Whip the heavy cream with vanilla and a pinch of salt to firm peaks.
Gently fold in the condensed milk until no streaks remain.
Scrape into a loaf tin, cover with cling film and freeze at least 6 hours.
Soften 5 minutes at room temperature before scooping; serve with chocolate chips or fresh berries.

name: Date and Oat Energy Balls
description: No-bake bites of dates, oats, peanut butter and cocoa rolled in coconut, ready in 15 minutes.
instructions: Soak the dates in hot water for 5 minutes if they are dry, then drain.
Blend dates, oats, peanut butter, cocoa, honey and a pinch of salt into a sticky paste.
Roll into walnut-sized balls with damp hands.
Roll in desiccated coconut and chill 30 minutes before eating; keep in the fridge for up to a week.

name: Dark Chocolate Truffles
description: Melt-in-the-mouth ganache truffles with a hint of rum, rolled in cocoa or chopped nuts.
instructions: Finely chop the chocolate and place in a bowl.
Heat the cream until steaming, pour over the chocolate, wait 2 minutes and stir until smooth; add butter and rum.
Chill the ganache for 2 hours until firm enough to scoop.
Scoop teaspoons and quickly roll into balls with cold hands.
Roll half in cocoa powder and half in finely chopped hazelnuts; keep refrigerated.

name: Affogato
description: A scoop of vanilla ice cream drowned in a shot of hot espresso, finished with shaved chocolate.
instructions: Chill 4 small glasses or cups in the freezer for 10 minutes.
Place a generous scoop of vanilla ice cream in each glass.
Brew 4 shots of strong espresso.
Pour the hot coffee over the ice cream at the table and top with grated dark chocolate and a crushed biscuit.

name: Classic Scones with Jam and Cream
description: Tall, fluffy buttermilk scones served warm with strawberry jam and thick whipped cream.
instructions: Mix flour, baking powder, sugar and salt, then rub in the cold butter until crumbly.
Stir in the buttermilk with a knife until a shaggy dough forms; do not overwork.
Pat out to 3 cm thick on a floured surface and cut 8 rounds with a 6 cm cutter.
Brush the tops with beaten egg and bake at 220 C for 12 to 14 minutes until risen and golden.
Whip the cream to firm peaks and serve the warm scones split with jam and cream.

name: Cinnamon Rolls with Cream Cheese Glaze
