description: Soft spiral buns swirled with brown sugar and cinnamon, topped with a tangy cream cheese glaze.
instructions: Warm the milk, dissolve the yeast with a spoon of sugar and leave 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour, remaining sugar, salt, egg, 60 g melted butter and the yeast milk; knead 10 minutes until smooth, then let rise 1 hour.
Roll into a 30 by 40 cm rectangle, spread with 60 g soft butter and sprinkle with brown sugar and cinnamon.
Roll up tightly from the long side, cut into 12 slices and arrange in a buttered dish; rise 30 minutes.
Bake at 180 C for 22 to 25 minutes until golden.
Beat cream cheese with powdered sugar, vanilla and a splash of milk and spread over the warm rolls.

name: Peach Cobbler
description: Juicy cinnamon peaches baked under a soft, golden biscuit-style topping.
instructions: Slice the peaches and toss with 60 g sugar, cornstarch, lemon juice and cinnamon; spread in a buttered baking dish.
Mix flour, remaining sugar, baking powder and salt, rub in the cold butter, then stir in the milk to a thick batter.
Drop spoonfuls of batter over the peaches, leaving gaps for steam.
Sprinkle with brown sugar and bake at 190 C for 35 to 40 minutes until bubbling and golden.
Serve warm with vanilla ice cream.

name: Oatmeal Raisin Cookies
description: Soft, chewy oat cookies spiced with cinnamon and packed with plump raisins.
instructions: Cream the soft butter with brown sugar and white sugar until light.
Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Stir in flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt, then fold in the oats and raisins.
Drop heaped tablespoons onto lined trays and flatten slightly.
Bake at 180 C for 11 to 13 minutes until golden at the edges but still soft; cool on the tray.

name: Pan-Fried Trout with Garlic
description: Whole trout dusted in flour, fried until crisp and finished with sizzling garlic butter and lemon.
instructions: Rinse the trout, pat dry and season inside and out with salt and pepper.
Dredge each fish lightly in flour, shaking off the excess.
Heat the oil in a large pan and fry the trout for 5 to 6 minutes per side until golden and the flesh flakes easily.
Remove the fish and add the butter and sliced garlic to the pan, swirling until fragrant.
Pour the garlic butter over the trout, squeeze over lemon juice and scatter with parsley before serving.

name: Romanian Fish Plachie
description: Carp pieces baked on a bed of slow-cooked onions, tomatoes and garlic with a splash of white wine.
instructions: Cut the carp into thick portions, season with salt and pepper and set aside.
Slice the onions thinly and cook them gently in oil for 15 minutes until soft and sweet.
Add the sliced garlic, chopped tomatoes, bay leaves and wine and simmer for 5 minutes.
Spread half the onion mixture in a baking dish, lay the fish on top and cover with the rest.
Top with lemon slices and bake at 180 C for 35 minutes until the fish is cooked through.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Carp Saramură
description: Danube Delta classic: grilled carp doused in a hot garlic, chili and tomato brine, served with polenta.
instructions: Cut the carp into thick slices, salt them and grill or pan-sear on high heat for 5 minutes per side.
Char the tomatoes and chili pepper in a dry pan or under the grill until the skins blister.
Crush the garlic with a pinch of salt and chop the charred tomatoes and chili.
Bring the water to a boil with the thyme, garlic, tomatoes, chili and a good amount of salt.
Arrange the grilled fish in a deep dish and pour the boiling brine over it.
Let it rest 5 minutes, scatter with parsley and serve with hot polenta.

name: Baked Carp with Vegetables
description: A whole carp roasted over potatoes, carrots, peppers and tomatoes with white wine and dill.
instructions: Clean the carp, score the skin diagonally and rub with salt, pepper and crushed garlic.
Cut the potatoes, carrots and peppers into chunks and toss with oil in a large roasting tin.
Roast the vegetables at 200 C for 20 minutes to give them a head start.
Lay the fish on the vegetables, tuck in the tomato wedges and onion and pour over the wine.
Bake for another 35 to 40 minutes, basting once, until the fish flakes at the thickest part.
Finish with chopped dill and serve from the tin.

name: Fish Cakes
description: Golden patties of flaked white fish and mashed potato with spring onion, parsley and lemon.
instructions: Boil the potatoes until tender, drain well and mash roughly.
Poach the fish fillets in simmering water for 6 minutes, drain and flake.
Mix the potato, fish, chopped spring onions, parsley, lemon zest, one egg, salt and pepper.
Shape into 8 patties, coat in breadcrumbs and chill for 15 minutes to firm up.
Fry in hot oil for 3 to 4 minutes per side until crisp and golden.
Serve with lemon wedges and a spoon of mayonnaise.

name: Oven-Baked Fish and Chips
description: Crunchy paprika-breadcrumb cod and crisp oven chips, no deep fryer needed.
instructions: Cut the potatoes into thick chips, toss with half the oil and salt and spread on a tray.
Bake at 220 C for 20 minutes, then turn the chips over.
Set up three bowls: flour seasoned with salt and pepper, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs mixed with paprika.
Coat each cod portion in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs and place on a second oiled tray.
Bake the fish with the chips for 15 minutes until the coating is golden and the fish flakes.
Serve with lemon wedges and a dollop of mayonnaise.

name: Lemon Butter Cod
description: Flaky cod fillets pan-seared and bathed in a bright garlic, lemon and parsley butter sauce.
instructions: Pat the cod dry and season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a non-stick pan and sear the cod for 3 to 4 minutes per side until opaque.
Transfer the fish to a warm plate.
Lower the heat, add the butter and minced garlic and cook for 1 minute without browning.
Stir in the lemon juice and zest and the chopped parsley.
Spoon the sauce over the cod and serve with steamed green beans.

name: Mackerel with Mustard
description: Oily, rich mackerel fillets grilled under a tangy mustard-dill crust with boiled potatoes.
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, about 20 minutes.
Mix the mustard with olive oil, crushed garlic, lemon juice, chopped dill and pepper.
Score the mackerel skin and lay the fish skin side down on a lined tray.
Spread the mustard mixture thickly over the flesh.
Grill or bake at 220 C for 10 to 12 minutes until the crust is bubbling and the fish is cooked.
Serve with the potatoes and extra lemon.

name: Sea Bass Baked in Salt Crust
description: Whole sea bass sealed in a herbed salt crust so it steams in its own juices, moist and delicate.
instructions: Heat the oven to 200 C and stuff the cleaned sea bass cavity with lemon slices, thyme and rosemary.
Mix the coarse salt with the lightly beaten egg whites until it feels like wet sand.
Spread a layer of the salt mixture on a baking tray and lay the fish on top.
Cover the fish completely with the remaining salt, pressing it firmly into a sealed crust.
Bake for 30 minutes, then rest 5 minutes and crack the crust open with the back of a spoon.
Lift off the skin, drizzle the fillets with olive oil and serve with lemon.

name: Mediterranean Sea Bream
description: Whole sea bream roasted with cherry tomatoes, olives, garlic, oregano and a splash of white wine.
instructions: Score the sea bream on both sides and season generously with salt and pepper.
Place the fish in a baking dish and scatter around the halved cherry tomatoes, olives and sliced garlic.
Tuck lemon slices into the cavities and sprinkle everything with oregano.
Drizzle with olive oil, pour in the wine and roast at 200 C for 25 minutes.
Spoon the pan juices over the fish and finish with chopped parsley.

name: Garlic Shrimp (Gambas al Ajillo)
description: Spanish tapas-style shrimp sizzled in olive oil with lots of garlic and chili, mopped up with bread.
instructions: Peel and devein the shrimp and pat them dry.
Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat with the sliced garlic and chili flakes.
When the garlic turns pale gold, raise the heat and add the shrimp in a single layer.
Cook for 2 minutes per side until pink and just curled, then season with salt.
Squeeze over lemon juice, scatter with parsley and serve straight from the pan with sliced baguette.

name: Mussels in White Wine
description: A big pot of mussels steamed open in white wine, shallots and garlic with a touch of cream.
instructions: Scrub the mussels, pull off the beards and discard any that stay open when tapped.
Melt the butter in a large lidded pot and soften the chopped shallots and garlic for 3 minutes.
Pour in the wine, bring to a boil and tip in the mussels.
Cover and steam for 4 to 5 minutes, shaking the pot, until the shells open.
Stir in the cream, parsley and black pepper and discard any mussels still closed.
Serve in deep bowls with baguette for the broth.

name: Crispy Calamari Rings
description: Light, crunchy squid rings in a paprika flour coating with a quick garlic mayo and lemon.
instructions: Slice the squid tubes into 1 cm rings and pat them very dry.
Mix the flour, cornstarch, paprika, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Stir the crushed garlic into the mayonnaise with a squeeze of lemon for the dip.
Heat 3 cm of oil in a deep pan to 180 C.
Toss the rings in the flour mixture and fry in batches for 2 minutes until golden; do not overcrowd.
Drain on paper, salt lightly and serve hot with lemon wedges and the garlic mayo.

name: Sesame-Crusted Tuna Steak
description: Seared tuna with a crunchy sesame crust, pink in the middle, over dressed salad greens.
instructions: Brush the tuna steaks with soy sauce and let them sit for 10 minutes.
Press both sides of each steak firmly into the sesame seeds.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy pan until very hot.
Sear the tuna for 1 to 2 minutes per side so the crust browns and the centre stays pink.
Whisk the lime juice, sesame oil, grated ginger and pepper into a dressing and toss with the greens.
Slice the tuna thickly and serve on the salad.

name: Salmon with Dill Sauce
description: Roasted salmon fillets with a cool, creamy sour cream and dill sauce and buttery new potatoes.
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain.
Rub the salmon with olive oil, salt and pepper and place skin side down on a lined tray.
Roast at 200 C for 12 to 14 minutes until just opaque in the centre.
Stir together the sour cream, yogurt, chopped dill, mustard, lemon zest and juice; season.
Serve the salmon with the potatoes and a generous spoonful of dill sauce.

name: Salmon Patties
description: Tender pan-fried salmon burgers bound with egg and breadcrumbs, brightened with red onion and dill.
instructions: Remove the skin from the salmon and chop the flesh finely with a sharp knife.
Mix the salmon with the finely diced red onion, dill, egg, breadcrumbs, lemon zest, salt and pepper.
Form into 8 patties and chill for 20 minutes so they hold together.
Fry in hot oil for 3 to 4 minutes per side until golden and cooked through.
Stir lemon juice into the mayonnaise and serve alongside the patties.

name: Baked Trout with Potatoes
description: Whole trout stuffed with lemon and rosemary, baked over crisp garlic potatoes in one tray.
instructions: Slice the potatoes 1 cm thick, toss with olive oil, half the garlic, salt and pepper and spread on a tray.
Roast at 200 C for 25 minutes until the edges start to brown.
Fill each trout cavity with lemon slices, a rosemary sprig and the remaining sliced garlic.
Lay the trout on the potatoes, dot with butter and bake for 20 more minutes.
Rest for 3 minutes and serve with the pan juices spooned over.

name: Romanian Fish Stew (Ghiveci de Pește)
description: Chunks of white fish simmered with potatoes, peppers, zucchini and carrots in a tomato sauce.
instructions: Soften the chopped onion and diced carrots in oil for 5 minutes.
Add the diced peppers, potatoes and garlic and cook for 3 minutes more.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and 300 ml water, add the bay leaves and season; simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the zucchini chunks and cook 5 minutes until the potatoes are nearly tender.
Lay the fish pieces on top, cover and simmer gently for 10 minutes without stirring.
Scatter with parsley and serve with bread.

name: Smoked Mackerel Potato Bake
description: Layers of sliced potato, leek and flaked smoked mackerel baked in mustardy cream under melted cheese.
instructions: Slice the potatoes thinly and parboil for 5 minutes, then drain.
Soften the sliced leek in butter for 5 minutes.
Flake the smoked mackerel, discarding skin and bones.
Whisk the cream, milk, mustard and pepper together.
Layer potatoes, leek and mackerel in a buttered dish, pouring cream between layers and finishing with potato.
Top with grated cheese and bake at 190 C for 35 minutes until golden; scatter with chives.

name: Crispy Breaded Fish Fillets
description: Classic pane: white fish fillets in a seasoned breadcrumb crust, shallow-fried until golden.
instructions: Pat the fillets dry and season with salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Dredge in flour, dip in beaten egg, then press into breadcrumbs to coat evenly.
Heat 1 cm of oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the fillets for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

name: Romanian Potato Stew (Mâncare de Cartofi)
description: Humble, deeply savoury potatoes stewed with onion, pepper, paprika and tomato paste.
instructions: Soften the chopped onion, diced carrot and pepper in oil over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Stir in the paprika and tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.
Add the potato chunks, bay leaf, thyme and enough water to just cover.
Simmer gently for 25 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the sauce has thickened.
Stir in the crushed garlic, season with salt and finish with chopped parsley.

name: Romanian Bean Stew (Iahnie de Fasole)
description: Creamy white beans slow-cooked with root vegetables, paprika and tomato, finished with dill.
instructions: Soak the beans overnight, then drain and boil in fresh water for 10 minutes; drain again.
Return the beans to the pot with the diced carrot and celery root, cover with water and simmer 60 minutes.
Meanwhile soften the finely chopped onions in oil until golden, then stir in the paprika and tomato paste.
Add the onion mixture, bay leaf and thyme to the beans and cook 15 minutes more until thick and creamy.
Stir in the crushed garlic, season with salt and pepper and scatter with dill before serving.

name: Romanian Pea Stew (Mâncare de Mazăre)
description: Sweet green peas in a light tomato and dill sauce, the everyday Romanian weeknight favourite.
instructions: Soften the finely chopped onion and grated carrot in oil for 6 minutes.
Sprinkle over the flour and stir for 1 minute, then add the tomato paste.
Add the peas, a pinch of sugar and 400 ml water; season with salt and pepper.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until the sauce coats the peas.
Stir in the crushed garlic and chopped dill and rest 5 minutes before serving.

name: Romanian Vegetable Ghiveci
description: A summer harvest baked together: eggplant, zucchini, peppers, beans, potatoes and tomatoes.
instructions: Cut all the vegetables into bite-sized chunks and trim the green beans.
Soften the onion in oil in a large oven-proof pot, then add the carrots and potatoes for 5 minutes.
Add the eggplant, zucchini, peppers, green beans, garlic and chopped tomatoes and season well.
Stir, cover and bake at 180 C for 45 minutes, stirring once halfway.
Uncover for the last 10 minutes to thicken, then finish with parsley.

name: Mushroom Tocăniță with Polenta
description: Juicy mushrooms stewed with onion, paprika, white wine and dill, served over soft polenta.
instructions: Sauté the chopped onion in oil until golden, about 8 minutes.
Add the quartered mushrooms and cook on high heat until their liquid evaporates.
Stir in the paprika, tomato paste and garlic, then pour in the wine and let it bubble.
Add 150 ml water, season and simmer for 15 minutes until saucy.
Meanwhile whisk the cornmeal into 1.2 litres of salted boiling water and cook, stirring, for 20 minutes.
Serve the mushrooms over the polenta with plenty of dill.

name: Rice and Vegetable Stuffed Peppers
description: Romanian fasting-style peppers filled with rice, mushrooms and carrots, simmered in tomato sauce.
instructions: Cut the tops off the peppers and scoop out the seeds.
Soften the chopped onion and grated carrot in oil, then add the chopped mushrooms and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the rinsed rice, thyme, half the dill and parsley, salt and pepper and cook 2 minutes.
Fill the peppers three-quarters full and stand them upright in a deep pot.
Pour the tomato sauce and 300 ml water around them, cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
Rest 10 minutes and scatter with the remaining herbs.

name: Stuffed Zucchini (Dovlecei Umpluți)
description: Hollowed zucchini halves filled with herbed rice and vegetables, baked and served with sour cream.
instructions: Halve the zucchini lengthwise and scoop out the centres, leaving a 1 cm shell; chop the flesh.
Soften the onion and grated carrot in oil, add the zucchini flesh and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the rinsed rice, chopped tomatoes, dill, salt and pepper and cook 3 minutes, then cool slightly.
Mix in the beaten egg and fill the zucchini shells.
Arrange in a baking dish, add 150 ml water to the dish, cover with foil and bake at 180 C for 40 minutes.
Uncover for 10 minutes to colour and serve with sour cream.

name: Baked Eggplant with Tomatoes
description: Roasted eggplant slices layered with tomatoes, garlic and thyme and crumbled with salty telemea.
instructions: Slice the eggplants 1 cm thick, salt them and leave for 20 minutes, then pat dry.
Brush the slices with olive oil and roast at 220 C for 20 minutes until golden.
Soften the sliced onion and garlic in the remaining oil, add the chopped tomatoes and thyme and simmer 10 minutes.
Layer the eggplant and tomato sauce in a baking dish, finishing with sauce.
Crumble the telemea on top and bake at 190 C for 20 minutes.
Scatter with parsley and serve warm with bread.

name: Mămăligă with Cheese and Sour Cream
description: Golden Romanian polenta topped with crumbled telemea, cold sour cream, butter and a fried egg.
instructions: Bring the water to a boil in a heavy pot with the salt.
Rain in the cornmeal while whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Lower the heat and cook, stirring often with a wooden spoon, for 25 to 30 minutes until thick and pulling from the sides.
Fry the eggs in a little butter until the whites are set.
Turn the polenta out onto a board, slice with a string or knife and top each portion with telemea, sour cream, a knob of butter and a fried egg.

name: Vegetable Patties (Chiftele de Legume)
description: Crisp fasting-day patties of grated potato, carrot and mushroom with garlic and fresh herbs.
instructions: Grate the potatoes and carrots coarsely and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Finely chop the mushrooms and onion and sauté in 1 tbsp oil until dry, then cool.
Combine all vegetables with the crushed garlic, breadcrumbs, flour, chopped parsley and dill, salt and pepper.
Shape into small flat patties with wet hands.
Fry in hot oil for 4 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper and serve with a tomato sauce or garlic sauce.

name: Vegan Sarmale (Sarmale de Post)
description: Pickled cabbage rolls filled with rice, mushrooms, carrot and onion, slow-baked in tomato sauce.
instructions: Rinse the pickled cabbage leaves, trim the thick ribs and set a few torn leaves aside.
Soften the finely chopped onions and grated carrots in oil, add the chopped mushrooms and cook until dry.
Stir in the rinsed rice, thyme, dill, pepper and a little salt and cook for 2 minutes.
Place a spoonful of filling on each leaf, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Line a pot with torn leaves, pack the rolls in tightly, add the bay leaves and pour over tomato sauce and water to cover.
Cover and bake at 170 C for 2 hours; serve with polenta.

name: Ratatouille
description: Provencal stew of eggplant, zucchini, peppers and tomatoes, each cooked separately then married with basil.
instructions: Dice the eggplant, zucchini and peppers into 2 cm pieces and chop the tomatoes.
In a wide pan, fry the eggplant in 2 tbsp olive oil until golden, then remove.
Repeat with the zucchini, then the peppers, adding oil as needed, and set aside.
Soften the onion and garlic in the pan, add the tomatoes and thyme and simmer 10 minutes.
Return all vegetables, season and simmer gently for 20 minutes until tender but holding shape.
Tear in the basil and serve warm with crusty bread.

name: Eggplant Parmigiana
description: Fried eggplant layered with tomato sauce, mozzarella, parmesan and basil, baked until bubbling.
instructions: Slice the eggplants lengthwise 1 cm thick, salt and drain for 30 minutes, then pat dry.
Dust the slices in flour, dip in beaten egg and fry in olive oil until golden on both sides.
Warm the tomato sauce with the sliced garlic and half the basil for 5 minutes.
In a baking dish, layer sauce, eggplant, torn mozzarella and grated parmesan; repeat, ending with cheese.
Bake at 190 C for 35 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Rest 10 minutes and top with the remaining basil.

name: Vegetable Moussaka
description: Greek-style layers of eggplant, potato and cinnamon-spiced lentils under a golden bechamel.
instructions: Simmer the lentils in water for 20 minutes until tender, then drain.
Slice the eggplant and potatoes 1 cm thick, brush with olive oil and roast at 220 C for 20 minutes.
Soften the onion in oil, add the lentils, crushed tomatoes, cinnamon, salt and pepper and simmer 15 minutes.
Make the bechamel: melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the milk and cook until thick; add half the cheese.
Layer potatoes, lentil sauce and eggplant in a dish, pour over the bechamel and top with the remaining cheese.
Bake at 180 C for 40 minutes until golden; rest 15 minutes before cutting.

name: Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms
description: Meaty portobello caps filled with garlicky spinach and goat cheese under a crisp parmesan crumb.
instructions: Remove the mushroom stems, brush the caps with olive oil and season; roast gill side up at 200 C for 10 minutes.
Chop the stems and cook them with the garlic in olive oil for 3 minutes.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted, then squeeze out excess liquid and mix with the goat cheese and thyme.
Pour off any liquid from the caps and fill them with the spinach mixture.
Mix the breadcrumbs with parmesan and a drizzle of oil and sprinkle on top.
Bake for 15 minutes until the topping is golden.

name: Chickpea and Spinach Stew
description: Smoky Spanish-style chickpeas simmered with tomatoes, cumin and paprika, finished with wilted spinach.
instructions: Soften the chopped onion in olive oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and drained chickpeas with 200 ml water and simmer for 15 minutes.
Crush a few chickpeas against the side of the pot to thicken the sauce.
Stir in the spinach in handfuls until wilted.
Season with salt, pepper and lemon juice and serve with crusty bread.

name: Lentil Shepherd's Pie
description: Rich lentil and vegetable gravy baked under a blanket of creamy mashed potato.
instructions: Boil the potatoes until tender, drain and mash with the butter and milk; season.
Soften the onion, carrots and celery in oil for 10 minutes, then add the garlic and tomato paste.
Add the lentils, broth and thyme and simmer for 25 minutes until the lentils are soft and the sauce thick.
Season well and spoon into a baking dish.
Spread the mash over the top and rough up the surface with a fork.
Bake at 200 C for 25 minutes until the top is golden and crisp.

name: Cauliflower Steaks with Chimichurri
description: Thick roasted cauliflower slabs with crispy chickpeas and a punchy herb and garlic chimichurri.
instructions: Cut the cauliflower through the core into 4 thick steaks, keeping the loose florets.
Brush with olive oil, season with smoked paprika, salt and pepper and lay on a tray with the drained chickpeas.
Roast at 220 C for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until charred at the edges.
Finely chop the parsley, coriander and garlic and mix with vinegar, chili flakes, olive oil and salt.
Spoon the chimichurri generously over the steaks and chickpeas.

name: Black Bean Veggie Burgers
description: Hearty, smoky bean patties that hold together, served in buns with lettuce, tomato and mayo.
instructions: Drain and rinse the beans, pat dry and mash roughly, leaving some texture.
Mix in the oats, breadcrumbs, egg, finely chopped red onion, garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, salt and pepper.
Shape into 4 thick patties and chill for 20 minutes.
Fry in a little oil over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side until crisp and heated through.
Toast the buns and build the burgers with lettuce, tomato slices and mayonnaise.

name: Three-Bean Chili
description: Warming vegan chili loaded with mixed beans, corn and peppers, finished with lime and coriander.
instructions: Soften the chopped onion and peppers in oil for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, chili powder and cumin and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Tip in the crushed tomatoes, drained beans and corn and 200 ml water.
Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick.
Season with salt and lime juice and scatter with chopped coriander.
Serve with rice or tortilla chips.

name: Greek Zucchini Fritters with Feta
description: Crispy kolokithokeftedes: grated zucchini, feta, mint and dill fritters with a cool yogurt dip.
instructions: Grate the zucchini, toss with a teaspoon of salt and leave in a sieve for 15 minutes, then squeeze very dry.
Mix the zucchini with the crumbled feta, eggs, flour, chopped spring onions, dill, mint and pepper.
Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Drop in heaped spoonfuls of batter, flatten slightly and fry for 3 minutes per side until golden.
Drain on paper and serve hot with yogurt and lemon wedges.

name: Potato and Spinach Bake
description: A creamy gratin of thin potato slices and garlicky spinach with nutmeg and melted gruyere.
instructions: Slice the potatoes very thinly.
Soften the sliced onion and garlic in butter, add the spinach and cook until wilted; squeeze out excess liquid.
Warm the cream and milk with the nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Layer potatoes and spinach in a buttered dish, pouring the cream mixture over each layer.
Top with grated cheese, cover with foil and bake at 180 C for 45 minutes.
Uncover and bake 20 minutes more until golden and a knife slides in easily.

name: Halloumi with Roasted Vegetables
description: Golden seared halloumi over oregano-roasted peppers, zucchini and red onion with a honey-lemon drizzle.
instructions: Cut the peppers, zucchini and red onion into chunks and toss with olive oil, oregano, salt and pepper.
Roast at 220 C for 20 minutes, add the cherry tomatoes and roast 10 minutes more.
Slice the halloumi 1 cm thick and sear in a dry hot pan for 2 minutes per side until golden.
Whisk the lemon juice with the honey and a tablespoon of olive oil.
Pile the vegetables on plates, top with halloumi, drizzle with the dressing and scatter with mint.

name: Falafel Plate
description: Crunchy herb-packed chickpea falafel with warm pita and a lemony tahini sauce.
instructions: Soak the dried chickpeas in plenty of water for 12 hours, then drain well; do not cook them.
Blend the chickpeas with the onion, garlic, parsley, coriander, cumin, salt and baking soda to a coarse, grainy paste.
Chill the mixture for 30 minutes, then shape into walnut-sized balls.
Fry in 170 C oil for 4 minutes until deep brown and crisp; drain on paper.
Whisk the tahini with lemon juice, a pinch of salt and enough water to make a pourable sauce.
Serve the falafel with warm pita and the tahini sauce.

name: Quinoa-Stuffed Butternut Squash
description: Roasted squash halves filled with quinoa, kale, cranberries and toasted walnuts with a maple glaze.
instructions: Halve the squash lengthwise, scoop out the seeds, brush with oil and roast cut side down at 200 C for 40 minutes.
Rinse the quinoa and simmer in 400 ml water for 15 minutes until fluffy.
Soften the red onion and garlic in olive oil, add the chopped kale and cook until wilted.
Stir the quinoa, cranberries, walnuts, cinnamon, maple syrup, salt and pepper into the kale.
Turn the squash over, pile the filling into the cavities and bake for 10 minutes more.

name: Sarmale (Stuffed Cabbage Rolls)
description: Pickled cabbage leaves wrapped around a pork and rice filling, slow-simmered with smoked bacon and dill.
instructions: Rinse the pickled cabbage leaves, cut out the thick ribs and set aside; shred any torn leaves.
Sauté the chopped onions in oil until soft, add the rice and cook for 2 minutes, then cool.
Mix the minced pork with the onion-rice mixture, dill, thyme, pepper and 100 ml tomato sauce.
Place a spoonful of filling on each leaf, fold in the sides and roll tightly.
Line a heavy pot with shredded cabbage, pack the rolls in layers with the smoked bacon and bay leaves.
Pour over the remaining tomato sauce and enough water to cover, then simmer gently for 2 to 3 hours.
Serve hot with polenta and a spoonful of sour cream.

name: Mici (Romanian Grilled Minced Meat Rolls)
description: Juicy skinless sausages of beef and pork, seasoned with garlic, savory and pepper and grilled until charred.
instructions: Crush the garlic into a paste with a little salt and mix it with the beef broth.
Combine the minced meat with the garlic broth, baking soda, savory, pepper, paprika and salt.
Knead the mixture vigorously for 10 minutes until sticky, then cover and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight.
With wet hands, shape the meat into rolls about 7 cm long and 3 cm thick.
Grill over high heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side, turning often, until browned and cooked through.
Serve hot with mustard, fresh bread and pickles.

name: Tochitură (Romanian Pork Stew with Polenta)
description: Pork, sausages and smoked bacon fried with garlic and wine, served over polenta with a fried egg and cheese.
instructions: Cut the pork into 3 cm cubes and slice the sausages into chunks; dice the smoked bacon.
Render the bacon in a large pan, then brown the pork in batches over high heat.
Add the sausages and cook for 5 minutes, then pour in the wine and let it bubble.
Add the crushed garlic, paprika, thyme, pepper and a splash of water; cover and simmer for 40 minutes until tender.
Meanwhile bring 1 l salted water to the boil, whisk in the cornmeal and cook for 20 minutes to make polenta.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up.
Serve the stew over polenta, topped with a fried egg and crumbled telemea.

name: Chiftele (Romanian Fried Meatballs)
description: Crisp golden meatballs of minced pork, grated potato and onion, fragrant with garlic, dill and parsley.
instructions: Grate the potato and onion finely and squeeze out the excess liquid.
Mix the minced pork with the potato, onion, crushed garlic, egg, chopped dill and parsley, salt and pepper.
Add 2 tbsp flour to bind, then shape into walnut-sized balls and flatten slightly.
Roll each meatball in flour and shake off the excess.
Heat the oil in a deep pan and fry the meatballs in batches over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes per side until golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with mashed potatoes or a salad.

name: Chicken in Sour Cream with Polenta (Pui cu Smântână)
description: Braised chicken thighs in a garlicky sour cream sauce, ladled over soft golden polenta.
instructions: Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper and brown them in butter on both sides.
Add the chopped onion and cook until soft, then pour in the broth, cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Whisk the sour cream with the flour and a ladle of hot cooking liquid until smooth.
Stir the sour cream mixture and crushed garlic into the pan and simmer for 5 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Meanwhile bring 1 l salted water to the boil, rain in the cornmeal and cook, stirring, for 20 minutes.
Finish the chicken with chopped dill and serve over the polenta.

name: Ostropel (Chicken in Garlic Tomato Sauce)
description: Chicken pieces simmered in a sharp, garlicky tomato sauce with a splash of vinegar and fresh parsley.
instructions: Cut the chicken into pieces, season with salt and pepper and brown in oil until golden.
Remove the chicken, add the chopped onion to the pan and cook until soft.
Stir in the flour and paprika, then add the tomato sauce, tomato paste and 300 ml water.
Return the chicken, add the bay leaf and simmer covered for 30 minutes.
Stir in the crushed garlic and vinegar and simmer uncovered for 10 more minutes until the sauce thickens.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve with polenta or mashed potatoes.

name: Ciulama (Chicken in White Sauce)
description: Tender poached chicken in a silky white roux sauce, a Romanian classic served with hot polenta.
instructions: Simmer the chicken pieces with the whole onion, carrot, bay leaf and salt in 1.2 l water for 40 minutes.
Lift out the chicken, strain and reserve the broth, and discard the vegetables.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes without colouring.
Gradually whisk in 600 ml of the hot broth and the milk until smooth; simmer for 10 minutes.
Season with salt and white pepper, return the chicken to the sauce and warm through.
Serve over polenta, sprinkled with chopped parsley.

name: Romanian Roast Pork Neck (Friptură de Porc la Tavă)
description: Pork neck rubbed with garlic, paprika and thyme, roasted slowly in wine until deeply browned and juicy.
instructions: Make deep slits in the pork neck and push in slivers of garlic.
Rub the meat all over with lard, paprika, thyme, salt and pepper and leave for 30 minutes.
Place in a roasting tin with the quartered onions, pour in the wine and 200 ml water.
Cover with foil and roast at 180°C for 1 hour 15 minutes, basting occasionally.
Remove the foil, raise the heat to 220°C and roast for 20 more minutes until browned.
Rest for 10 minutes, slice and serve with the pan juices and pickles.

name: Chicken Schnitzel (Șnițel de Pui)
description: Thin chicken breast cutlets in a crisp golden breadcrumb crust, fried and finished with a squeeze of lemon.
instructions: Slice each chicken breast horizontally into two thin cutlets and pound them to 1 cm thickness.
Season with salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Set up three plates: flour, beaten eggs mixed with milk, and breadcrumbs.
Coat each cutlet in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, pressing gently.
Fry in hot oil over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve with lemon wedges and mashed potatoes.

name: Drob de Miel (Romanian Lamb Easter Loaf)
description: Easter loaf of chopped lamb offal, green onions and herbs bound with eggs, baked with whole eggs hidden inside.
instructions: Boil the offal in salted water for 20 minutes, drain, cool and chop finely.
Soak the bread in milk, squeeze and crumble it.
Hard-boil 3 of the eggs and peel them.
Sauté the chopped green onions in oil until soft, then mix with the offal, bread, 3 raw eggs, dill, parsley, salt and pepper.
Line a loaf tin with baking paper, fill halfway with the mixture, lay the boiled eggs in a row and cover with the rest.
Bake at 180°C for 50 minutes until firm and browned, then cool before slicing.

name: Chicken and Pea Stew (Mâncare de Mazăre cu Pui)
description: Sweet green peas and chicken thighs simmered in a light tomato sauce with plenty of fresh dill.
instructions: Brown the chicken thighs in oil on both sides, then set aside.
Soften the chopped onion and grated carrot in the same pan for 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and paprika, then add the tomato sauce and 400 ml water.
Return the chicken, season, cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the peas and cook for 10 more minutes until tender and the sauce has thickened.
Finish with chopped dill and serve with bread.

name: Green Bean Stew with Pork (Mâncare de Fasole Verde)
description: Tender green beans and pork shoulder braised with tomatoes, garlic and dill in a summery Romanian stew.
instructions: Trim the green beans and cut them in half.
Brown the pork cubes in oil over high heat, then add the chopped onion and cook until soft.
Add the grated tomatoes, tomato paste, paprika and 300 ml water; cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the green beans and cook for 20 minutes until tender.
Stir in the crushed garlic, season with salt and pepper and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Sprinkle with chopped dill and serve with bread.

name: Pork Goulash with Potatoes (Gulaș de Porc)
description: Hearty paprika-rich pork and potato goulash with peppers and caraway, a Transylvanian one-pot favourite.
instructions: Fry the chopped onions in lard until golden, then take the pan off the heat and stir in the paprika.
Add the pork cubes, return to the heat and brown for 5 minutes.
Add the chopped peppers, tomatoes, caraway, garlic, bay leaf and 800 ml water; simmer covered for 45 minutes.
Add the cubed potatoes and cook for 25 more minutes until tender.
Season with salt and pepper and let stand for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve with bread and a spoonful of sour cream.

name: Chicken Paprikash (Paprikaș de Pui)
description: Chicken thighs braised in a velvety paprika and sour cream sauce, perfect over dumplings or polenta.
instructions: Season the chicken thighs and brown them in lard, then set aside.
Cook the chopped onions in the same pan until golden, about 10 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the paprika, then add the chopped pepper, tomato and chicken broth.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer for 35 minutes until tender.
Whisk the sour cream with the flour, stir into the sauce and simmer gently for 5 minutes without boiling.
Season and serve with egg dumplings, polenta or boiled potatoes.

name: Stuffed Bell Peppers (Ardei Umpluți)
description: Bell peppers filled with minced meat and rice, simmered in tomato sauce and served with sour cream.
instructions: Cut the tops off the peppers and remove the seeds.
Sauté the chopped onion and grated carrot in oil until soft, add the rice and cook for 2 minutes.
Mix the minced meat with the onion-rice mixture, egg, chopped dill, salt and pepper.
Fill the peppers loosely with the mixture, leaving room for the rice to swell.
Stand the peppers in a pot, pour over the tomato sauce and 500 ml water, add the bay leaf and thyme.
Cover and simmer gently for 60 minutes until the peppers are soft and the rice is cooked.
Serve hot with a spoonful of sour cream.

name: Baked Potatoes with Pork (Cartofi cu Carne la Cuptor)
description: Layers of potatoes, onions and marinated pork neck baked in white wine until golden and tender.
instructions: Cut the pork into 3 cm chunks and toss with crushed garlic, paprika, thyme, salt, pepper and 2 tbsp oil.
Peel the potatoes and cut into thick wedges; slice the onions.
Spread the potatoes and onions in a large roasting tin and nestle the pork among them.
Pour over the wine and 200 ml water, tuck in the bay leaves and cover with foil.
Bake at 190°C for 60 minutes, then uncover and bake for 25 more minutes until browned.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with pickles.

name: Romanian Beef Stew (Tocană de Vită)
description: Slow-cooked beef with onions, tomatoes, garlic and red wine, served the Romanian way over polenta.
instructions: Brown the beef cubes in hot oil in batches and set aside.
Cook the sliced onions slowly in the same pot for 15 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the tomato paste and paprika, then add the wine and let it reduce by half.
Return the beef, add the crushed tomatoes, bay leaves, thyme and 400 ml water.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 hours until the beef is fork-tender.
Stir in the crushed garlic, season and simmer for 10 more minutes; serve with polenta.

name: Potato Moussaka (Musaca de Cartofi)
description: Sliced potatoes layered with spiced minced meat and tomato, baked under a creamy egg and sour cream top.
instructions: Peel and slice the potatoes 5 mm thick and parboil for 5 minutes; drain.
Brown the minced meat with the chopped onion, add the tomato sauce, thyme, salt and pepper and cook for 10 minutes.
Grease a baking dish, lay in half the potatoes, spread the meat over and top with the remaining potatoes.
Whisk the eggs with the sour cream and milk and pour evenly over the top.
Sprinkle with grated cheese and bake at 180°C for 50 minutes until golden.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting into squares.

name: Braised Cabbage with Sausages (Varză Călită cu Cârnați)
description: Sweet cabbage slowly braised with onion, tomato and thyme, topped with pan-fried pork sausages.
instructions: Shred the cabbage finely, sprinkle with salt and squeeze with your hands to soften.
Cook the chopped onion in oil until soft, add the cabbage and cook over medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring.
Stir in the tomato paste, thyme, pepper and 200 ml water; cover and braise for 40 minutes until very soft.
Fry the sausages in a separate pan for 12 to 15 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Stir the chopped dill into the cabbage and check the seasoning.
Serve the cabbage topped with the sausages and polenta or bread.

name: Hungarian Beef Pörkölt
description: Rich Hungarian beef stew built on slowly cooked onions, sweet paprika and lard, with a thick glossy sauce.
instructions: Melt the lard and cook the finely chopped onions over low heat for 20 minutes until deeply golden.
Remove from the heat, stir in the paprika and caraway, then add the beef cubes and coat well.
Add the chopped peppers, tomato, crushed garlic, salt and 300 ml water.
Cover and simmer very gently for 2 hours, adding a splash of water only if it dries out.
Uncover and cook for 15 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Serve with egg dumplings or boiled potatoes and a dollop of sour cream.

name: Polish Bigos (Hunter's Stew)
description: Sauerkraut and fresh cabbage slow-cooked with pork, smoked sausage, mushrooms and prunes.
instructions: Rinse the sauerkraut lightly and shred the fresh cabbage.
Brown the pork cubes and diced bacon in a large pot, then add the chopped onion and cook until soft.
Add the sliced smoked sausage, mushrooms, sauerkraut, cabbage, prunes, bay leaves, allspice and marjoram.
Pour in the wine and 400 ml water, stir in the tomato paste and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat for 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with rye bread; it tastes even better reheated the next day.

name: Serbian Pljeskavica (Grilled Meat Patties)
description: Large, juicy grilled patties of beef and pork with onion and paprika, served in flatbread with raw onion.
instructions: Mix the minced meat with the finely grated onion, crushed garlic, paprika, sparkling water, salt and pepper.
Knead well for 5 minutes until sticky, then cover and chill for at least 2 hours.
Divide into 4 portions and shape into wide, flat patties about 1.5 cm thick.
Grill or pan-fry over high heat for 5 to 6 minutes per side until charred and cooked through.
Warm the flatbreads briefly on the grill.
Serve the patties in flatbread with sliced red onion and a spoonful of sour cream or cream cheese.

name: Bulgarian Pork Kavarma
description: Bulgarian clay-pot stew of pork, peppers, mushrooms and tomatoes in white wine, topped with a cracked egg.
instructions: Brown the pork cubes in oil over high heat, then add the sliced onions and cook until soft.
Add the chopped peppers and mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, paprika, savory, wine, salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer for 45 minutes until the pork is tender and the sauce is thick.
Divide between ovenproof dishes, crack an egg on top of each and bake at 200°C for 10 minutes until just set.
Scatter with parsley and serve with crusty bread.

name: Classic Meatloaf
description: Moist beef and pork meatloaf with onion and herbs, baked under a sticky, tangy ketchup glaze.
instructions: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes.
Soften the finely chopped onion and garlic in a little oil, then cool.
Mix the minced meat with the soaked breadcrumbs, onion, eggs, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, salt and pepper.
Shape into a loaf on a lined baking tray or press into a loaf tin.
Stir the ketchup with the brown sugar and spread over the top.
Bake at 180°C for 60 minutes until cooked through; rest 10 minutes before slicing.

name: Meatballs in Tomato Sauce
description: Tender beef and pork meatballs simmered in a rich garlic and basil tomato sauce.
instructions: Soak the bread in milk, squeeze and crumble into a bowl.
Mix the minced meat with the bread, egg, grated Parmesan, half the garlic, chopped parsley, salt and pepper.
Shape into 20 meatballs and brown them in olive oil on all sides; set aside.
In the same pan, cook the chopped onion and remaining garlic until soft, then add the crushed tomatoes and oregano.
Return the meatballs to the sauce, cover and simmer for 25 minutes.
Tear in the basil leaves and serve with mashed potatoes, polenta or crusty bread.

name: Pork Chops with Caramelised Apples
description: Pan-seared pork chops with buttery caramelised apples and onions in a cider vinegar and thyme pan sauce.
instructions: Pat the pork chops dry and season generously with salt and pepper.
Sear in hot oil for 4 minutes per side until golden, then transfer to a plate.
Melt the butter in the pan, add the sliced apples and onion and cook for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the thyme, vinegar and brown sugar and let it bubble for 1 minute.
Pour in the broth, return the chops and simmer for 5 minutes until cooked through and the sauce is glossy.
Serve with mashed potatoes.

name: Shepherd's Pie
description: Minced lamb and vegetables in a savoury gravy, baked under a golden crust of buttery mashed potatoes.
instructions: Boil the peeled potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes, drain and mash with the butter and milk.
Brown the minced lamb in a large pan, then add the chopped onion, carrots and celery and cook for 8 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and flour, then add the broth, Worcestershire sauce and thyme.
Simmer for 15 minutes until thickened, stir in the peas and season.
Spoon the filling into a baking dish, top with the mash and rough up the surface with a fork.
Bake at 200°C for 25 minutes until golden and bubbling.

name: Chicken Cordon Bleu
description: Breaded chicken breasts rolled around ham and melting Emmental, fried golden and finished in the oven.
instructions: Butterfly the chicken breasts, cover with cling film and pound to 1 cm thickness.
Season each breast, lay a slice of ham and a slice of cheese on top and roll up tightly; secure with toothpicks.
Dredge the rolls in flour, dip in beaten egg and coat in breadcrumbs.
Fry in oil and butter over medium heat for 3 minutes per side until golden.
Transfer to a baking tray and bake at 180°C for 15 minutes until cooked through.
Remove the toothpicks and serve with a green salad or buttered vegetables.

name: Coq au Vin
description: French chicken braised in red wine with bacon, mushrooms and shallots until the sauce is dark and glossy.
instructions: Fry the diced bacon in butter until crisp, remove, then brown the seasoned chicken pieces in the fat.
Add the whole peeled shallots and cook until golden, then stir in the garlic and flour.
Pour in the brandy and the red wine, scraping the bottom of the pot, then add the broth, thyme and bay leaf.
Return the bacon, cover and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Sauté the mushrooms in butter and add them for the last 10 minutes.
Season, sprinkle with parsley and serve with mashed potatoes or crusty bread.

name: Beef Bourguignon
description: Burgundy-style beef slow-braised in red wine with bacon, carrots, pearl shallots and mushrooms.
instructions: Fry the diced bacon in oil until crisp, remove, then brown the beef cubes in batches.
Add the chopped onion and sliced carrots and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in the flour and tomato paste.
Pour in the wine and broth, add the garlic, thyme and bay leaf and return the bacon.
Cover and cook in the oven at 160°C for 2.5 hours until the beef is meltingly tender.
Brown the shallots and mushrooms in butter and stir them in for the final 30 minutes.
Season and serve with boiled potatoes and chopped parsley.

name: Swedish Meatballs in Cream Gravy
description: Small nutmeg-spiced meatballs in a creamy brown gravy, served with mashed potatoes and lingonberry jam.
instructions: Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes.
Mix the minced meat with the soaked crumbs, finely grated onion, egg, allspice, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Roll into small 3 cm meatballs and fry in butter in batches until browned all over; set aside.
Stir the flour into the pan fat and cook for 1 minute, then whisk in the beef broth.
Add the cream and mustard, return the meatballs and simmer for 10 minutes until the gravy thickens.
Serve with mashed potatoes and a spoonful of lingonberry jam.

name: Pork Tenderloin Medallions in Mustard Cream Sauce
description: Quick-seared pork medallions in a silky wholegrain mustard, white wine and cream sauce.
instructions: Slice the tenderloin into 3 cm medallions and season with salt and pepper.
Sear in butter and oil over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden; set aside.
Soften the chopped shallots in the pan, then deglaze with the white wine and reduce by half.
Stir in the broth, cream and mustard and simmer for 3 minutes.
Return the medallions and warm through for 2 minutes without boiling.
Sprinkle with chopped chives and serve with potatoes or green beans.

name: Honey-Mustard Baked Chicken Thighs
description: Sticky, golden chicken thighs baked in a honey, Dijon mustard and garlic glaze.
instructions: Whisk together the honey, mustard, olive oil, crushed garlic, lemon juice, thyme, salt and pepper.
Pat the chicken thighs dry and toss them in the glaze; marinate for 20 minutes if time allows.
Arrange skin-side up in a baking dish and pour over any remaining glaze.
Bake at 200°C for 35 to 40 minutes, basting once, until golden and cooked through.
Spoon the pan juices over the chicken and sprinkle with parsley.
Serve with rice, potatoes or steamed vegetables.

name: Lemon-Garlic Roast Chicken
description: A whole chicken roasted with lemon, garlic, thyme and butter for crisp skin and juicy meat.
instructions: Pat the chicken dry and season the cavity with salt and pepper.
Mash the softened butter with the lemon zest, 2 crushed garlic cloves and chopped thyme.
Loosen the skin over the breast and push the butter underneath; rub the rest over the skin.
Stuff the cavity with the halved lemon, the remaining whole garlic cloves and thyme sprigs.
Set the chicken on the sliced onions in a roasting tin, pour in the broth and roast at 200°C for 1 hour 20 minutes.
Rest for 15 minutes, carve and serve with the pan juices.

name: Chicken Kiev
description: Crisp breaded chicken breast hiding a molten core of garlic and parsley butter.
instructions: Mash the butter with the crushed garlic, chopped parsley, lemon juice and a pinch of salt; shape into 4 logs and freeze for 20 minutes.
Cut a deep pocket into the side of each chicken breast and insert a butter log; press the edges to seal.
Coat each breast in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs; repeat the egg and crumb layer for a thick crust.
Chill for 20 minutes to set the coating.
Fry in hot oil for 3 minutes per side until golden, then bake at 180°C for 15 minutes.
Serve immediately so the butter runs out when cut.

name: Wiener Schnitzel
description: Paper-thin veal cutlets in a puffed, golden breadcrumb crust, fried in butter and served with lemon.
instructions: Pound the veal cutlets between cling film to 4 mm thickness and season with salt.
Coat each cutlet in flour, then in the beaten eggs, then in breadcrumbs without pressing.
Heat the clarified butter and oil in a wide pan until a crumb sizzles immediately.
Fry the schnitzels one at a time for about 2 minutes per side, swirling the pan so the crust puffs.
Drain on paper towels.
Serve with lemon wedges, parsley and a potato salad or parsley potatoes.

name: Roast Pork Belly with Crackling
description: Slow-roasted pork belly with shatteringly crisp salted crackling and a fennel and garlic rub.
instructions: Score the pork skin in lines 1 cm apart, pat very dry and rub with 1 tbsp salt; leave uncovered in the fridge overnight.
Crush the fennel seeds, garlic, pepper and thyme with the oil and rub into the meat side only.
Lay the sliced onions and halved apples in a roasting tin and set the pork on top, skin up.
Roast at 240°C for 30 minutes until the skin blisters, then reduce to 160°C and roast for 1 hour 45 minutes.
Rest for 15 minutes while you add the wine to the tin juices and simmer into a gravy.
Slice with a serrated knife and serve with the gravy and roast apples.

name: Rosemary and Garlic Lamb Chops
description: Lamb chops marinated in rosemary, garlic and olive oil, seared pink with a squeeze of lemon.
instructions: Mix the olive oil with the crushed garlic, chopped rosemary, lemon zest, salt and pepper.
Coat the lamb chops in the marinade and leave for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Heat a heavy pan or grill until very hot.
Sear the chops for 3 to 4 minutes per side for pink meat, holding the fat edge against the pan to crisp it.
Rest for 5 minutes under foil.
Squeeze over the lemon juice and serve with roast potatoes or a green salad.

name: Irish Lamb Stew
description: Simple, soul-warming Irish stew of lamb, potatoes, carrots and onions simmered slowly in broth with thyme.
instructions: Brown the lamb cubes in oil in batches and set aside.
Soften the sliced onions and leek in the same pot for 5 minutes.
Return the lamb, add the broth, bay leaf and thyme, cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the thickly sliced carrots and halved potatoes and cook for 40 more minutes until tender.
Mash a few potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken the broth.
Season with salt and pepper and scatter with parsley before serving.

name: Oven-Baked BBQ Pork Ribs
description: Fall-off-the-bone pork ribs rubbed with smoky spices, slow-baked and lacquered with sticky barbecue sauce.
instructions: Peel the membrane off the back of the ribs.
Mix the brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, pepper and cayenne and rub all over the ribs.
Wrap tightly in foil and bake at 150°C for 2.5 hours until tender.
Unwrap, brush generously with BBQ sauce mixed with the vinegar.
Bake uncovered at 220°C for 15 minutes, brushing once more, until sticky and charred at the edges.
Rest for 5 minutes, cut between the bones and serve with extra sauce.

name: Sloppy Joes
description: Saucy, sweet-and-tangy minced beef with peppers and onion piled into soft toasted burger buns.
instructions: Brown the minced beef in a large pan, breaking it up with a spoon.
Add the chopped onion, bell pepper and garlic and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the tomato sauce, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, brown sugar and vinegar.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes until thick and glossy; season with salt and pepper.
Split and toast the burger buns.
Pile the meat onto the buns and serve with pickles.

name: Chicken Parmesan
description: Crisp breaded chicken cutlets baked under tomato sauce, melted mozzarella and Parmesan.
instructions: Halve the chicken breasts horizontally and pound to 1 cm thick; season with salt and pepper.
Mix the breadcrumbs with half the Parmesan and the oregano.
Coat the cutlets in flour, then beaten egg, then the Parmesan crumbs.
Fry in olive oil for 3 minutes per side until golden and transfer to a baking dish.
Spoon the tomato sauce over each cutlet, top with sliced mozzarella and the remaining Parmesan.
Bake at 200°C for 15 minutes until bubbling; scatter with basil and serve.

name: Duck Breast with Orange Sauce
description: Crisp-skinned pan-roasted duck breast sliced over a glossy bittersweet orange and honey sauce.
instructions: Score the duck skin in a diamond pattern and season with salt and pepper.
Place skin-side down in a cold pan and cook over medium heat for 8 minutes until the fat renders and the skin is crisp.
Flip and cook for 3 minutes, then transfer to a 200°C oven for 6 minutes for pink meat; rest 5 minutes.
Pour off the fat, add the honey and let it caramelise, then deglaze with the vinegar.
Add the orange juice, zest and broth and reduce by half; whisk in the cold butter.
Slice the duck and serve with the sauce and orange segments.

name: Beef Stroganoff
description: Strips of seared beef and mushrooms in a tangy sour cream, mustard and paprika sauce.
instructions: Slice the beef into thin strips and season with salt, pepper and paprika.
Sear the beef in very hot butter in batches for 1 minute until browned but still pink; set aside.
Cook the sliced onion and mushrooms in the pan for 8 minutes until golden.
Stir in the flour, then add the broth, Worcestershire sauce and mustard and simmer for 3 minutes.
Lower the heat, stir in the sour cream and return the beef; warm through without boiling.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with mashed potatoes or buttered rice.

name: Sausage and Mash with Onion Gravy
description: British pub classic of browned pork sausages on creamy mash, smothered in sweet, rich onion gravy.
instructions: Boil the peeled potatoes for 20 minutes, drain and mash with the butter, warm milk, salt and pepper.
Fry the sausages in a little oil over medium heat for 15 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through; keep warm.
In the same pan cook the thinly sliced onions with the sugar for 15 minutes until deeply caramelised.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the beef broth and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer for 5 minutes until the gravy thickens and season to taste.
Serve the sausages on the mash with plenty of onion gravy.

name: Butter Chicken
description: Tender yogurt-marinated chicken simmered in a silky, buttery tomato and cream sauce with warm spices.
instructions: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and mix with the yogurt, half the garam masala, turmeric and a pinch of salt; marinate for at least 15 minutes.
Melt the butter in a large pan and brown the chicken pieces in batches, then set aside.
In the same pan, soften the finely chopped onion, then add the grated garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, remaining garam masala and sweet paprika and simmer for 10 minutes until thick.
Blend the sauce until smooth if you like, return the chicken to the pan and pour in the cream.
Simmer gently for 10 minutes, season with salt and serve with rice or naan, scattered with fresh coriander.

name: Chicken Tikka Masala
description: Charred spiced chicken chunks folded into a fragrant, creamy tomato masala sauce.
instructions: Cube the chicken breast and toss with yogurt, lemon juice, half the garam masala, cumin, smoked paprika and a little salt; marinate 20 minutes.
Heat a grill pan or heavy frying pan very hot and sear the chicken until charred at the edges; set aside.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and cook the chopped onion until golden, then add garlic, ginger and the chili pepper for 1 minute.
Add the remaining garam masala, coriander seeds and crushed tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cooking cream and the seared chicken and simmer 8 to 10 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Finish with chopped fresh coriander and serve with basmati rice.

name: Chana Masala
description: Hearty chickpeas stewed with tomatoes, ginger and toasted spices, finished with lime and coriander.
instructions: Heat the oil in a deep pan and toast the cumin seeds for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the finely chopped onion and cook until deeply golden, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the grated garlic, ginger and chopped chili and cook for 1 minute, then add turmeric, ground coriander and garam masala.
Add the crushed tomatoes and simmer for 5 minutes until the oil starts to separate.
Tip in the drained chickpeas with 200 ml water, season with salt and simmer for 15 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas to thicken.
Squeeze in lime juice, scatter with fresh coriander and serve with rice or flatbread.

name: Dal Tadka
description: Creamy red lentils with turmeric, topped with a sizzling tempering of garlic, cumin and chili in butter.
instructions: Rinse the lentils and simmer with 900 ml water, the turmeric and a pinch of salt for 20 minutes until soft and creamy.
Stir in the chopped tomato and cook 5 minutes more, mashing lightly with a spoon.
For the tadka, melt the butter in a small pan and sizzle the cumin seeds and mustard seeds until they pop.
Add the sliced garlic, chopped onion and chili and fry until golden, then stir in the chili flakes and garam masala for a few seconds.
Pour the hot tempering over the dal, stir once, and finish with lemon juice and fresh coriander.
Serve with rice or warm flatbread.

name: Aloo Gobi
description: Golden potatoes and cauliflower florets pan-roasted with turmeric, cumin and ginger until tender.
instructions: Cut the potatoes into 2 cm cubes and break the cauliflower into small florets.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and toast the cumin seeds, then add the chopped onion and cook until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger and chili and stir for 1 minute, then add turmeric, ground coriander and sweet paprika.
Add the potatoes, cauliflower, chopped tomatoes and salt, stir to coat, and cover with a lid.
Cook on low heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are tender and lightly browned.
Sprinkle with garam masala and fresh coriander and serve with flatbread.

name: Palak Paneer
description: Cubes of fried paneer in a vibrant, spiced spinach puree enriched with a swirl of cream.
instructions: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 1 minute, drain, cool under cold water and blend to a coarse puree.
Fry the paneer cubes in half the butter until golden on all sides and set aside.
Melt the remaining butter and cook the chopped onion until soft, then add garlic, ginger and chili for 1 minute.
Add cumin, garam masala and the chopped tomato and cook for 5 minutes until jammy.
Stir in the spinach puree and 100 ml water, season with salt and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the paneer and cream, warm through for 3 minutes and serve with naan or rice.

name: Thai Green Chicken Curry
description: Fragrant coconut curry with chicken, green beans and bell pepper, sharpened with lime and fish sauce.
instructions: Slice the chicken thighs into strips, trim the green beans and slice the bell pepper.
Heat the oil in a wok and fry the green curry paste for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add half the coconut milk and simmer until the oil splits and the sauce thickens slightly.
Add the chicken and cook for 5 minutes, then pour in the remaining coconut milk, fish sauce and brown sugar.
Add the green beans and pepper and simmer 8 minutes until the chicken is cooked and vegetables are tender-crisp.
Finish with lime juice and torn basil leaves and serve over jasmine rice.

name: Thai Red Curry with Shrimp
description: Plump shrimp and butternut squash in a rich red coconut curry, ready in under half an hour.
instructions: Peel and cube the butternut squash into 2 cm pieces and slice the red onion.
Fry the red curry paste in oil for 1 minute, then add the coconut milk and 100 ml water.
Add the squash and simmer for 12 minutes until almost tender.
Stir in the fish sauce, brown sugar and grated ginger, then add the shrimp and cook 3 to 4 minutes until pink.
Add a handful of spinach and let it wilt, then squeeze in the lime juice.
Serve over rice with fresh coriander and a few slices of chili on top.

name: Pad Thai
description: Stir-fried rice noodles with shrimp, egg and bean sprouts in a sweet-sour tamarind-style sauce with peanuts.
instructions: Soak the rice noodles in hot water for 8 to 10 minutes until pliable, then drain.
Mix the fish sauce, brown sugar, lime juice and a splash of soy sauce for the sauce.
Heat the oil in a large wok and fry the garlic and shrimp for 2 minutes until the shrimp turn pink.
Push everything to one side, crack in the eggs and scramble, then add the noodles and the sauce and toss for 2 minutes.
Add the bean sprouts and most of the chopped green onions and toss for 1 more minute.
Serve topped with crushed peanuts, chili flakes, fresh coriander and lime wedges.

name: Thai Basil Chicken
description: Fiery minced chicken stir-fried with garlic, chili and a mountain of basil, served over rice with a fried egg.
instructions: Cook the rice according to the package instructions and keep warm.
Pound or finely chop the garlic and chilies together.
Heat the oil in a wok over very high heat and fry the garlic-chili mix for 30 seconds.
Add the minced chicken and stir-fry, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through, about 6 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce and brown sugar and toss for 1 minute, then turn off the heat and fold in the basil leaves.
Fry the eggs in a separate pan until the edges are crisp and serve on top of the chicken and rice.

name: Sweet and Sour Chicken
description: Crispy battered chicken tossed with peppers and pineapple in a glossy sweet and sour sauce.
instructions: Cut the chicken into chunks, season, and toss in beaten egg then cornstarch until coated.
Shallow-fry the chicken in hot oil in batches until golden and crisp, then drain on paper.
Whisk together the pineapple juice from the can, ketchup, vinegar, soy sauce, sugar and 1 tbsp cornstarch.
In a wok, stir-fry the chopped onion, bell peppers and garlic for 3 minutes.
Pour in the sauce and pineapple chunks and simmer until thick and glossy, about 2 minutes.
Toss the crispy chicken through the sauce and serve immediately with rice.

name: Kung Pao Chicken
description: Sichuan-style stir-fry of chicken, dried chilies and roasted peanuts in a savoury, tangy glaze.
instructions: Dice the chicken and marinate with 1 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tbsp cornstarch for 10 minutes.
Mix the remaining soy sauce, rice vinegar, hoisin sauce, sugar and 2 tbsp water for the sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok until smoking, add the whole chilies and black pepper and toast for 20 seconds.
Add the chicken and stir-fry for 4 to 5 minutes until golden, then add garlic, ginger and the diced bell pepper.
Pour in the sauce and toss until it coats everything and thickens, about 1 minute.
Stir in the peanuts and green onions, drizzle with sesame oil and serve with steamed rice.

name: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
description: Velvety strips of beef and crisp broccoli florets glazed in a garlicky oyster-soy sauce.
instructions: Slice the beef thinly against the grain and toss with 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp cornstarch and a pinch of baking soda; rest 15 minutes.
Blanch the broccoli florets in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Mix the remaining soy sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil and 100 ml beef broth for the sauce.
Sear the beef in very hot oil in batches until browned, about 2 minutes per batch, and set aside.
Stir-fry the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, add the broccoli and sauce and bubble until thickened.
Return the beef, toss to coat and serve over rice with sesame seeds.

name: Mapo Tofu
description: Silky tofu and minced pork in a bold, numbing-hot chili and garlic sauce over steamed rice.
instructions: Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes and leave in warm salted water while you prepare the sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok and brown the minced pork, breaking it up, for 4 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, chopped chilies, chili flakes and ground black pepper and fry for 1 minute.
Stir in the hoisin sauce, soy sauce and miso paste, then pour in the chicken broth and bring to a simmer.
Gently slide in the drained tofu and simmer for 5 minutes, then thicken with the cornstarch mixed in 2 tbsp water.
Finish with sesame oil and green onions and serve over rice.

name: Egg Fried Rice with Vegetables
description: Takeaway-style fried rice with fluffy egg, peas, carrots and spring onions, best made with cold leftover rice.
instructions: Use rice cooked the day before, or cook it fresh and spread it out to cool completely.
Beat the eggs and scramble them in 1 tbsp oil over high heat until just set; remove from the wok.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the diced carrot, garlic and ginger for 2 minutes, then add the peas.
Add the cold rice, pressing and tossing it for 3 to 4 minutes until every grain is hot and slightly crisp.
Season with soy sauce, oyster sauce and white pepper, then fold in the eggs and sliced green onions.
Drizzle with sesame oil and serve straight away.

ingredients.note: cooked and cooled, from about 350 g dry

name: Chicken Chow Mein
description: Springy egg noodles tossed with chicken, cabbage, carrots and bean sprouts in a savoury soy glaze.
instructions: Cook the egg noodles until just tender, drain, rinse under cold water and toss with 1 tsp sesame oil.
Slice the chicken thinly and marinate with 1 tbsp soy sauce and the cornstarch.
Mix the remaining soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and 3 tbsp water for the sauce.
Stir-fry the chicken in hot oil for 4 minutes until golden, then add garlic, shredded cabbage and julienned carrot for 2 minutes.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes until the noodles are glossy.
Toss in the bean sprouts and green onions, cook 1 minute more and serve.

name: Chicken Teriyaki
description: Juicy chicken thighs lacquered in a sticky homemade soy, honey and ginger glaze over steamed rice.
instructions: Mix the soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, grated ginger and garlic in a bowl.
Pat the chicken thighs dry and cook skin-side down in a hot pan with the oil for 6 minutes until golden, then flip.
Pour the sauce over the chicken, lower the heat and simmer, turning occasionally, for 10 minutes.
Remove the chicken and reduce the sauce until it is thick and glossy, about 2 minutes.
Slice the chicken, spoon over the glaze and sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onions.
Serve with steamed rice and lightly steamed broccoli.

name: Chicken Katsu Curry
description: Crunchy panko-crusted chicken cutlets served with a mild, sweet Japanese-style curry sauce and rice.
instructions: For the sauce, soften the chopped onion, carrot and garlic in half the oil, then stir in the flour and curry powder and cook 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the chicken broth, add the soy sauce and honey and simmer 15 minutes until smooth and thick; blend if desired.
Flatten the chicken breasts to even thickness, season, then coat in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs.
Shallow-fry the chicken in the remaining oil for 4 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through.
Rest the cutlets for 2 minutes, then slice into strips.
Serve over rice with the curry sauce poured over and shredded cabbage on the side.

name: Salmon Teriyaki
description: Pan-seared salmon fillets glazed with teriyaki sauce, served with sesame bok choy and rice.
instructions: Cook the rice and keep warm.
Pat the salmon dry and season lightly with salt; heat the oil in a non-stick pan.
Sear the salmon skin-side down for 4 minutes, flip and cook 2 minutes more.
Pour in the teriyaki sauce, honey and grated ginger and spoon the bubbling glaze over the fish for 1 to 2 minutes.
In another pan, stir-fry the halved bok choy with garlic and a splash of soy sauce for 3 minutes until just wilted.
Serve the salmon on rice with the bok choy, drizzled with sesame oil and sprinkled with sesame seeds and green onions.

name: Chicken Yakitori Skewers
description: Grilled chicken and spring onion skewers brushed with a sweet soy tare glaze, served over rice.
instructions: Soak the wooden skewers in water for 20 minutes to prevent burning.
Simmer the soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, garlic and ginger for 8 minutes until syrupy to make the tare.
Cut the chicken thighs into 3 cm pieces and the green onions into 3 cm lengths; thread alternately onto the skewers.
Brush with oil and grill on a hot grill pan or barbecue for 4 minutes per side.
Brush generously with the tare and grill 1 to 2 more minutes per side until caramelised.
Serve over rice with the remaining glaze, sesame seeds and a squeeze of lemon.

name: Bibimbap
description: Korean rice bowl with seasoned beef, sauteed vegetables, a fried egg and a spoonful of spicy gochujang.
instructions: Cook the rice and keep warm.
Slice the beef thinly and marinate with 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, half the garlic and 1 tsp sugar for 10 minutes.
Saute the julienned carrot, sliced zucchini and mushrooms separately in a little oil, seasoning each with salt; wilt the spinach and dress it with sesame oil and the remaining garlic.
Stir-fry the beef over high heat for 3 minutes until browned.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up.
Divide the rice among bowls, arrange the vegetables and beef on top, add an egg, a spoon of gochujang and sesame seeds, and mix before eating.

name: Beef Bulgogi
description: Thin slices of beef marinated in soy, pear, garlic and sesame, seared hot and served with rice and lettuce.
instructions: Freeze the beef for 30 minutes so you can slice it paper-thin against the grain.
Grate the pear and mix with soy sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, grated garlic, ginger and black pepper.
Toss the beef and sliced onion in the marinade and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat a large pan or grill pan until very hot and sear the beef in batches for 2 to 3 minutes until caramelised.
Sprinkle with green onions and sesame seeds.
Serve with rice and lettuce leaves for wrapping, with gochujang on the side.

name: Vietnamese Lemongrass Pork
description: Charred lemongrass-marinated pork over rice noodles with crisp cucumber, herbs and a tangy lime dressing.
instructions: Finely chop the tender inner part of the lemongrass and mix with fish sauce, brown sugar, garlic, shallots and oil.
Slice the pork thinly, coat in the marinade and leave for at least 30 minutes.
Cook the rice noodles per the packet, rinse under cold water and drain.
Whisk the lime juice with 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 4 tbsp water and the sliced chili for the dressing.
Grill or pan-sear the pork over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side until charred at the edges.
Serve the pork over the noodles with cucumber ribbons, lettuce, mint and coriander, with the dressing poured over and peanuts on top.

name: Vietnamese Caramelised Pork
description: Pork belly braised in a dark, savoury caramel with fish sauce, black pepper and shallots until sticky.
instructions: Cut the pork belly into 3 cm cubes and blanch in boiling water for 3 minutes; drain and pat dry.
Melt the sugar with 2 tbsp water in a heavy pot over medium heat until it turns a deep amber caramel.
Carefully add the pork and stir to coat, then add the sliced shallots, garlic and ginger.
Pour in the fish sauce, soy sauce, coconut water and black pepper and bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise over low heat for 45 minutes, then uncover and reduce until the sauce is glossy and the pork is tender.
Add the halved boiled eggs for the last 5 minutes and serve over rice with green onions and sliced chili.

name: Chicken Fajitas
description: Sizzling strips of spiced chicken with charred peppers and onions, wrapped in warm tortillas.
instructions: Slice the chicken, bell peppers and onions into thin strips.
Toss the chicken with the oil, cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, dried oregano, garlic and salt.
Heat a large skillet until very hot and cook the chicken for 5 to 6 minutes until browned; set aside.
Add the peppers and onions to the pan and char for 5 minutes, then return the chicken and squeeze over the lime.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan or wrapped in foil in the oven.
Serve the fajita mix in tortillas with sour cream, avocado slices and fresh coriander.

name: Beef Tacos
description: Spiced minced beef in warm tortillas piled with lettuce, tomato, cheese and a squeeze of lime.
instructions: Heat the oil in a pan and soften the chopped onion and garlic for 4 minutes.
Add the minced beef and brown well, breaking it up with a spoon.
Stir in the cumin, chili powder, smoked paprika, dried oregano and tomato paste and cook 1 minute.
Add 150 ml water and simmer for 10 minutes until thick and saucy; season with salt.
Warm the tortillas and shred the lettuce, dice the tomatoes and grate the cheese.
Fill the tortillas with beef and toppings, add sour cream and finish with lime juice and coriander.

name: Chicken Enchiladas
description: Tortillas rolled around shredded chicken and beans, smothered in smoky chili-tomato sauce and melted cheese.
instructions: Poach the chicken breasts in simmering water for 15 minutes, then shred with two forks.
For the sauce, cook the chopped onion and garlic in oil, add chili powder, cumin and smoked paprika, then the tomato sauce and chicken broth and simmer 10 minutes.
Mix the shredded chicken with the drained beans, canned corn, half the cheese and a ladle of sauce.
Spread a little sauce in a baking dish, fill each tortilla with the chicken mixture, roll and place seam-side down.
Pour the remaining sauce over the top and scatter with the remaining cheese.
Bake at 200 C for 20 minutes until bubbling; serve with sour cream and fresh coriander.

name: Chicken Burrito Bowl
description: Lime-coriander rice topped with spiced chicken, black beans, corn, avocado and salsa for a filling bowl.
instructions: Cook the rice, then fold through chopped coriander and the juice of one lime.
Toss the diced chicken with oil, cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, garlic and salt and pan-fry for 7 to 8 minutes until cooked.
Warm the drained black beans in a small pan with a pinch of cumin and salt.
Dice the tomatoes and red onion and mix with the remaining lime juice to make a quick salsa.
Slice the avocado and drain the corn.
Assemble bowls with rice, chicken, beans, corn, salsa and avocado, finishing with sour cream and grated cheese.

name: Chili con Carne
description: Slow-simmered beef and kidney bean chili with smoky spices, a touch of cocoa and plenty of heat.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot and cook the chopped onion, bell pepper and garlic until soft, about 6 minutes.
Add the minced beef and brown thoroughly, breaking it up.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, dried oregano, cocoa powder and tomato paste and cook 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes, beef broth and bay leaf, season and simmer uncovered for 40 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the drained kidney beans and cook 10 minutes more; adjust salt and heat with hot sauce.
Serve with rice or tortilla chips, topped with sour cream, grated cheese and coriander.

name: Chicken Quesadillas
description: Crisp golden tortillas stuffed with spiced chicken, peppers and gooey melted cheese, cut into wedges.
instructions: Dice the chicken and cook in oil with cumin, smoked paprika, salt and the chopped onion and bell pepper for 8 minutes.
Stir in the drained corn and chopped green onions and remove from the heat.
Lay a tortilla in a dry non-stick pan, cover half with grated cheese, chicken mixture and a little more cheese, then fold over.
Cook over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and the cheese has melted.
Repeat with the remaining tortillas, keeping the cooked ones warm in a low oven.
Cut into wedges and serve with sour cream, lime wedges and chopped coriander.

name: Chicken Shawarma Plate
description: Yogurt and spice marinated chicken roasted until charred, served with garlic sauce, pita and salad.
