instructions: Mix the yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil, garlic, cumin, coriander, sweet paprika, turmeric, cinnamon and salt.
Coat the chicken thighs in the marinade and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, ideally overnight.
Roast the chicken with the sliced onion at 220 C for 25 to 30 minutes until charred at the edges, then slice into strips.
Stir the extra garlic into the remaining 150 g yogurt with a pinch of salt for a quick garlic sauce.
Dice the cucumber and tomatoes and toss with chopped parsley and a squeeze of lemon.
Serve the chicken with warm pita, the salad, garlic sauce and hummus.

name: Lamb Kofta with Yogurt Sauce
description: Juicy grilled lamb and herb koftas with a cooling mint yogurt sauce, warm pita and tomato salad.
instructions: Grate the onion and squeeze out the excess juice, then mix with the minced lamb, garlic, cumin, coriander, allspice, chili flakes, chopped parsley and salt.
Shape into 12 oval koftas around skewers or free-form, and chill for 15 minutes.
Stir the chopped mint and half a crushed garlic clove into the yogurt with lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Grill the koftas on a hot grill pan or barbecue brushed with olive oil for 4 minutes per side until browned and cooked through.
Dice the tomatoes and red onion for a quick salad and dress with lemon and olive oil.
Serve the koftas with warm pita, the yogurt sauce and salad.

name: Moroccan Chicken Tagine
description: Chicken thighs braised with preserved-lemon-style zest, green olives, saffron and warm spices.
instructions: Season the chicken thighs with salt, cumin, ginger powder, turmeric, sweet paprika and cinnamon.
Brown the chicken in olive oil in a heavy casserole, skin side first, then remove.
Soften the sliced onions and garlic in the same pot for 6 minutes.
Return the chicken, add the chicken broth, saffron and lemon zest and juice, cover and simmer gently for 35 minutes.
Add the olives and chopped coriander stems and cook uncovered for 10 minutes to thicken the sauce.
Scatter with coriander leaves and serve with couscous or flatbread.

name: Moroccan Vegetable Tagine
description: Sweet and spiced stew of squash, chickpeas, carrots and apricots with harissa, served over couscous.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a casserole and soften the chopped onion and garlic for 5 minutes.
Stir in the cumin, ground coriander, cinnamon, turmeric and harissa and fry for 1 minute.
Add the cubed butternut squash, sliced carrots, chopped zucchini, crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth.
Simmer covered for 20 minutes, then add the drained chickpeas and chopped dried apricots and cook 10 minutes more until the vegetables are tender.
Season with salt and a squeeze of lemon.
Serve over couscous with fresh coriander and toasted almonds.

name: Harissa Chicken with Couscous
description: Spicy harissa-roasted chicken and red onions on fluffy lemon couscous with herbs and feta.
instructions: Mix the harissa, olive oil, lemon zest, cumin, honey and salt and rub all over the chicken thighs.
Spread the chicken and wedges of red onion on a tray and roast at 210 C for 30 minutes until sticky and cooked through.
Pour boiling chicken broth over the couscous, cover and leave for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Stir the lemon juice, chopped parsley, mint and halved cherry tomatoes into the couscous.
Crumble the feta over the couscous.
Serve the chicken and onions on the couscous with the tray juices spooned over.

name: BBQ Pulled Pork Sandwiches
description: Slow-roasted pork shoulder shredded into smoky barbecue sauce and piled onto soft buns with crunchy slaw.
instructions: Rub the pork shoulder with brown sugar, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cumin, salt and pepper.
Place in a deep roasting dish with the sliced onion, 100 ml apple cider vinegar and 200 ml water, cover tightly with foil.
Roast at 150 C for 4 hours until the pork pulls apart easily.
Shred the meat with two forks, discard excess fat, and mix with the BBQ sauce and some of the pan juices.
Toss the shredded cabbage and grated carrot with mayonnaise, a splash of vinegar and salt for the slaw.
Toast the buns and fill with pulled pork and slaw.

name: Buffalo Chicken Wings
description: Oven-crisped chicken wings tossed in buttery hot sauce, served with blue cheese dip and celery sticks.
instructions: Pat the wings dry and toss with baking powder, salt, garlic powder and black pepper.
Arrange on a rack over a tray and bake at 220 C for 40 to 45 minutes, turning once, until crisp and golden.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce, vinegar and honey and whisk until smooth.
Toss the hot wings in the buffalo sauce until fully coated.
Mash the gorgonzola into the sour cream and mayonnaise with a squeeze of lemon for the dip.
Serve the wings with the dip and celery sticks.

name: Chicken and Chorizo Jambalaya
description: One-pot Louisiana rice loaded with chicken, smoky chorizo, shrimp, peppers and Cajun spice.
instructions: Brown the sliced chorizo in oil in a large pot, then remove; brown the diced chicken thighs in the fat and set aside.
Cook the chopped onion, celery, bell pepper and garlic for 6 minutes until soft.
Stir in the smoked paprika, cayenne, dried thyme, dried oregano and tomato paste, then add the rice and coat in the spices.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and chicken broth, return the chorizo and chicken, add the bay leaf and season.
Cover and simmer gently for 20 minutes until the rice is almost tender, stirring once.
Lay the shrimp on top, cover and cook 5 minutes more, then fluff and serve with green onions.

name: Smash Burgers
description: Thin, crispy-edged beef patties smashed on a hot pan, topped with melted cheese and tangy burger sauce.
instructions: Divide the minced beef into 8 loose balls of about 90 g each without compressing them.
Mix the mayonnaise, ketchup, mustard, finely chopped pickles and a pinch of paprika for the burger sauce.
Heat a cast-iron pan until smoking, add a ball of beef and smash flat with a spatula; season with salt and pepper.
Cook 2 minutes until the edges are crisp, flip, top with a slice of cheese and cook 1 minute more; repeat with the rest.
Toast the buns cut-side down in the pan with a little butter.
Build each burger with sauce, two patties, sliced onion, pickles and lettuce.

name: BBQ Chicken Drumsticks
description: Sticky oven-baked drumsticks in a smoky, sweet homemade barbecue glaze with roasted corn on the cob.
instructions: Season the drumsticks with smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper and rub with oil.
Arrange on a lined tray and bake at 200 C for 25 minutes.
Meanwhile simmer the BBQ sauce, ketchup, honey, apple cider vinegar and Worcestershire sauce for 5 minutes until glossy.
Brush the drumsticks generously with the glaze and return to the oven for 15 minutes, brushing again halfway, until sticky and cooked through.
Wrap the corn cobs in foil with a knob of butter and roast alongside for the final 20 minutes.
Serve the drumsticks with the corn and any remaining glaze.

name: Pasta alla Norma
description: Sicilian rigatoni with golden fried eggplant, garlicky tomato sauce, basil and salty grated ricotta.
instructions: Cut the eggplant into 2 cm cubes, salt generously and leave to drain in a colander for 20 minutes, then pat dry.
Fry the eggplant in batches in 4 tbsp of olive oil until deep golden on all sides; drain on paper towels.
In the same pan, soften the sliced garlic in the remaining oil, add the crushed tomatoes and chili flakes and simmer for 15 minutes.
Cook the rigatoni in salted boiling water until al dente, reserving a cup of the cooking water.
Toss the pasta with the sauce, most of the eggplant and torn basil, loosening with a splash of pasta water.
Serve topped with the remaining eggplant, grated ricotta salata and more basil.

name: Spaghetti alla Puttanesca
description: Bold Neapolitan spaghetti with anchovies, olives, capers and chili melted into a quick tomato sauce.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente.
Meanwhile warm the olive oil in a wide pan and melt the anchovies with the sliced garlic and chili flakes over low heat.
Add the crushed tomatoes, olives and rinsed capers and simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Drain the spaghetti, reserving a little pasta water, and toss it through the sauce for a minute.
Finish with chopped parsley and serve immediately.

name: Bucatini all'Amatriciana
description: Roman bucatini with crisp guanciale, tomato and a snowfall of pecorino, finished with a kick of chili.
instructions: Cut the guanciale into short strips and render it slowly in a dry pan with a teaspoon of oil until golden and crisp.
Lift out the crisp pieces, add the chili flakes to the fat, then pour in the white wine and let it bubble away.
Add the crushed tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes until thick; return the guanciale to the pan.
Cook the bucatini in salted boiling water until al dente and drain, keeping a cup of the water.
Toss the pasta in the sauce with half the pecorino and a splash of pasta water until glossy.
Serve with the remaining pecorino and plenty of black pepper.

name: Pasta Primavera
description: Spring asparagus, zucchini, peas and cherry tomatoes tossed with farfalle in a light lemon-parmesan cream.
instructions: Cook the farfalle in salted boiling water until al dente; add the peas for the last 2 minutes, then drain and reserve a cup of water.
Meanwhile heat the olive oil in a large pan and sauté the sliced asparagus and diced zucchini for 4 minutes.
Add the garlic and halved cherry tomatoes and cook for 2 more minutes until the tomatoes just soften.
Pour in the cream, lemon zest and juice, and let it bubble briefly.
Toss in the pasta and peas with the parmesan, loosening with pasta water, and season.
Scatter with torn basil and serve.

name: Tuna Pasta Bake
description: Family-friendly penne baked with tuna, sweetcorn and tomato under a bubbling cheddar and mozzarella crust.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C and cook the penne in salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet says; drain.
Soften the chopped onion in olive oil, add the garlic and oregano, then pour in the crushed tomatoes and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the drained tuna and sweetcorn, season, and fold in the pasta and half the cheddar.
Tip into a baking dish, top with the remaining cheddar and torn mozzarella.
Bake for 20-25 minutes until golden and bubbling, and rest for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Spinach and Ricotta Cannelloni
description: Pasta rolls filled with creamy spinach and ricotta, baked in passata with melted mozzarella and parmesan.
instructions: Wilt the spinach in a large pan with the garlic and a little olive oil, cool, then squeeze out all the liquid and chop.
Mix the spinach with the ricotta, egg, half the parmesan, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Season the passata with torn basil, salt and a drizzle of olive oil, and spread a third over the base of a baking dish.
Blanch the lasagne sheets briefly if dried, then spread filling along each sheet and roll into a tube; lay seam-side down in the dish.
Cover with the remaining passata, torn mozzarella and parmesan.
Bake at 190°C for 35-40 minutes until golden; rest 10 minutes before serving.

ingredients.name: Lasagne sheets, for rolling into cannelloni

name: Gnocchi with Sage Butter
description: Pillowy gnocchi in nutty brown butter with crisp sage leaves, lemon and shaved parmesan, ready in 15 minutes.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil for the gnocchi.
Melt the butter in a wide pan over medium heat with the whole garlic clove and the sage leaves.
Cook until the butter foams, smells nutty and turns light brown and the sage is crisp, then take off the heat and discard the garlic.
Drop the gnocchi into the boiling water and lift them out with a slotted spoon as soon as they float.
Toss the gnocchi in the sage butter with a squeeze of lemon and a spoonful of cooking water.
Serve with grated parmesan and black pepper.

name: Gnocchi al Pomodoro
description: Soft potato gnocchi in a sweet, slow-simmered tomato and basil sauce with melting pockets of mozzarella.
instructions: Soften the finely chopped onion in olive oil over low heat for 8 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Pour in the passata, add a pinch of sugar and salt, and simmer gently for 15 minutes with a few basil leaves.
Cook the gnocchi in salted boiling water until they float, then lift them straight into the sauce.
Fold through the torn mozzarella and remaining basil so the cheese just begins to melt.
Serve with grated parmesan.

name: Pesto Gnocchi with Green Beans
description: Gnocchi and crisp-tender green beans coated in basil pesto with blistered cherry tomatoes and toasted pine nuts.
instructions: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan until golden and set aside.
Boil the trimmed green beans in salted water for 4 minutes, then add the gnocchi and cook until they float; drain, keeping a little water.
Meanwhile sear the cherry tomatoes in olive oil in a large pan until they blister and split.
Add the gnocchi and beans to the pan, take off the heat and stir in the pesto with a splash of cooking water.
Serve with pine nuts, grated parmesan and black pepper.

name: Orecchiette with Sausage and Broccoli
description: Puglian-style orecchiette with crumbled pork sausage, tender broccoli, garlic, chili and pecorino.
instructions: Cut the broccoli into small florets and boil in salted water for 4 minutes; lift out and keep the water for the pasta.
Cook the orecchiette in the same water until al dente.
Meanwhile squeeze the sausage meat from its casings and brown it in olive oil, breaking it into crumbs.
Add the sliced garlic and chili flakes, pour in the wine and let it reduce by half.
Add the broccoli and crush it slightly into the sauce, then toss in the drained pasta with a splash of water.
Finish with grated cheese and serve.

name: Lemon Ricotta Pasta
description: Silky no-cook sauce of ricotta, lemon zest and parmesan tossed with hot spaghetti and torn basil.
instructions: Cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water until al dente, reserving a cup of the water.
Meanwhile whisk the ricotta in a large bowl with the lemon zest, lemon juice, grated garlic, parmesan, olive oil and black pepper.
Loosen the ricotta with a few spoonfuls of hot pasta water until it is creamy and pourable.
Add the drained spaghetti to the bowl and toss well, adding more water as needed to coat every strand.
Serve with torn basil, extra parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Creamy Mushroom Tagliatelle
description: Ribbons of tagliatelle in a thyme-scented cream sauce with golden chestnut and button mushrooms.
instructions: Slice the mushrooms and fry them in batches in butter over high heat until golden; set aside.
In the same pan soften the chopped shallots, add the garlic and thyme leaves, then deglaze with the white wine.
Return the mushrooms, pour in the cream and simmer for 3 minutes; season well.
Cook the tagliatelle in salted boiling water until al dente and drain, keeping a cup of water.
Toss the pasta in the sauce with the parmesan, loosening with pasta water.
Scatter with chopped parsley and serve.

name: Pasta e Fagioli
description: Hearty Italian one-pot of small pasta and cannellini beans in a rosemary tomato broth with pancetta.
instructions: Fry the diced pancetta in olive oil until golden, then add the chopped onion, carrot and celery and soften for 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and rosemary, then add the crushed tomatoes and broth and bring to a simmer.
Add the drained beans and simmer for 15 minutes; mash a ladleful against the side of the pot to thicken.
Add the pasta directly to the pot and cook until al dente, adding water if it gets too thick.
Season, rest for 5 minutes and serve with grated parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Orzo with Roasted Vegetables and Feta
description: Rice-shaped orzo tossed with oven-roasted peppers, zucchini and tomatoes, crumbled feta and lemon.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C; toss the chopped zucchini, peppers, red onion, cherry tomatoes and garlic with 3 tbsp oil, oregano and salt.
Roast on a large tray for 25-30 minutes until charred at the edges.
Cook the orzo in salted boiling water until al dente, drain and toss with the remaining oil.
Fold the roasted vegetables and their juices through the orzo with the lemon zest and juice.
Crumble over the feta, scatter with basil and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Macaroane cu Brânză (Sweet Baked Pasta with Cheese)
description: Romanian comfort classic: macaroni baked with sweetened cottage cheese, eggs, raisins and lemon zest.
instructions: Cook the macaroni in salted water until just tender, drain and toss with half the butter.
Beat the eggs with the sugar, vanilla sugar, lemon zest and a pinch of salt, then mix in the cottage cheese and sour cream.
Fold the cheese mixture and raisins through the warm macaroni.
Butter a baking dish, dust with breadcrumbs and spread the pasta mixture evenly; dot with the remaining butter.
Bake at 180°C for 40-45 minutes until set and golden on top.
Cool for 10 minutes, cut into squares and serve warm, dusted with sugar if you like.

name: Tăiței cu Nucă (Noodles with Walnuts)
description: Buttered egg noodles tossed with ground walnuts, sugar and lemon zest — a nostalgic Romanian sweet supper.
instructions: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes, cool, then grind coarsely and mix with the sugar, vanilla sugar and lemon zest.
Cook the noodles in lightly salted boiling water until tender and drain well.
Return the noodles to the pot with the butter and toss until glossy.
Add two-thirds of the walnut mixture and toss to coat.
Serve warm, sprinkled with the remaining walnut sugar.

name: Penne alla Vodka
description: Penne in a blush-pink sauce of tomato paste, cream and a splash of vodka, with chili and parmesan.
instructions: Soften the finely chopped onion in the butter and olive oil over low heat for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and chili flakes.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 3 minutes until it darkens to brick red.
Pour in the vodka and let it bubble for 2 minutes, then add the cream and simmer gently.
Cook the penne in salted boiling water until al dente, reserving a cup of the water.
Toss the pasta in the sauce with the parmesan and enough pasta water to make it glossy.
Serve with torn basil and extra parmesan.

name: Fettuccine Alfredo
description: Rich, glossy fettuccine coated in butter, cream and a generous mountain of parmesan with a hint of nutmeg.
instructions: Cook the fettuccine in salted boiling water until al dente, reserving a cup of the water.
Meanwhile melt the butter in a wide pan with the crushed garlic clove, pour in the cream and simmer for 3 minutes; discard the garlic.
Take the pan off the heat and whisk in the parmesan a handful at a time until smooth.
Add the drained pasta and toss, adding pasta water until the sauce coats every strand.
Season with nutmeg, black pepper and salt, scatter with parsley and serve at once.

name: Linguine with Mussels
description: Linguine tossed with mussels steamed open in white wine, garlic, chili and burst cherry tomatoes.
instructions: Scrub the mussels, pull off the beards and discard any that stay open when tapped.
Heat the olive oil in a very large pan and sizzle the sliced garlic and chili flakes for 1 minute, then add the halved cherry tomatoes.
Pour in the wine, add the mussels, cover and steam for 4-5 minutes until they open; discard any that remain shut.
Cook the linguine in salted boiling water until al dente and drain, keeping a cup of the water.
Toss the linguine through the mussels and their juices with chopped parsley and lemon zest, adding pasta water if needed.
Serve with lemon wedges.

name: Pappardelle with Slow-Cooked Beef Ragù
description: Wide pappardelle with beef braised for hours in red wine and tomato until it falls into shreds.
instructions: Season the beef cubes and brown them in batches in olive oil in a heavy casserole; set aside.
Soften the finely chopped onion, carrot and celery in the same pot for 10 minutes, then add the garlic.
Return the beef, pour in the red wine and reduce by half, then add the crushed tomatoes, broth and bay leaves.
Cover and simmer very gently on the hob or in a 160°C oven for 2.5-3 hours until the beef shreds easily.
Shred the meat into the sauce with two forks, season and simmer uncovered to thicken if needed.
Cook the pappardelle until al dente, toss with the ragù and serve with grated parmesan.

name: Salmon and Dill Tagliatelle
description: Flaked pan-seared salmon folded into a lemony dill cream with peas and tagliatelle.
instructions: Season the salmon and sear skin-side down in butter for 4 minutes, turn and cook 2 more minutes; set aside and flake, discarding the skin.
Soften the chopped shallots in the same pan, pour in the wine and reduce by half.
Add the cream, peas and lemon zest and simmer for 3 minutes.
Cook the tagliatelle in salted boiling water until al dente and drain, keeping a little water.
Toss the pasta in the sauce with the flaked salmon, chopped dill and a squeeze of lemon; season and serve.

name: Spaghetti and Meatballs
description: Juicy parmesan-laced meatballs simmered in a basil tomato sauce and piled onto spaghetti.
instructions: Mix the minced meat with the breadcrumbs, egg, half the grated onion, 1 grated garlic clove, half the parmesan, salt and pepper; shape into 16 meatballs.
Brown the meatballs in olive oil in a wide pan on all sides, then remove.
Soften the remaining onion and garlic in the pan, add the crushed tomatoes and oregano and simmer for 10 minutes.
Return the meatballs to the sauce, cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
Cook the spaghetti until al dente, toss with some of the sauce and top with meatballs, basil and the remaining parmesan.

name: Spaghetti with Zucchini, Lemon and Mint
description: Summery spaghetti with soft golden zucchini coins, garlic, lemon zest, fresh mint and parmesan.
instructions: Slice the zucchini into thin coins and fry in the olive oil over medium-high heat until golden and soft, about 10 minutes.
Add the sliced garlic for the last minute and season with salt.
Cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water until al dente, reserving a cup of the water.
Toss the pasta into the zucchini with the lemon zest, lemon juice, parmesan and a splash of water, mashing some zucchini into a sauce.
Finish with torn mint and black pepper.

name: Sesame Peanut Noodles
description: Chilled egg noodles in a creamy peanut-sesame dressing with cucumber, spring onions and toasted sesame.
instructions: Cook the noodles according to the packet, rinse under cold water and drain well.
Whisk the peanut butter with the soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, honey, grated garlic, grated ginger and hot sauce, adding warm water until pourable.
Cut the cucumber into matchsticks and slice the spring onions.
Toss the noodles with the dressing, most of the cucumber and spring onions.
Serve topped with the remaining vegetables and toasted sesame seeds.

name: Singapore Noodles
description: Curry-spiced rice vermicelli stir-fried with shrimp, ham, egg, peppers and bean sprouts.
instructions: Soak the rice vermicelli in hot water until just pliable, drain and snip into shorter lengths.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok, scramble the beaten eggs, break into pieces and set aside.
Stir-fry the shrimp for 2 minutes until pink, then remove.
Add the remaining oil, the garlic, sliced pepper and ham strips and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the noodles, curry powder, turmeric and soy sauce and toss until evenly yellow and hot.
Return the eggs and shrimp with the bean sprouts and spring onions, toss for 1 minute and serve.

name: Beef Udon Stir-Fry
description: Chewy udon noodles tossed with seared sliced beef, bok choy and a glossy soy-oyster sauce.
instructions: Cook the udon according to the packet, rinse briefly and drain.
Mix the soy sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Heat the oil in a wok until smoking and sear the thinly sliced beef in two batches for 1-2 minutes; remove.
Stir-fry the garlic, ginger and halved bok choy for 2 minutes until the greens wilt.
Add the noodles, beef and sauce and toss over high heat for 2 minutes until everything is coated.
Top with sliced spring onions and sesame seeds.

name: Mushroom Risotto
description: Creamy arborio risotto stirred with golden sautéed mushrooms, white wine, butter and parmesan.
instructions: Fry the sliced mushrooms in half the butter and the olive oil over high heat until golden; season and set aside.
Keep the broth at a gentle simmer in a separate pan.
Soften the finely chopped onion and garlic in the remaining olive oil, add the rice and toast for 2 minutes until the edges turn translucent.
Pour in the wine and stir until absorbed, then add hot broth a ladle at a time, stirring, waiting for each to be absorbed.
After about 18 minutes, when the rice is creamy but still has bite, stir in the mushrooms.
Take off the heat and beat in the remaining butter and parmesan; rest 2 minutes, then serve with parsley.

name: Pumpkin and Sage Risotto
description: Golden autumn risotto with sweet roasted pumpkin, crispy sage leaves and a whisper of nutmeg.
instructions: Toss the diced pumpkin with 1 tbsp olive oil and salt and roast at 200°C for 25 minutes until soft and caramelised.
Fry the sage leaves in half the butter until crisp and set aside on paper.
Soften the chopped onion and garlic in the remaining oil, add the rice and toast for 2 minutes.
Add the wine, then hot broth one ladle at a time, stirring until each is absorbed, for about 18 minutes.
Mash half the pumpkin into the risotto and fold in the rest with the nutmeg.
Off the heat beat in the remaining butter and parmesan, then serve topped with crispy sage.

name: Risotto alla Milanese
description: The Milanese classic: saffron-gold risotto finished with plenty of butter and parmesan.
instructions: Steep the saffron in a ladle of hot broth for 10 minutes; keep the rest of the broth simmering.
Soften the very finely chopped onion in half the butter and the olive oil without colouring.
Add the rice and toast for 2 minutes, then pour in the wine and stir until absorbed.
Add hot broth a ladle at a time, stirring, until the rice is creamy with a slight bite, about 18 minutes; add the saffron broth halfway.
Off the heat beat in the remaining cold butter and parmesan vigorously until glossy.
Season, rest for 2 minutes and serve.

name: Seafood Risotto
description: Risotto ai frutti di mare with shrimp, squid and mussels, white wine, cherry tomatoes and parsley.
instructions: Clean the mussels and slice the squid into rings; keep the broth simmering.
Heat half the oil in a wide pan, add the mussels and a splash of wine, cover until they open, then remove and shell most of them, keeping the liquid.
Soften the shallots and garlic in the remaining oil, add the rice and toast for 2 minutes, then add the rest of the wine.
Add the mussel liquid and hot broth a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 15 minutes.
Stir in the squid, shrimp and halved cherry tomatoes and cook 3-4 minutes more until the seafood is just done.
Fold in the mussels, parsley, lemon zest and a drizzle of oil; season and serve.

name: Pea and Mint Risotto
description: Bright green risotto with sweet peas, fresh mint and lemon, finished with butter and parmesan.
instructions: Blend a third of the peas with a ladle of hot broth and half the mint into a smooth purée.
Soften the chopped onion and garlic in olive oil, add the rice and toast for 2 minutes.
Add the wine and stir until absorbed, then add hot broth a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 15 minutes.
Stir in the whole peas and the pea purée and cook for 3 more minutes.
Off the heat beat in the butter, parmesan, lemon zest and the remaining chopped mint.
Season and serve with a squeeze of lemon.

name: Pilaf cu Legume (Romanian Vegetable Pilaf)
description: Fluffy Romanian rice pilaf with carrots, peppers, peas and a touch of tomato, finished with fresh dill.
instructions: Soften the finely chopped onion in sunflower oil over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add the grated carrots and diced pepper and cook for 5 more minutes, then stir in the garlic and tomato paste.
Add the rinsed rice and stir for 2 minutes until coated and glossy.
Pour in the hot broth, add the peas and salt, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 18 minutes.
Take off the heat and let it stand covered for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and fold in the chopped dill and parsley.

name: Pilaf cu Pui (Romanian Chicken Pilaf)
description: Homestyle Romanian pilaf: browned chicken thighs cooked into rice with onion, carrot, pepper and parsley.
instructions: Season the chicken thighs and brown them in sunflower oil in a deep pan until golden on both sides; set aside.
Soften the chopped onion, grated carrot and diced pepper in the same pan for 8 minutes, then add the garlic.
Stir in the rinsed rice and toast for 2 minutes.
Nestle the chicken into the rice, pour in the hot broth, add the bay leaf, salt and pepper and bring to a boil.
Cover and cook on very low heat for 20 minutes, or transfer to a 180°C oven, until the rice is tender and the chicken cooked through.
Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff and scatter with parsley.

name: Paella Mixta (Chicken and Seafood Paella)
description: Saffron-scented Spanish rice with chicken thighs, shrimp, mussels, peppers and peas, crisp at the base.
instructions: Steep the saffron in a little hot broth; keep the rest of the broth hot.
Brown the seasoned chicken thighs in olive oil in a wide shallow pan for 8 minutes, then push to the edges.
Fry the diced pepper, then add the garlic, grated tomatoes and smoked paprika and cook to a thick sofrito.
Stir in the rice to coat, pour in the hot broth with the saffron, spread everything evenly and do not stir again.
Simmer briskly for 10 minutes, then lower the heat, add the peas, shrimp and mussels and cook 8-10 minutes more until the liquid is absorbed.
Raise the heat for 1 minute to crisp the base, cover with a cloth and rest for 5 minutes before serving.

name: Spanish Chicken and Rice (Arroz con Pollo)
description: One-pan chicken thighs and chorizo baked into smoky paprika rice with peppers, tomato and peas.
instructions: Season the chicken thighs and brown them skin-side down in olive oil in a large ovenproof pan; set aside.
Fry the sliced chorizo until it releases its oil, then add the chopped onion and pepper and soften for 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and smoked paprika, then the crushed tomatoes and the rice, stirring to coat.
Pour in the hot broth, season, and nestle the chicken on top.
Cover and simmer gently, or bake at 180°C, for 25 minutes; scatter the peas over for the final 5 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve from the pan.

name: Spanakorizo (Greek Spinach Rice)
description: Greek one-pot rice simmered with heaps of spinach, dill, spring onions and lemon, served with feta.
instructions: Soften the chopped onion and spring onions in the olive oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic.
Add the spinach in handfuls, letting each wilt before adding more.
Stir in the rinsed rice, pour in the hot broth and season with salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer gently for 18-20 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed.
Stir in the chopped dill, lemon zest and juice and let stand covered for 5 minutes.
Serve warm with crumbled feta and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Kedgeree
description: Anglo-Indian curried basmati with flaked smoked mackerel, soft-boiled eggs, peas, parsley and lemon.
instructions: Rinse the basmati and cook in salted water until just tender; drain and keep warm.
Boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool in cold water, peel and quarter.
Melt the butter in a large pan and soften the chopped onion for 8 minutes, then stir in the curry powder and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the rice and peas and toss until coated and hot.
Fold in the flaked smoked mackerel, most of the parsley and the lemon juice; season well.
Top with the eggs and remaining parsley and serve with lemon wedges.

name: Caribbean Coconut Rice and Beans
description: Fragrant rice cooked in coconut milk with kidney beans, thyme, allspice, spring onion and a whole chili.
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and drain the beans.
Put the rice, beans, coconut milk, water, sliced spring onions, crushed garlic, thyme sprigs, allspice and salt in a pot.
Add the whole chili without cutting it, and bring to a boil.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Rest off the heat for 10 minutes, remove the chili and thyme stalks and fluff with a fork.

name: Mujadara (Lentils and Rice with Crispy Onions)
description: Levantine comfort food of cumin-spiced lentils and rice heaped with sweet, deeply caramelised onions.
instructions: Thinly slice the onions and fry slowly in the olive oil for 25-30 minutes, stirring, until deep brown and crisp at the edges; drain on paper.
Meanwhile simmer the lentils in the water for 15 minutes until almost tender.
Add the rinsed rice, cumin, cinnamon, salt, pepper and a spoonful of the onion oil to the lentils.
Cover and cook on low heat for 18 minutes until the rice is tender and the water absorbed; rest 10 minutes.
Fold half the onions through, pile the rest on top and serve with yogurt and parsley.

name: Turkish Bulgur Pilaf
description: Nutty coarse bulgur cooked with onion, pepper and tomato paste in butter, finished with parsley and mint.
instructions: Melt the butter with the olive oil and soften the finely chopped onion and diced pepper for 6 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and paprika and cook for 1 minute, then add the chopped tomato.
Add the bulgur and stir for 2 minutes to coat the grains.
Pour in the hot broth, season with salt, bring to a boil, cover and cook on low heat for 12-15 minutes.
Rest off the heat, covered with a tea towel under the lid, for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and fold through the chopped parsley and mint.

name: Couscous with Roasted Vegetables and Chickpeas
description: Fluffy couscous piled with cumin-roasted peppers, eggplant, zucchini and chickpeas, with harissa and lemon.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C and cut the zucchini, eggplant, peppers and red onion into 3 cm chunks.
Toss the vegetables and drained chickpeas with 3 tbsp olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika and salt, and roast for 30 minutes, turning once.
Put the couscous in a bowl with the remaining oil and a pinch of salt, pour over 350 ml boiling water, cover and leave for 5 minutes.
Fluff the couscous with a fork and stir in the lemon zest and juice.
Pile the roasted vegetables over the couscous, dot with harissa and scatter with chopped coriander.

name: Mediterranean Quinoa Bowl
description: Lemony quinoa topped with chickpeas, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, avocado, feta and toasted pumpkin seeds.
instructions: Rinse the quinoa, then simmer it in 500 ml salted water for 15 minutes until the germ spirals out; rest covered for 5 minutes and fluff.
Whisk the lemon juice and zest with the olive oil and salt, and toss half of it through the warm quinoa.
Halve the cherry tomatoes, dice the cucumber and avocado, and thinly slice the red onion.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
Divide the quinoa between bowls and arrange the vegetables, drained chickpeas and crumbled feta on top.
Drizzle with the remaining dressing and scatter with parsley and pumpkin seeds.

name: Hrișcă cu Ciuperci (Buckwheat with Mushrooms)
description: Toasted buckwheat groats simmered in broth and folded with buttery mushrooms, onions and sour cream.
instructions: Toast the rinsed buckwheat in a dry pot for 3 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the hot broth, add salt, cover and simmer on low heat for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed; rest 5 minutes.
Meanwhile fry the sliced onions in the oil and half the butter for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the sliced mushrooms and cook over high heat until browned, then add the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.
Fold the mushrooms into the buckwheat with the remaining butter and the sour cream; season.
Serve scattered with chopped parsley.

name: Mămăligă with Mushroom Ragout
description: Soft Romanian polenta topped with a garlicky mushroom and dill ragout, sour cream and crumbled telemea.
instructions: Bring the water to a boil with the salt, rain in the cornmeal while whisking and cook on low heat, stirring often, for 25-30 minutes until thick and pulling from the sides.
Beat half the butter into the mămăligă and keep warm.
Fry the chopped onion in the oil and remaining butter for 5 minutes, then add the sliced mushrooms and cook over high heat until golden.
Add the crushed garlic, season, and stir in 2 tbsp of the sour cream and the chopped dill.
Spoon the mămăligă into bowls, top with the mushroom ragout, the rest of the sour cream and crumbled telemea.

name: Cajun Dirty Rice
description: Louisiana rice cooked with spiced pork, chicken livers, celery, green pepper and onion.
instructions: Finely chop the chicken livers and brown them with the minced pork in a little oil, breaking up the meat, for 6 minutes.
Add the chopped onion, celery and green pepper and cook for 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic.
Stir in the cayenne, smoked paprika, thyme and salt, then add the rinsed rice and coat in the spiced fat.
Pour in the hot broth, bring to a boil, cover and cook on the lowest heat for 18 minutes.
Rest for 10 minutes, fluff with a fork and stir through the sliced spring onions.

name: Salată de Boeuf
description: Romania's festive salad of diced beef, root vegetables, pickles and peas bound in creamy mustard mayonnaise.
instructions: Simmer the beef in salted water for about 1 hour until tender, then cool and dice finely.
Boil the potatoes, carrots and parsnip in their skins until just tender; cool, peel and dice small.
Hard-boil the eggs, cool and chop two of them, keeping one for decoration.
Dice the pickles and drain the peas, then combine everything in a large bowl.
Stir the mustard into the mayonnaise and fold it gently through the salad; season with salt and pepper.
Smooth the top, decorate with sliced egg and strips of pickled pepper, and chill for at least 2 hours before serving.

name: Salată Orientală
description: Rustic Romanian potato salad with boiled eggs, red onion, black olives and pickles in a simple oil and vinegar dressing.
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until tender, about 20 minutes; cool slightly, peel and slice into thick rounds.
Hard-boil the eggs, cool them in cold water, then peel and cut into wedges.
Slice the red onion thinly and the pickles into rounds.
Layer the potatoes, onion, pickles, olives and eggs in a wide bowl.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, salt and pepper and pour over the salad while the potatoes are still warm.
Scatter with chopped parsley and let stand 15 minutes before serving.

name: Salată de Vinete
description: Smoky Romanian roasted eggplant salad whipped with sunflower oil and finely chopped onion, perfect on fresh bread.
instructions: Prick the eggplants and roast them on a grill pan, gas flame or under a hot broiler, turning, until the skin is charred and the flesh collapses, about 30 minutes.
Let them cool slightly, peel away the skin and leave the flesh in a colander for 30 minutes to drain the bitter juices.
Chop the eggplant very finely with a wooden or plastic knife until almost a paste.
Beat in the oil gradually with a wooden spoon until the mixture becomes pale and creamy.
Stir in the finely chopped onion and season with salt and a little lemon juice.
Chill for 1 hour and serve with sliced tomatoes and fresh bread.

name: Salată de Icre
description: Silky Romanian fish roe spread emulsified with oil and brightened with lemon and finely chopped onion.
instructions: Soak the bread in a little water, squeeze dry and mash into a paste in a bowl.
Add the roe and beat with a wooden spoon or hand mixer for 2 minutes until smooth.
Pour in the oil in a very thin stream while beating constantly, as for mayonnaise, until thick and pale.
Beat in the lemon juice a teaspoon at a time to lighten the mixture.
Fold in the finely chopped onion and season lightly with salt if needed.
Chill for 1 hour and serve on bread or toast, garnished with black olives.

name: Salată de Varză
description: Crunchy Romanian white cabbage salad massaged with salt and tossed with dill, oil and a splash of vinegar.
instructions: Remove the outer leaves and core of the cabbage and shred it as finely as possible.
Sprinkle with salt and massage firmly with your hands for 2 to 3 minutes until the cabbage softens and releases juice.
Grate the carrot and add it with the chopped dill.
Dress with the oil, vinegar and a pinch of pepper and toss well.
Rest for 15 minutes before serving alongside grilled meats or stews.

name: Salată de Sfeclă cu Hrean
description: Earthy boiled beetroot grated with fiery fresh horseradish and sharpened with vinegar, a classic Romanian side.
instructions: Scrub the beetroots and boil them whole in their skins for 45 to 60 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Drain, cool under running water and rub off the skins.
Coarsely grate the beetroot into a bowl and finely grate the peeled horseradish over it.
Season with salt, sugar and vinegar, then stir in the oil and caraway seeds if using.
Pack into a jar or bowl and refrigerate at least 2 hours; the flavour improves overnight.

name: Salată de Ardei Copți
description: Sweet charred kapia peppers peeled and marinated in garlicky oil and vinegar, served cool with crusty bread.
instructions: Roast the whole peppers on a grill pan or under a hot broiler, turning until blistered and blackened all over, about 20 minutes.
Pile the hot peppers in a bowl, sprinkle with salt, cover tightly and let steam for 15 minutes.
Peel off the skins, pull out the stems and seeds, and leave the peppers whole or tear into wide strips.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, crushed garlic, salt and a pinch of sugar and pour over the peppers.
Scatter with parsley and marinate for at least 1 hour before serving.

name: Salată de Fasole cu Ceapă
description: Hearty Romanian white bean salad with sweet softened onions, garlic and a tangy vinegar dressing.
instructions: Soak the beans overnight, then simmer in fresh water with a bay leaf for 60 to 90 minutes until tender; drain and cool.
Slice the onions thinly and soften them in 2 tablespoons of oil over low heat for 8 minutes without browning.
Combine the beans with the warm onions, crushed garlic and the remaining oil.
Season with vinegar, salt and pepper and toss gently to avoid breaking the beans.
Sprinkle with sweet paprika and chopped parsley and serve at room temperature.

name: Salată de Roșii cu Ceapă și Telemea
description: Juicy summer tomatoes and thin red onion rings topped with crumbled telemea cheese and good oil.
instructions: Cut the tomatoes into thick wedges and arrange on a platter.
Slice the red onion into thin rings and scatter over the tomatoes.
Season with salt and pepper and drizzle with oil and vinegar.
Crumble the telemea over the top and finish with chopped parsley.
Serve immediately with bread to mop up the juices.

name: Salată de Castraveți cu Smântână
description: Cool sliced cucumbers folded into sour cream with dill and garlic, a refreshing Romanian summer side.
instructions: Peel the cucumbers in stripes and slice them very thinly.
Toss with salt in a colander and leave 15 minutes, then squeeze out the excess water.
Mix the sour cream with the crushed garlic, chopped dill, vinegar and pepper.
Fold the cucumbers into the dressing and taste for salt.
Chill for 20 minutes and serve cold.

name: Salată de Țelină cu Mere
description: Crisp grated celery root and tart apple in a light lemony mayonnaise with toasted walnuts.
instructions: Peel the celery root and apples and grate both coarsely into a bowl.
Immediately toss with the lemon juice to prevent browning.
Stir the mayonnaise and yogurt together and fold through the celery and apple.
Season with salt and pepper and stir in most of the chopped walnuts.
Chill for 30 minutes and top with the remaining walnuts before serving.

name: Salată de Ciuperci cu Maioneză
description: Sautéed mushrooms cooled and folded with garlic mayonnaise and dill, a beloved Romanian party salad.
instructions: Clean the mushrooms and slice them thickly.
Heat the oil in a large pan and sauté the mushrooms over high heat until golden and their liquid has evaporated, about 10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and let cool completely.
Mix the mayonnaise with the crushed garlic, lemon juice and chopped dill.
Fold the mushrooms through the dressing, chill for 1 hour and serve with bread.

name: Salată de Varză Roșie cu Mere
description: Vibrant shredded red cabbage with sweet apple, honey and apple cider vinegar for a crunchy winter salad.
instructions: Shred the red cabbage very finely and place in a large bowl with the salt.
Massage the cabbage for 2 minutes until it softens slightly and turns glossy.
Core the apple and cut into thin matchsticks; add to the cabbage.
Whisk the vinegar, honey, oil and pepper and pour over the salad.
Toss well, stir in the parsley and let marinate for 20 minutes before serving.

name: Salată de Ridichi cu Ceapă Verde
description: Peppery spring radishes and green onions tossed with lemon and oil, served over crisp lettuce leaves.
instructions: Trim and thinly slice the radishes and chop the green onions.
Tear the lettuce into bite-size pieces and arrange on a platter.
Toss the radishes and green onions with the lemon juice, oil, salt and pepper.
Spoon over the lettuce and finish with chopped parsley.
Serve immediately while the radishes are crisp.

name: Shopska Salad
description: Bulgarian chopped salad of tomatoes, cucumber, peppers and onion buried under a snowdrift of grated brined cheese.
instructions: Roast the pepper under a broiler until charred, peel and chop; or simply dice it raw for a crunchier salad.
Dice the tomatoes and cucumber into 2 cm pieces and finely chop the onion.
Combine the vegetables with the chopped parsley in a bowl.
Dress with oil, vinegar, salt and pepper and toss gently.
Pile onto plates and grate a thick layer of telemea or feta over the top just before serving.

name: Vinegret
description: Russian beetroot salad with diced potatoes, carrots, pickles, sauerkraut and peas in a bright sunflower dressing.
instructions: Boil the beetroots, potatoes and carrots separately in their skins until tender; cool and peel.
Dice all the vegetables into small, even cubes and place the beetroot in a separate bowl.
Toss the beetroot with 1 tablespoon of oil so it does not stain the other vegetables.
Combine the potatoes, carrots, diced pickles, drained sauerkraut, peas and finely chopped onion.
Add the beetroot, dress with the remaining oil, vinegar, salt and pepper and mix gently.
Chill for 1 hour and sprinkle with dill before serving.

name: Greek Salad (Horiatiki)
description: Chunky tomatoes, cucumber, red onion and kalamata olives crowned with a slab of feta and oregano.
instructions: Cut the tomatoes into wedges and the cucumber into thick half-moons.
Slice the red onion and bell pepper into thin rings.
Toss the vegetables with the olives, olive oil, red wine vinegar, salt and pepper.
Lay the feta on top in one piece or large chunks and sprinkle generously with oregano.
Drizzle a little more oil over the feta and serve with crusty bread.

name: Chicken Caesar Salad
description: Crisp romaine, golden croutons and grilled chicken in a garlicky anchovy-parmesan dressing.
instructions: Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper, brush with a little oil and grill or pan-fry for 6 minutes per side; rest and slice.
Mash the anchovies and garlic to a paste, then whisk in the egg yolk, mustard and lemon juice.
Slowly whisk in the olive oil until creamy, then stir in half the grated parmesan.
Tear the romaine into a large bowl and toss with the dressing until every leaf is coated.
Top with the sliced chicken, croutons and remaining parmesan and finish with black pepper.

name: Salade Niçoise
description: Provençal composed salad of tuna, green beans, potatoes, eggs, olives and tomatoes with a mustard vinaigrette.
instructions: Boil the potatoes until tender, about 15 minutes, then slice; cook the green beans in salted water for 4 minutes and cool in iced water.
Hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool, peel and quarter.
Whisk the mustard, red wine vinegar, olive oil, salt and pepper into a vinaigrette.
Arrange the lettuce on a platter and group the potatoes, beans, tomato wedges, eggs and flaked tuna on top.
Scatter with olives, anchovies and capers and spoon the vinaigrette over everything.

name: Waldorf Salad
description: Classic New York salad of crisp apple, celery, grapes and toasted walnuts in a light lemony mayo dressing.
instructions: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes until fragrant, then roughly chop.
Core and dice the apples and toss with the lemon juice to prevent browning.
Slice the celery thinly and halve the grapes.
Stir the mayonnaise and yogurt together and season with salt and pepper.
Fold in the apples, celery, grapes and most of the walnuts.
Serve on lettuce leaves topped with the remaining walnuts.

name: Classic Creamy Coleslaw
description: Finely shredded cabbage and carrot in a sweet-tangy creamy dressing, the perfect partner for burgers and BBQ.
instructions: Quarter and core the cabbage and shred it as thinly as possible; grate the carrots.
Whisk the mayonnaise, yogurt, apple cider vinegar, mustard, sugar, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Add the cabbage and carrot and toss until evenly coated.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes so the cabbage softens slightly.
Toss again and adjust salt and vinegar before serving.

name: Asian Sesame Slaw
description: Crunchy red cabbage, carrot and bean sprouts in a ginger-soy-sesame dressing with toasted sesame seeds.
instructions: Shred the red cabbage finely, cut the carrots into thin matchsticks and slice the green onions.
Whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, honey, grated ginger and lime juice into a dressing.
Toss the cabbage, carrots, bean sprouts and green onions with the dressing.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for 2 minutes until golden.
Let the slaw sit 10 minutes, then top with sesame seeds and chopped coriander.

name: Cucumber Yogurt Salad with Mint
description: Cooling diced cucumber in thick garlicky yogurt with fresh mint and a drizzle of olive oil.
instructions: Dice the cucumbers small, salt them lightly and drain in a colander for 10 minutes.
Stir the yogurt with the crushed garlic, chopped mint, lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Pat the cucumber dry and fold it into the yogurt.
Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with olive oil and dust with sumac or black pepper.
Serve chilled alongside grilled meats or warm pita.

name: Beetroot, Feta and Walnut Salad
description: Sweet roasted beetroot wedges with salty feta, toasted walnuts and peppery arugula in balsamic dressing.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Peel and cut the beetroots into wedges, toss with 1 tablespoon of oil and salt, and roast for 35 to 40 minutes until tender.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes and roughly chop.
Whisk the remaining olive oil with the balsamic vinegar, honey, salt and pepper.
Arrange the arugula on a platter and top with the warm beetroot.
Crumble over the feta, scatter the walnuts and drizzle with the dressing.

name: Roasted Vegetable Salad with Balsamic
description: Caramelised zucchini, peppers, red onion and cherry tomatoes over greens with a balsamic glaze and goat cheese.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C. Cut the zucchini, peppers and red onion into chunks and halve the cherry tomatoes.
Toss the vegetables with the olive oil, dried thyme, salt and pepper and spread on a baking tray.
Roast for 25 minutes, turning once, until edges are golden and caramelised.
Let the vegetables cool for 10 minutes, then pile onto the salad greens.
Crumble over the goat cheese, drizzle with balsamic glaze and scatter with torn basil.

name: Tabbouleh
description: Lebanese herb salad packed with parsley and mint, fine bulgur, tomatoes and plenty of lemon.
instructions: Rinse the bulgur, cover with just-boiled water and let soak for 15 minutes; drain and squeeze dry.
Finely chop the parsley and mint leaves and dice the tomatoes very small, discarding the watery seeds.
Chop the green onions finely.
Combine the herbs, tomatoes, onions and bulgur in a bowl.
Dress with lemon juice, olive oil, salt and pepper, toss well and rest for 10 minutes before serving.

name: Quinoa Salad with Roasted Sweet Potato
description: Fluffy quinoa with caramelised sweet potato cubes, spinach, feta and pumpkin seeds in a lemon-honey dressing.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Dice the sweet potatoes, toss with 1 tablespoon of oil, cumin and salt and roast for 25 minutes.
Rinse the quinoa, cook in 400 ml of water for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed, then fluff and cool.
Whisk the remaining olive oil with the lemon juice, honey, salt and pepper.
Toss the quinoa with the spinach, red onion and dressing.
Fold in the warm sweet potato and top with crumbled feta and pumpkin seeds.

name: Moroccan Couscous Salad
description: Spiced couscous with chickpeas, dried apricots, almonds and fresh herbs, dressed with lemon and olive oil.
instructions: Place the couscous in a bowl with the cumin, cinnamon and a pinch of salt; pour over 300 ml of boiling water, cover and leave 5 minutes.
Fluff the couscous with a fork and drizzle with 1 tablespoon of olive oil.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 3 minutes and chop the apricots into small pieces.
Stir in the drained chickpeas, apricots, almonds, diced cucumber and chopped herbs.
Dress with the remaining olive oil and lemon juice, season and serve at room temperature.

name: Lentil Salad with Feta and Herbs
description: Nutty green lentils with cherry tomatoes, red onion, feta and a sharp mustard vinaigrette.
instructions: Rinse the lentils and simmer in plenty of water with the bay leaf for 20 to 25 minutes until tender but holding their shape; drain.
While still warm, toss the lentils with the red wine vinegar, mustard, olive oil, salt and pepper.
Finely chop the red onion and halve the cherry tomatoes.
Fold the onion, tomatoes and chopped parsley through the lentils.
Top with crumbled feta and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Mediterranean Chickpea Salad
description: Protein-rich chickpeas with cucumber, tomatoes, olives, red onion and parsley in a lemon-garlic dressing.
instructions: Drain and rinse the chickpeas and pat dry.
Dice the cucumber and tomatoes, finely chop the red onion and halve the olives.
Whisk the olive oil, lemon juice, crushed garlic, oregano, salt and pepper.
Combine the chickpeas and vegetables, pour over the dressing and toss.
Stir in the chopped parsley and let marinate 15 minutes before serving.

name: Italian Pasta Salad
description: Fusilli with salami, mozzarella, cherry tomatoes, olives and peppers in a zesty oregano vinaigrette.
instructions: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water until al dente, drain, rinse briefly under cold water and toss with 1 tablespoon of olive oil.
Whisk the remaining olive oil with the red wine vinegar, oregano, crushed garlic, salt and pepper.
Halve the cherry tomatoes, dice the pepper and mozzarella and cut the salami into strips.
Combine the pasta with the tomatoes, pepper, mozzarella, salami, olives and red onion.
Pour over the dressing, toss well and chill for 30 minutes; finish with torn basil.

name: German Potato Salad with Bacon
description: Warm sliced potatoes tossed with crispy bacon, onion and a tangy mustard-vinegar dressing instead of mayo.
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins until just tender, about 20 minutes; peel while warm and slice.
Fry the diced bacon in a pan until crisp, then remove and soften the chopped onion in the fat for 5 minutes.
Add the vinegar, broth, mustard and sugar to the pan and bring to a simmer.
Pour the hot dressing over the warm potatoes and toss gently to coat.
Fold in the bacon and chives, season with salt and pepper and serve warm.

name: Tuna and White Bean Salad
description: Tuscan-style salad of creamy cannellini beans, flaked tuna, red onion and parsley with lemon and olive oil.
instructions: Drain and rinse the beans and drain the tuna.
Slice the red onion paper-thin and soak in cold water for 5 minutes to mellow, then drain.
Combine the beans, flaked tuna, onion, halved cherry tomatoes and chopped parsley.
Dress with olive oil, lemon juice, salt and plenty of black pepper.
Toss gently and serve with crusty bread or over arugula.

name: Egg Salad with Chives
description: Creamy chopped hard-boiled eggs with mayonnaise, mustard, crunchy celery and fresh chives for sandwiches.
instructions: Place the eggs in cold water, bring to a boil and cook for 9 minutes; cool in iced water and peel.
Chop the eggs roughly and finely dice the celery.
Mix the mayonnaise, mustard, lemon juice, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Fold in the eggs, celery and most of the chopped chives.
Chill for 20 minutes and serve on bread or lettuce leaves, topped with remaining chives.

name: Chicken Salad with Grapes and Almonds
description: Tender poached chicken with sweet grapes, celery and toasted almonds in a tarragon-scented creamy dressing.
instructions: Poach the chicken breasts in gently simmering salted water for 15 minutes, cool and dice.
Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 3 minutes until golden.
Halve the grapes and thinly slice the celery.
Mix the mayonnaise, yogurt, lemon juice, chopped tarragon, salt and pepper.
Fold in the chicken, grapes and celery and chill for 30 minutes.
Top with the almonds and serve in lettuce cups or on bread.

name: Cobb Salad
description: The American classic: rows of chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, tomato and blue cheese over lettuce with red wine vinaigrette.
instructions: Season the chicken, pan-fry in 1 tablespoon of oil for 6 minutes per side, rest and dice.
Fry the bacon until crisp and crumble; hard-boil the eggs for 9 minutes, cool and chop.
Whisk the remaining olive oil with the red wine vinegar, mustard, salt and pepper.
Spread the chopped lettuce on a large platter.
Arrange the chicken, bacon, eggs, diced avocado, halved cherry tomatoes and crumbled blue cheese in neat rows on top.
Drizzle with the vinaigrette just before serving and toss at the table.

name: Mexican Black Bean and Corn Salad
description: Zesty black beans and sweetcorn with red pepper, red onion, jalapeño, coriander and lime, great with tortilla chips.
instructions: Drain and rinse the black beans and the corn.
Dice the bell pepper, finely chop the red onion and mince the chili, removing seeds for less heat.
Whisk the lime juice, olive oil, cumin, salt and pepper.
Combine the beans, corn, pepper, onion and chili and toss with the dressing.
Fold in the diced avocado and chopped coriander just before serving with tortilla chips.

name: Thai Rice Noodle Salad with Peanuts
description: Cold rice noodles with crunchy vegetables, herbs and roasted peanuts in a lime, fish sauce and chili dressing.
instructions: Soak or cook the rice noodles according to the pack, rinse under cold water and drain well.
Cut the carrots and cucumber into thin matchsticks and slice the green onions and chili.
Whisk the lime juice, fish sauce, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil, grated ginger and chili into a dressing.
Toss the noodles with the vegetables and dressing until well coated.
Top with chopped roasted peanuts, coriander and mint and serve cold.

name: Spinach and Strawberry Salad with Almonds
description: Tender baby spinach with sweet strawberries, toasted almonds and goat cheese in a honey-balsamic dressing.
instructions: Toast the almonds in a dry pan for 3 minutes until golden and set aside to cool.
Hull and slice the strawberries and thinly slice the red onion.
Whisk the olive oil, balsamic vinegar, honey, mustard, salt and pepper.
Toss the spinach with the dressing in a large bowl.
Top with the strawberries, red onion, crumbled goat cheese and almonds and serve at once.

name: Pear, Gorgonzola and Walnut Salad
description: Sliced ripe pears, creamy gorgonzola and candied-style toasted walnuts over mixed greens with honey vinaigrette.
instructions: Toast the walnuts in a pan with 1 teaspoon of honey for 3 minutes until glossy; cool on baking paper.
Core and thinly slice the pears and toss with a squeeze of lemon.
Whisk the olive oil, remaining honey, lemon juice, mustard, salt and pepper.
Toss the mixed greens with half the dressing and arrange on plates.
Top with the pear slices, crumbled gorgonzola and walnuts and drizzle with the rest of the dressing.

name: Watermelon, Feta and Mint Salad
description: Icy cubes of watermelon with salty feta, fresh mint and a lime and olive oil drizzle, the ultimate summer salad.
instructions: Cut the watermelon into 3 cm cubes, removing any seeds, and chill well.
Slice the red onion paper-thin and soak in the lime juice for 10 minutes.
Arrange the watermelon on a platter and scatter over the onion and crumbled feta.
Drizzle with olive oil and the lime juice from the onion.
Finish with torn mint leaves and a little black pepper and serve immediately.

name: Fattoush
description: Levantine chopped salad with crisp toasted pita shards, radishes, cucumber and tomatoes in a sumac-lemon dressing.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Tear the pita into bite-size pieces, toss with 1 tablespoon of olive oil and bake for 8 minutes until crisp.
Chop the lettuce, dice the cucumber and tomatoes and slice the radishes and green onions.
Whisk the remaining olive oil with the lemon juice, sumac, crushed garlic, salt and pepper.
Toss the vegetables with the chopped parsley and mint and the dressing.
Add the toasted pita just before serving and sprinkle with more sumac.

name: Tropical Fruit Salad
description: Juicy mango, pineapple, kiwi and banana tossed with lime, honey and a scattering of toasted coconut.
instructions: Peel and dice the mango and pineapple into 2 cm chunks.
Peel and slice the kiwis and bananas.
Whisk the lime juice and honey and pour over the fruit; toss gently.
Toast the desiccated coconut in a dry pan for 2 minutes until lightly golden.
Chill the salad for 15 minutes and sprinkle with coconut and torn mint before serving.

name: Berry Fruit Salad with Honey and Lime
description: Strawberries, blueberries, raspberries and grapes glossed with a honey-lime syrup and fresh mint.
instructions: Hull and quarter the strawberries and halve the grapes.
Gently combine all the berries and grapes in a serving bowl.
Whisk the honey with the lime juice and zest until smooth.
Pour the syrup over the fruit and fold very gently so the raspberries stay whole.
Chill for 20 minutes and scatter with chopped mint; serve with yogurt if you like.

name: Brown Rice Salad with Cranberries and Pecans
description: Chewy brown rice with tart dried cranberries, toasted pecans, celery and green onions in an orange vinaigrette.
instructions: Rinse the brown rice and simmer in plenty of salted water for 30 to 35 minutes until tender; drain and cool.
Toast the pecans in a dry pan for 3 minutes and roughly chop.
Whisk the orange juice and zest with the olive oil, apple cider vinegar, honey, salt and pepper.
Combine the rice with the cranberries, sliced celery, chopped green onions and parsley.
Pour over the dressing, toss well and top with the pecans; serve at room temperature.

name: Classic Hummus
description: Silky chickpea and tahini dip brightened with lemon, garlic and a drizzle of olive oil.
instructions: Drain and rinse the chickpeas, reserving a few tablespoons of the liquid.
Blend chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin and salt until smooth.
Add cold water a spoon at a time until the hummus is creamy and fluffy.
Spoon into a bowl, drizzle with olive oil and dust with paprika before serving.

name: Tzatziki
description: Cool Greek yogurt dip with grated cucumber, garlic, dill and lemon for grilled meats and pita.
instructions: Coarsely grate the cucumber, salt it lightly and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Mix the yogurt with crushed garlic, chopped dill, lemon juice and olive oil.
Fold in the drained cucumber and season with salt and pepper.
Chill for at least 30 minutes so the flavours meld before serving.

name: Guacamole
description: Chunky mashed avocado with lime, red onion, tomato, chili and fresh coriander.
instructions: Halve the avocados, remove the stones and scoop the flesh into a bowl.
Mash roughly with a fork, leaving some chunks, and stir in the lime juice.
Finely dice the red onion, tomato and chili and fold them in with chopped coriander.
Season with salt and serve right away with tortilla chips.

name: Pico de Gallo
description: Fresh chopped tomato salsa with onion, chili, coriander and lime, ready in ten minutes.
instructions: Deseed and finely dice the tomatoes, then dice the red onion and chili.
Combine in a bowl with chopped coriander and lime juice.
Season generously with salt and let stand 10 minutes for the juices to release.
Drain off excess liquid if needed and serve with tacos or chips.

name: Basil Pesto
description: Vibrant Genovese-style pesto of fresh basil, toasted pine nuts, parmesan and olive oil.
instructions: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan for 2-3 minutes until golden, then cool.
Blend basil leaves, pine nuts, garlic and parmesan to a coarse paste.
Stream in the olive oil while blending until the pesto is creamy but still textured.
Season with salt and pepper and store under a thin layer of oil in the fridge.

name: Marinara Sauce
description: Simple Italian tomato sauce simmered with garlic, oregano and basil for pasta or pizza.
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a saucepan and gently fry the sliced garlic until fragrant, not browned.
Add the crushed tomatoes, oregano, sugar, salt and pepper and bring to a simmer.
Cook uncovered for 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until thickened.
Tear in the basil leaves, taste for seasoning and serve or cool and store.

name: Béchamel Sauce
description: Smooth French white sauce of butter, flour and milk with a whisper of nutmeg for lasagna and gratins.
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat and whisk in the flour.
Cook the roux for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, without letting it colour.
Gradually whisk in the warm milk until smooth, then simmer 8-10 minutes until thickened.
Season with salt, white pepper and freshly grated nutmeg.

name: Mujdei de Usturoi
description: Punchy Romanian garlic sauce whipped with oil and water, perfect over grilled meats, fish or polenta.
instructions: Peel the garlic and crush it with the salt in a mortar to a smooth paste.
Add the oil a little at a time, stirring vigorously until it emulsifies.
Thin with cold water to a pourable consistency and season with pepper.
Rest 15 minutes so the sharpness mellows, then serve.

name: Fasole Bătută
description: Creamy Romanian white bean purée topped with golden caramelised onions and paprika oil.
instructions: Soak the beans overnight, then simmer with a bay leaf until very soft, about 90 minutes.
Drain, reserving some cooking liquid, and blend the beans with garlic, salt and 3 tbsp oil until smooth.
Thin with cooking liquid as needed and spoon into a serving dish.
Fry the sliced onions in the remaining oil until golden, stir in the paprika and pour over the beans.

name: Sos de Smântână cu Usturoi și Mărar
description: Tangy Romanian sour cream sauce with crushed garlic and fresh dill for grilled meat, fish or potatoes.
instructions: Crush the garlic with a pinch of salt to a fine paste.
Stir the garlic paste into the sour cream with the finely chopped dill.
Add lemon juice, salt and pepper to taste and mix until smooth.
Chill for 20 minutes before serving.

name: Chimichurri
description: Herby Argentinian sauce of parsley, garlic, oregano, chili and red wine vinegar for grilled steak.
instructions: Finely chop the parsley and garlic by hand for the best texture.
Combine in a bowl with oregano, chili flakes, red wine vinegar and salt.
Stir in the olive oil and let the sauce rest for at least 30 minutes.
Spoon generously over grilled meats or roasted vegetables.

name: Garlic Aioli
description: Rich homemade garlic mayonnaise emulsified from egg yolk, mustard, lemon and olive oil.
instructions: Crush the garlic with salt to a paste and whisk with the egg yolk, mustard and lemon juice.
Add the vegetable oil drop by drop at first, whisking constantly, until the mixture thickens.
Continue in a thin stream with the olive oil until thick and glossy.
Adjust with salt and lemon, and chill until needed.

name: Honey Mustard Dressing
description: Sweet and tangy dressing of honey, Dijon mustard and cider vinegar that doubles as a dip for chicken.
instructions: Whisk together the honey, mustard and apple cider vinegar in a small bowl.
Slowly whisk in the olive oil until the dressing is smooth and glossy.
Season with salt and pepper and adjust sweetness to taste.
Store in a jar in the fridge for up to a week; shake before use.

name: Classic Vinaigrette
description: Bright French-style dressing of olive oil, red wine vinegar, shallot and Dijon mustard.
instructions: Finely mince the shallot and soak it in the vinegar with a pinch of salt for 5 minutes.
Whisk in the mustard until combined.
Drizzle in the olive oil while whisking until emulsified.
Season with pepper and toss with salad just before serving.

name: Caesar Dressing
description: Creamy, savoury Caesar dressing with anchovy, garlic, parmesan, lemon and Worcestershire sauce.
instructions: Mash the anchovies and garlic together to a paste.
Whisk the paste into the mayonnaise with lemon juice, mustard and Worcestershire sauce.
Stir in the grated parmesan and season with plenty of black pepper.
Thin with a splash of water if needed and toss with romaine and croutons.

name: Peanut Satay Sauce
description: Creamy Thai-style peanut sauce with coconut milk, soy, lime, ginger and a touch of chili heat.
instructions: Grate the garlic and ginger and warm them in a saucepan with a splash of the coconut milk.
Whisk in the peanut butter, remaining coconut milk, soy sauce, brown sugar and hot sauce.
Simmer gently for 5 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy.
Finish with lime juice and thin with water if needed; serve warm with skewers.

name: Onion Gravy
description: Deep, glossy British onion gravy slow-cooked with butter, thyme, beef stock and Worcestershire sauce.
instructions: Melt the butter and cook the sliced onions over low heat for 20 minutes until soft and caramelised.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually add the beef broth, whisking to avoid lumps, then add thyme and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer 10 minutes until thickened and season with salt and pepper.

name: Cheddar Cheese Sauce
description: Velvety cheese sauce with a mustard kick, ideal over macaroni, broccoli, nachos or baked potatoes.
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan, whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk and simmer until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Remove from the heat and stir in the grated cheese until melted and smooth.
Season with mustard, nutmeg, salt and pepper and serve warm.

name: Cranberry Sauce
description: Glossy sweet-tart cranberry sauce with orange zest and cinnamon, the classic partner for roast turkey.
instructions: Rinse the cranberries and place them in a saucepan with the sugar, orange juice and zest.
Add the water and cinnamon and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and simmer for 10-12 minutes until the berries burst and the sauce thickens.
Cool completely; it will set further as it chills.

name: Creamy Mashed Potatoes (Piure de Cartofi)
description: Fluffy potatoes beaten with warm milk and butter, finished with a whisper of nutmeg.
instructions: Peel the potatoes, cut them into even chunks and place in a pot of cold salted water.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 18-20 minutes until a knife slides in with no resistance.
Meanwhile warm the milk with the butter in a small pan until the butter melts.
Drain the potatoes well and let them steam dry in the pot for a minute.
Mash thoroughly, then beat in the warm milk and butter until smooth and fluffy.
Season with salt, white pepper and a pinch of nutmeg; serve hot.

name: Crispy Roast Potatoes with Rosemary
description: Parboiled, roughed-up potatoes roasted in hot oil until shatteringly crisp with garlic and rosemary.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C and put a roasting tray with the oil inside to heat up.
Peel the potatoes, cut into large chunks and parboil in salted water for 8 minutes.
Drain and shake the colander hard to rough up the edges of each piece.
Carefully tip the potatoes into the hot oil and turn to coat.
Roast for 25 minutes, turn the potatoes, add the garlic cloves and rosemary, then roast 20 minutes more until deep golden.
Season generously with salt and pepper and serve immediately.

name: Baked Paprika Potato Wedges
description: Skin-on wedges tossed in olive oil, paprika and oregano, baked until crisp outside and fluffy inside.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Scrub the potatoes and cut each into 6-8 wedges, leaving the skin on.
Toss the wedges with olive oil, paprika, garlic powder, oregano, salt and pepper until evenly coated.
Spread in a single layer, skin side down where possible.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp at the edges.

name: Hasselback Potatoes
description: Thinly sliced fan potatoes basted with garlic-thyme butter and crowned with crisp Parmesan.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Place each potato between two wooden spoon handles and slice thinly across, stopping before you cut through.
Melt the butter with the olive oil, crushed garlic and thyme leaves.
Set the potatoes in a baking dish, brush with half the butter and season with salt.
Bake for 30 minutes, brush with the remaining butter so it seeps between the slices, and bake 25 minutes more.
Scatter over the Parmesan and bake 5 more minutes until golden and crisp.

name: Potato Dauphinoise
description: Layers of thin potato slices baked slowly in garlic-infused cream under a golden Gruyère crust.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 160°C and butter a deep baking dish.
Peel the potatoes and slice them 3 mm thick with a mandoline or sharp knife.
Bring the cream, milk, crushed garlic, nutmeg, salt and white pepper to a simmer in a wide pan.
Add the potato slices and simmer gently for 10 minutes, stirring now and then so they do not stick.
Transfer to the dish, level the top and scatter over the grated cheese.
Bake for 60-65 minutes until the potatoes are tender and the top is deeply golden; rest 10 minutes before serving.

name: Cartofi Țărănești (Country-Style Potatoes with Smoked Bacon)
description: Romanian pan-fried potatoes with smoky bacon, onion, garlic and sweet paprika, finished with parsley.
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 15 minutes until just tender, then cool, peel and cut into thick slices.
Dice the bacon and fry it in the oil in a large pan over medium heat until the fat renders and it turns golden.
Add the chopped onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the potato slices in a single layer and fry without stirring too often until browned on both sides.
Stir in the crushed garlic and paprika, cook for 1 minute, then season with salt and pepper.
Scatter with chopped parsley and serve hot.

name: Cartofi Natur cu Mărar (Buttered Potatoes with Dill)
description: Simple boiled potatoes tossed in melted butter and a generous handful of fresh dill.
instructions: Peel the potatoes and cut any large ones in half so they are all a similar size.
Cook in boiling salted water for 18-20 minutes until tender, then drain well.
Return the potatoes to the hot pot, add the butter and shake gently to coat.
Scatter over the chopped dill, season with salt and serve warm.

name: Crispy Sweet Potato Fries
description: Oven-baked sweet potato batons dusted with cornstarch and smoked paprika for extra crunch.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C and line two baking trays with baking paper.
Peel the sweet potatoes and cut into 1 cm thick sticks; pat them very dry.
Toss with the cornstarch until lightly coated, then add the oil, smoked paprika, garlic powder and salt.
Spread out in a single layer with space between the fries.
Bake for 15 minutes, flip, and bake 12-15 minutes more until crisp at the edges; cool 5 minutes before serving.

name: Mămăligă (Romanian Polenta)
description: Golden cornmeal porridge stirred until thick, the classic Romanian partner for stews, cheese and sour cream.
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a rolling boil in a heavy pot.
Pour the cornmeal in a thin steady stream while whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
Reduce the heat to low and cook for 25-30 minutes, stirring often with a wooden spoon, until it pulls away from the sides.
Stir in the butter, then turn out onto a board or into a bowl.
Let it set for 2 minutes and cut into wedges with a string or knife.

name: Varză Călită (Romanian Braised Cabbage)
description: Shredded cabbage slowly braised with onion, tomato paste, thyme and dill until sweet and silky.
instructions: Remove the outer leaves and core from the cabbage, then shred it finely.
Soften the chopped onions in the oil in a large pot over medium heat for 8 minutes.
Add the cabbage in batches with a pinch of salt, stirring until it wilts enough to fit.
Stir in the tomato paste, thyme, dill and bay leaves, and add a splash of water.
Cover and braise over low heat for 45-50 minutes, stirring occasionally, until very tender and lightly caramelised.
Season with salt and plenty of black pepper before serving.

name: Mâncare de Spanac (Romanian Garlicky Spinach)
description: Wilted spinach bound in a light milk and flour sauce with plenty of garlic, a Romanian spring staple.
instructions: Wash the spinach well, blanch in boiling salted water for 1 minute, drain and chop roughly.
Soften the finely chopped onion in the oil over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk to make a smooth sauce.
Add the spinach and crushed garlic and simmer for 8-10 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Season with salt and pepper; serve warm, traditionally with a fried egg on top.

name: Murături Rapide (Quick Pickled Vegetables)
description: Crunchy cucumber, carrot and cauliflower in a sweet-sour brine with garlic and mustard seeds, ready in a day.
instructions: Cut the cucumbers into spears, the carrots into sticks and the cauliflower into small florets.
Pack the vegetables tightly into clean jars with the peeled garlic cloves and bay leaves.
Bring the water, vinegar, sugar, salt and mustard seeds to a boil, stirring to dissolve.
Pour the hot brine over the vegetables to cover them completely.
Seal, cool to room temperature and refrigerate for at least 24 hours before eating; keeps 2 weeks.

name: Sote de Ciuperci (Garlic Mushroom Sauté)
description: Mushrooms seared in butter until golden, then tossed with garlic and a shower of parsley.
instructions: Wipe the mushrooms clean and halve or quarter them depending on size.
Heat the oil and butter in a large pan over high heat until foaming.
Add the mushrooms in a single layer and leave undisturbed for 3 minutes so they brown, then stir and cook 5 minutes more.
Add the crushed garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
