Season with salt and pepper, stir in the chopped parsley and serve.

name: Dovlecei Pane (Breaded Fried Zucchini)
description: Zucchini rounds coated in flour, egg and breadcrumbs, fried golden and served with cool sour cream.
instructions: Slice the zucchini into 1 cm rounds, salt them lightly and leave 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Set up three plates: flour seasoned with salt and pepper, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs.
Coat each slice in flour, dip in egg, then press into the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the slices in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with sour cream.

name: Conopidă Pane (Breaded Cauliflower)
description: Tender cauliflower florets in a crisp paprika breadcrumb crust, fried until golden brown.
instructions: Break the cauliflower into medium florets and boil in salted water for 5 minutes; drain and cool slightly.
Mix the breadcrumbs with the paprika; season the flour with salt and pepper; beat the eggs in a bowl.
Roll each floret in flour, dip in egg and coat well in the breadcrumbs.
Heat the oil in a deep pan over medium heat and fry the florets in batches for 3-4 minutes, turning, until golden.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with a little salt and serve hot.

name: Fasole Verde cu Usturoi (Green Beans with Garlic)
description: Blanched green beans tossed with raw garlic, oil, dill and a splash of vinegar, served warm or cold.
instructions: Trim the green beans and cook in boiling salted water for 6-8 minutes until tender but still bright.
Drain and rinse briefly under cold water to stop the cooking.
Crush the garlic with a pinch of salt and whisk with the oil and vinegar.
Toss the warm beans with the garlic dressing and the chopped dill.
Taste for salt and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Mazăre Sote (Buttered Peas with Dill)
description: Sweet green peas simmered briefly with soft onion and butter, finished with fresh dill.
instructions: Melt the butter in a saucepan and soften the finely chopped onion for 5 minutes without browning.
Add the peas and the broth, bring to a simmer and cook for 6-8 minutes until the peas are tender.
Let most of the liquid bubble away so the peas are glossy, not soupy.
Season with salt and pepper and stir in the chopped dill just before serving.

name: Zacuscă de Casă (Roasted Eggplant and Pepper Spread)
description: Slow-cooked spread of roasted eggplant, kapia peppers and onion in tomato, Romania's autumn pantry classic.
instructions: Roast the eggplants and peppers over a flame or under a hot grill until the skins are blackened; cover and let steam 15 minutes.
Peel both, drain the eggplants well and chop everything finely.
Cook the finely chopped onions in the oil in a large heavy pot over medium heat for 15 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the peppers, eggplant, tomato paste, bay leaves, sugar, salt and pepper.
Simmer uncovered over low heat for 60-90 minutes, stirring often, until thick and the oil rises to the surface.
Remove the bay leaves, spoon into sterilised jars and seal while hot.

name: Honey-Roasted Carrots with Thyme
description: Whole carrots roasted until caramelised at the edges in honey, olive oil and fresh thyme.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Peel the carrots and halve lengthways any that are thick so they cook evenly.
Toss with the olive oil, honey, thyme leaves, salt and pepper on a baking tray.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and sticky at the edges.

name: Roasted Broccoli with Garlic and Lemon
description: High-heat roasted broccoli with crispy charred tips, sliced garlic, chili flakes and lemon zest.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C.
Cut the broccoli into even florets and toss with the olive oil, sliced garlic, chili flakes and salt.
Spread on a baking tray in a single layer, cut sides down.
Roast for 18-20 minutes until the edges are crisp and lightly charred.
Grate over the lemon zest, squeeze over the juice and serve.

name: Spiced Roasted Cauliflower
description: Cauliflower florets roasted in cumin, turmeric and smoked paprika until golden, finished with lemon and parsley.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Cut the cauliflower into bite-sized florets.
Mix the olive oil with the cumin, turmeric, smoked paprika and salt, and toss the florets in it until well coated.
Spread on a baking tray and roast for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until golden and tender with crisp edges.
Squeeze over the lemon juice and scatter with chopped parsley.

name: Grilled Zucchini with Mint and Lemon
description: Charred zucchini ribbons dressed with olive oil, lemon, garlic and torn fresh mint.
instructions: Slice the zucchini lengthways into 5 mm ribbons and brush lightly with a little of the olive oil.
Heat a grill pan over high heat and grill the slices for 2-3 minutes per side until marked and tender.
Whisk the remaining olive oil with the lemon juice, finely grated garlic, salt and pepper.
Layer the warm zucchini on a platter, spoon over the dressing and scatter with torn mint leaves.
Rest 10 minutes to let the flavours soak in before serving.

name: Roasted Beetroot with Balsamic and Walnuts
description: Sweet roasted beetroot wedges glazed in balsamic vinegar and thyme, topped with toasted walnuts.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Peel the beetroot and cut into wedges; toss with the olive oil, thyme leaves, salt and pepper.
Spread on a baking tray, cover with foil and roast for 30 minutes.
Uncover, drizzle with the balsamic vinegar and roast 15-20 minutes more until tender and glossy.
Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes, chop roughly and scatter over the beetroot.

name: Roasted Pumpkin with Sage and Garlic
description: Caramelised pumpkin chunks roasted with whole garlic cloves and crisp sage, finished with pumpkin seeds.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Cut the pumpkin into 3 cm chunks, leaving the skin on if it is thin.
Toss with the olive oil, unpeeled garlic cloves, salt and pepper and spread on a baking tray.
Roast for 25 minutes, then add the sage leaves and pumpkin seeds and roast 8-10 minutes more until the pumpkin is tender and the sage crisp.
Squeeze the soft garlic from its skins over the pumpkin before serving.

name: Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Bacon
description: Halved sprouts roasted with bacon until crisp and caramelised, finished with a drizzle of balsamic glaze.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 210°C.
Trim the sprouts, halve them and toss with the olive oil, salt and pepper.
Spread cut side down on a baking tray and scatter over the chopped bacon.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, shaking the tray once, until the sprouts are browned and the bacon is crisp.
Drizzle with balsamic glaze and serve hot.

name: Braised Red Cabbage with Apples
description: Sweet-sour red cabbage slow-cooked with apple, cider vinegar, brown sugar and warm spices.
instructions: Quarter the cabbage, remove the core and shred finely; peel, core and dice the apples.
Melt the butter in a large pot and soften the sliced red onion for 5 minutes.
Add the cabbage, apples, vinegar, brown sugar, cloves, bay leaf and a good pinch of salt; stir well.
Cover and cook over low heat for 60-75 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the cabbage is very tender.
Remove the cloves and bay leaf, taste and adjust with more salt or vinegar.

name: Steakhouse Creamed Spinach
description: Rich spinach folded into a nutmeg-scented cream sauce with Parmesan, the classic steak companion.
instructions: Wilt the spinach in a large pan over high heat, drain in a colander and squeeze out as much liquid as possible; chop roughly.
Melt the butter in the same pan, add the crushed garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then whisk in the milk and cream until smooth and thickened.
Add the spinach, Parmesan and nutmeg and heat through for 3-4 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve hot.

name: Brown Sugar Glazed Carrots
description: Stovetop carrot coins simmered in butter and brown sugar until glossy, with a scatter of parsley.
instructions: Peel the carrots and slice into 1 cm coins.
Put the carrots, butter, brown sugar, water and a pinch of salt in a wide pan.
Bring to a boil, cover and simmer for 8 minutes until almost tender.
Uncover and cook over high heat for 5-6 minutes, shaking the pan, until the liquid reduces to a shiny glaze.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley and serve.

name: Cheesy Garlic Bread
description: A baguette slathered with garlic-parsley butter and Parmesan, baked until crunchy and golden.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Mash the softened butter with the crushed garlic, chopped parsley, Parmesan and a pinch of salt.
Cut the baguette into thick slices without cutting all the way through the base.
Spread the garlic butter generously between the slices and over the top.
Wrap loosely in foil and bake for 10 minutes, then open the foil and bake 5 minutes more until crisp.

name: Yorkshire Puddings
description: Tall, crisp, hollow batter puddings baked in smoking-hot oil, essential alongside a roast and gravy.
instructions: Whisk the flour, eggs, milk and salt into a smooth batter and rest it for at least 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 230°C and pour a little oil into each cup of a 12-hole muffin tin.
Heat the tin in the oven for 10 minutes until the oil is smoking hot.
Quickly pour the batter into the cups, filling each about halfway, and return to the oven immediately.
Bake for 20-25 minutes without opening the door until puffed, deep golden and crisp; serve at once.

name: Corn on the Cob with Chili-Lime Butter
description: Sweet corn cobs boiled or grilled and rolled in zesty chili-lime butter with fresh coriander.
instructions: Mash the softened butter with the lime zest, lime juice, chili powder and salt.
Husk the corn and boil in unsalted water for 8-10 minutes, or grill over high heat for 10 minutes, turning, until charred in spots.
Spread the chili-lime butter over the hot cobs so it melts and coats them.
Scatter with chopped coriander and serve with extra lime wedges.

name: Homemade Smoky Baked Beans
description: White beans simmered in a smoky, tangy tomato sauce with brown sugar and mustard, far better than the tin.
instructions: Soften the finely chopped onion in the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat for 6 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato sauce, brown sugar, mustard, smoked paprika and vinegar and bring to a simmer.
Drain and rinse the beans and add them to the sauce.
Simmer gently, uncovered, for 25-30 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and glossy.
Season with salt and serve hot on toast or alongside eggs and sausages.

name: Crispy Polenta Fries with Parmesan
description: Set polenta cut into batons and baked until golden and crunchy, dusted with Parmesan and rosemary.
instructions: Bring the water and salt to a boil and whisk in the cornmeal; cook over low heat for 25 minutes, stirring often.
Beat in the butter and half the Parmesan, then spread 2 cm thick in an oiled tray and chill for at least 1 hour until firm.
Preheat the oven to 220°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Cut the set polenta into thick fries, brush with olive oil and sprinkle with rosemary.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp; toss with the remaining Parmesan before serving.

name: Crispy Onion Rings
description: Thick onion rings in a crunchy paprika breadcrumb coating, deep-fried until golden brown.
instructions: Peel the onions, slice into 1 cm rings and separate them.
Set up three bowls: flour mixed with paprika and salt, eggs beaten with the milk, and breadcrumbs.
Dust each ring in flour, dip in the egg mixture, then coat in breadcrumbs, pressing to stick.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to 180°C and fry the rings in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden.
Drain on paper towels, sprinkle with salt and serve hot.

name: Caramelised Onions
description: Onions cooked low and slow in butter until deeply golden and jammy, finished with balsamic and thyme.
instructions: Peel and thinly slice the onions.
Heat the butter and olive oil in a wide heavy pan over medium-low heat and add the onions with the salt.
Cook for 35-40 minutes, stirring every few minutes and scraping the bottom, until soft and deep golden brown.
Stir in the brown sugar, balsamic vinegar and thyme leaves and cook 5 minutes more until sticky.
Serve warm, or cool and keep refrigerated for up to a week.

name: Creamy Cauliflower Mash
description: Silky low-carb mash of steamed cauliflower blended with garlic, cream cheese and Parmesan.
instructions: Cut the cauliflower into florets and steam or boil with the garlic cloves for 12-15 minutes until very tender.
Drain thoroughly and let it sit in the colander for 2 minutes so excess water evaporates.
Blend the cauliflower and garlic with the butter, cream cheese and Parmesan until smooth.
Season with salt and white pepper and serve hot.

name: Green Beans Almondine
description: Crisp-tender green beans tossed in nutty browned butter with toasted almonds, shallot and lemon.
instructions: Trim the beans and cook in boiling salted water for 5 minutes until crisp-tender; drain and refresh in cold water.
Melt the butter in a large pan over medium heat and toast the almonds for 2-3 minutes until golden.
Add the finely chopped shallot and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beans and toss for 2 minutes until hot and coated in butter.
Squeeze over the lemon juice, season with salt and pepper and serve.

name: Minted Pea Purée
description: Bright green pea purée blitzed with butter, fresh mint, a splash of cream and lemon.
instructions: Cook the peas in boiling salted water for 3-4 minutes until tender, then drain.
Blend the hot peas with the butter, mint leaves and cream until smooth, leaving a little texture if you like.
Add a squeeze of lemon juice and season with salt and pepper.
Return to the pan to warm through gently before serving.

name: Sage and Onion Stuffing
description: Buttery bread stuffing with soft onion, celery and fresh sage, baked until crisp on top and moist inside.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 180°C and butter a baking dish.
Tear the bread into small pieces and spread on a tray to dry out for 10 minutes in the oven.
Melt the butter in a pan and cook the chopped onions and celery for 8-10 minutes until soft.
Toss the bread with the onion mixture, chopped sage and parsley, salt and pepper.
Beat the egg into the broth, pour over the bread and mix gently until everything is moistened.
Spoon into the dish and bake for 35-40 minutes until golden and crisp on top.

name: Pateuri cu Brânză (Puff Pastry Cheese Pockets)
description: Golden puff pastry triangles stuffed with salty telemea and dill, the classic Romanian bakery snack.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C and line a baking tray with baking paper.
Mash the telemea with a fork, mix in the cottage cheese, one egg and the chopped dill.
Roll out the puff pastry and cut it into 10 cm squares.
Place a spoonful of filling in the centre of each square, fold into a triangle and press the edges with a fork to seal.
Beat the second egg and brush it over the pastries, then sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until puffed and golden; serve warm.

name: Saleuri (Romanian Cheese Sticks)
description: Crumbly, buttery cheese sticks with caraway seeds, the salty biscuit no Romanian party table is without.
instructions: Rub the cold cubed butter into the flour with the salt until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs.
Add the grated cascaval, sour cream and one egg yolk and knead briefly into a smooth dough; chill for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 180°C and line two trays with baking paper.
Roll the dough to 5 mm thickness and cut into 1 cm wide strips about 8 cm long.
Brush with the beaten remaining egg and sprinkle with caraway seeds and a little coarse salt.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until lightly golden and cool completely before serving.

name: Covrigei cu Sare (Salted Pretzel Rings)
description: Chewy little bread rings with a glossy crust and a crunchy coat of coarse salt, perfect for dipping.
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm water and let it foam for 5 minutes.
Mix in the flour, salt and oil and knead for 8 minutes into a smooth, elastic dough; cover and rise for 1 hour.
Divide the dough into 16 pieces, roll each into a 20 cm rope and pinch the ends together to form rings.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil with the baking soda and boil the rings for 30 seconds on each side.
Drain, place on a lined tray, brush with beaten egg and sprinkle generously with coarse salt.
Bake at 220°C for 15 to 18 minutes until deep golden brown.

ingredients.note: 1 tsp for dough, coarse salt for topping

name: Chifteluțe de Post (Vegan Vegetable Patties)
description: Crisp golden patties of grated potato, carrot and mushroom with dill and garlic, fried until crunchy.
instructions: Peel and coarsely grate the potatoes and carrots, then squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Finely chop the onion and mushrooms and sauté them in a little oil until the moisture evaporates.
Combine the vegetables with the crushed garlic, chopped dill, breadcrumbs and flour; season well with salt and pepper.
Shape the mixture with wet hands into small flat patties.
Fry in hot sunflower oil for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with mustard or a garlic sauce.

name: Bulz (Polenta Balls with Cheese)
description: Shepherd-style polenta balls hiding a molten telemea centre, baked with butter and served with sour cream.
instructions: Bring the water to a boil with the salt, pour in the cornmeal in a thin stream while whisking, and cook for 25 minutes, stirring often.
Let the polenta cool until you can handle it, then grease your hands with a little butter.
Take a handful of polenta, flatten it, place a cube of telemea and a little chopped smoked bacon in the centre and close into a ball.
Arrange the balls in a buttered oven dish and dot with the remaining butter.
Bake at 200°C for 20 minutes until the surface is golden and the cheese has melted.
Serve hot with a spoonful of sour cream on top.

name: Ouă Umplute (Romanian Deviled Eggs)
description: Hard-boiled egg halves piped with a creamy mustard-mayo yolk filling, dusted with sweet paprika.
instructions: Boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool them in cold water and peel.
Halve the eggs lengthwise and pop the yolks into a bowl.
Mash the yolks with the mayonnaise, mustard, finely chopped pickle and parsley; season with salt and pepper.
Spoon or pipe the filling back into the egg whites.
Dust with sweet paprika, chill for 20 minutes and serve on a platter.

name: Roșii Umplute cu Salată de Vinete (Tomatoes Stuffed with Eggplant Spread)
description: Juicy summer tomatoes hollowed out and filled with creamy roasted eggplant spread, topped with olives.
instructions: Cut a lid off each tomato and scoop out the seeds and pulp with a teaspoon; sprinkle the insides with salt and turn upside down for 10 minutes.
Mix the eggplant spread with the finely chopped red onion and half of the parsley.
Fill the tomatoes generously with the eggplant mixture.
Top each with an olive, a drizzle of olive oil and the remaining parsley.
Chill for 15 minutes and serve on a bed of lettuce leaves.

name: Cașcaval Pane (Breaded Fried Cheese)
description: Thick slices of cascaval in a crunchy paprika breadcrumb coat, fried until the centre oozes.
instructions: Cut the cascaval into 1.5 cm thick slices.
Set up three plates: flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs mixed with paprika and pepper.
Coat each slice in flour, dip in egg, then press into the breadcrumbs; repeat the egg and breadcrumb layer for a tight seal.
Heat 1 cm of oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the slices for about 1 minute per side until golden, working quickly so the cheese does not leak.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

name: Zacuscă on Toast
description: Toasted rye bread spread thick with smoky roasted pepper and eggplant zacuscă, finished with red onion rings.
instructions: Toast the rye bread slices until crisp on both sides.
Rub each warm slice lightly with the cut side of the garlic clove and drizzle with olive oil.
Spread a generous layer of zacuscă on every slice.
Top with thin red onion rings, chopped parsley and a grind of black pepper.
Cut in halves and serve at room temperature.

name: Langoși (Fried Dough with Cheese and Garlic)
description: Puffy fried yeast dough discs rubbed with garlic and piled with sour cream and crumbled telemea.
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm milk and let it foam for 5 minutes.
Add the flour and salt and knead into a soft dough; cover and let it rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Divide into 8 balls and stretch each into a thin 15 cm disc with your hands.
Heat 2 cm of oil in a deep pan and fry the discs for 1 to 2 minutes per side until puffed and golden.
Drain on paper towels, then rub each hot langoș with a cut garlic clove.
Spread with sour cream, scatter crumbled telemea over the top and serve immediately.

name: Classic Tomato Bruschetta
description: Garlic-rubbed toasted baguette topped with ripe diced tomatoes, torn basil and good olive oil.
instructions: Dice the tomatoes, discarding most of the seeds, and mix with torn basil, 2 tablespoons of olive oil, balsamic vinegar, salt and pepper; let stand 10 minutes.
Slice the baguette diagonally into 2 cm slices and brush with the remaining olive oil.
Toast the slices under a hot grill or in a pan until golden on both sides.
Rub each warm slice with the cut garlic clove.
Spoon the tomato mixture onto the toasts just before serving so they stay crisp.

name: Garlic Knots
description: Soft pizza-dough knots brushed with garlic butter and showered with parmesan and parsley.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C and line a tray with baking paper.
Roll the pizza dough into a rectangle and cut it into 12 strips about 2 cm wide.
Tie each strip loosely into a knot and arrange on the tray; let rest for 15 minutes.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden.
Meanwhile melt the butter with the crushed garlic and a pinch of salt over low heat for 2 minutes.
Brush the hot knots with the garlic butter and toss with grated parmesan and chopped parsley; serve with tomato sauce for dipping.

name: Cream Cheese Stuffed Mushrooms
description: Brown mushroom caps filled with garlicky herbed cream cheese and a crunchy parmesan crumb, baked until bubbling.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Wipe the mushrooms, remove the stems and chop the stems finely.
Sauté the chopped stems and garlic in 1 tablespoon of olive oil for 3 minutes until soft.
Mix the cooked stems with the cream cheese, half the parmesan, half the breadcrumbs and the chopped parsley; season with salt and pepper.
Fill each mushroom cap with the mixture and place in an oiled baking dish.
Top with the remaining breadcrumbs and parmesan and drizzle with the rest of the olive oil.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until the mushrooms are tender and the tops are golden.

name: Crispy Mozzarella Sticks
description: Double-breaded mozzarella batons fried until crunchy outside and stretchy inside, served with warm marinara.
instructions: Cut the mozzarella into 1.5 cm thick batons and pat them dry.
Mix the breadcrumbs with oregano, garlic powder and a pinch of salt.
Coat each stick in flour, dip in beaten egg, then roll in breadcrumbs; repeat the egg and crumb layers once more.
Freeze the coated sticks for at least 30 minutes so they hold their shape.
Heat 3 cm of oil to 180°C and fry the sticks in batches for about 1 minute until golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve right away with warm tomato sauce.

name: Loaded Nachos
description: A tray of tortilla chips buried under melted cheese, black beans, jalapeños and tomato, finished with sour cream.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C and spread the tortilla chips over a large baking tray.
Scatter the drained beans and half the grated cheese over the chips.
Top with the diced tomato, sliced chili pepper and the remaining cheese.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the cheese is fully melted and bubbling.
Finish with sliced green onions, chopped coriander and spoonfuls of sour cream; serve straight from the tray.

name: Chicken Quesadilla Bites
description: Crisp golden tortilla wedges packed with spiced chicken, peppers and melted cheese, cut into bite-size triangles.
instructions: Dice the chicken breast and bell pepper and fry in 1 tablespoon of oil with the cumin and a pinch of salt for 6 to 7 minutes until cooked.
Stir in the sliced green onions and remove from the heat.
Lay a tortilla in a dry pan, cover half with grated cheese, then the chicken mixture, then more cheese, and fold over.
Cook over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and the cheese has melted; repeat with the remaining tortillas.
Let rest for 1 minute, cut each quesadilla into 4 wedges and serve with sour cream.

name: Baked Vegetable Spring Rolls
description: Crisp oven-baked phyllo rolls filled with ginger-soy cabbage, carrot and bean sprouts, no deep frying needed.
instructions: Shred the cabbage and carrots finely and slice the green onions.
Stir-fry the vegetables with the grated ginger in 1 tablespoon of oil for 3 minutes, add the bean sprouts, soy sauce and sesame oil, cook 1 minute more and cool.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Cut the phyllo sheets in half, brush each with oil and stack two halves.
Place 2 tablespoons of filling near one edge, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Arrange seam-side down on a lined tray and brush the tops with oil.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp; serve with sweet chili sauce.

name: Loaded Potato Skins
description: Twice-baked crispy potato boats filled with melted cheddar and crumbled bacon, topped with sour cream and chives.
instructions: Bake the whole potatoes at 200°C for 50 minutes until tender, then cool slightly.
Fry the bacon until crisp, drain and crumble.
Halve the potatoes and scoop out most of the flesh, leaving a 1 cm shell.
Brush the shells inside and out with melted butter, season with salt and pepper and bake for 10 minutes until crisp.
Fill with grated cheese and bacon and return to the oven for 5 minutes until melted.
Top with sour cream and sliced green onions and serve hot.

name: Mini Ham and Cheese Quiches
description: Bite-size shortcrust tartlets filled with silky egg custard, diced ham, Emmental and chives.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 190°C and grease a 12-hole muffin tin.
Roll out the pastry, cut 10 cm circles and press them into the muffin holes.
Whisk the eggs with the cream, nutmeg, salt and pepper.
Divide the diced ham, grated Emmental and chopped chives between the pastry cases.
Pour the egg mixture over the filling until each case is nearly full.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the filling is set and golden; cool for 5 minutes before removing.

name: Sausage Rolls
description: Flaky golden puff pastry wrapped around seasoned sausage meat with onion, thyme and a hint of mustard.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C and line a tray with baking paper.
Squeeze the sausage meat out of the casings and mix it with the finely chopped onion, thyme, mustard and pepper.
Cut the puff pastry into two long strips and shape half the meat into a log down the centre of each.
Brush one edge with beaten egg, fold the pastry over the meat and press to seal; cut each log into 6 pieces.
Place seam-side down on the tray, brush with egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until puffed, golden and cooked through.

name: Parmesan Herb Popcorn
description: Freshly popped corn tossed in melted butter, grated parmesan, rosemary and garlic for a savoury movie-night snack.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large lidded pot over medium-high heat with 3 kernels inside.
When the test kernels pop, add the rest of the popcorn, cover and shake the pot occasionally until the popping slows to a few seconds apart.
Melt the butter in a small pan with the crushed rosemary and garlic powder.
Pour the popcorn into a large bowl, drizzle with the herb butter and toss well.
Sprinkle with the grated parmesan and salt, toss again and serve warm.

name: Crispy Roasted Chickpeas
description: Crunchy oven-roasted chickpeas dusted with smoked paprika, cumin and garlic, a healthy swap for chips.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Drain and rinse the chickpeas and dry them very well on a kitchen towel.
Toss the chickpeas with the olive oil and spread on a lined baking tray in a single layer.
Roast for 25 minutes, shaking the tray halfway through.
Mix the smoked paprika, cumin, garlic powder and salt and sprinkle over the hot chickpeas; toss to coat.
Return to the oven for 5 more minutes, then cool on the tray so they crisp up fully.

name: Crispy Kale Chips
description: Paper-thin kale leaves baked with olive oil, lemon and sea salt until they shatter like chips.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 150°C and line two trays with baking paper.
Strip the kale leaves from the tough stems, tear into chip-size pieces, wash and dry thoroughly.
Massage the leaves with the olive oil, lemon juice and garlic powder until lightly coated.
Spread in a single layer without overlapping and sprinkle with salt.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, rotating the trays once, until crisp but still green; cool for 3 minutes before eating.

name: Caprese Skewers
description: Cherry tomatoes, mini mozzarella balls and basil leaves threaded on picks and drizzled with balsamic glaze.
instructions: Drain the mozzarella balls and pat them dry.
Thread a cherry tomato, a folded basil leaf and a mozzarella ball onto each cocktail stick or short skewer.
Arrange the skewers on a serving platter.
Drizzle with olive oil and balsamic glaze and season with flaky salt and pepper just before serving.

name: Prosciutto-Wrapped Melon
description: Sweet ripe melon wedges wrapped in salty prosciutto with fresh mint and a crack of black pepper.
instructions: Halve the melon, scoop out the seeds and cut the flesh into 12 wedges, trimming off the rind.
Wrap each wedge with a slice of prosciutto, leaving the ends of the melon showing.
Arrange on a platter and tuck a mint leaf into each wrap.
Finish with a drizzle of balsamic glaze and freshly ground black pepper; serve chilled.

name: Smoked Salmon Blinis
description: Fluffy little homemade pancakes topped with dill sour cream, folds of smoked salmon and lemon zest.
instructions: Whisk the flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt, then beat in the egg and milk to make a thick, smooth batter.
Heat a little butter in a non-stick pan and drop in teaspoons of batter to make 5 cm blinis.
Cook for 1 minute until bubbles appear, flip and cook 30 seconds more; repeat with the remaining batter and cool.
Mix the sour cream with half the chopped dill and the lemon zest.
Top each blini with a dollop of dill cream, a fold of smoked salmon and a sprig of dill.
Finish with a squeeze of lemon juice and black pepper and serve within the hour.

name: Arancini (Fried Risotto Balls)
description: Golden breadcrumbed balls of parmesan risotto with a molten mozzarella heart, a Sicilian street-food classic.
instructions: Sauté the finely chopped onion in olive oil until soft, add the rice and stir for 1 minute.
Add the hot broth a ladle at a time, stirring until absorbed, for about 18 minutes until the rice is tender; stir in the parmesan and one egg, season, spread on a tray and chill for 1 hour.
With wet hands shape the cold risotto into golf-ball-size balls, pressing a cube of mozzarella into the centre of each and closing it over.
Roll the balls in flour, then the remaining beaten egg, then breadcrumbs.
Heat 4 cm of oil to 175°C and fry the arancini in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until deep golden.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with warm tomato sauce.

name: Cucumber Tea Sandwiches
description: Dainty crustless sandwiches of thin cucumber on herbed cream cheese, cool and crisp for an afternoon spread.
instructions: Slice the cucumber paper-thin, sprinkle lightly with salt and let drain on paper towels for 10 minutes.
Beat the cream cheese with the softened butter, chopped dill and chives until smooth.
Spread the mixture on all the bread slices right to the edges.
Layer the cucumber slices over half of the bread, season with pepper and close with the remaining slices.
Trim off the crusts and cut each sandwich into 4 fingers or triangles; serve immediately or cover with a damp cloth until needed.

name: Meatball Sour Soup (Ciorbă de Perișoare)
description: Tender pork and rice meatballs simmered in a tangy borș broth with root vegetables and lovage.
instructions: Dice the onion, carrots, bell pepper and celery root and sweat them in oil in a large pot for 5 minutes.
Add 2.5 litres of water and simmer for 15 minutes until the vegetables start to soften.
Mix the minced meat with the rice, one egg, salt and pepper and shape into walnut-sized meatballs.
Drop the meatballs into the simmering soup and cook for 20 minutes.
Add the grated tomatoes and the borș, bring back to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes.
Season with salt, stir in the chopped lovage and serve hot with sour cream.

name: Rădăuți Chicken Soup (Ciorbă Rădăuțeană)
description: Creamy Bukovina chicken soup thickened with sour cream and egg yolks, finished with garlic and vinegar.
instructions: Simmer the chicken breast with the carrots, parsnip, celery root and onion in 2.5 litres of salted water for 35 minutes.
Lift out the chicken, shred it and return it to the pot; discard the onion.
Whisk the sour cream with the egg yolks and flour, then temper with a few ladles of hot soup.
Pour the mixture back into the pot, stirring constantly, and heat gently without boiling.
Stir in the crushed garlic and vinegar, season with salt and pepper and sprinkle with parsley.

name: Tripe Soup (Ciorbă de Burtă)
description: Rich, velvety beef tripe soup with a sour cream and egg liaison, served with garlic sauce and hot peppers.
instructions: Rinse the tripe well, then boil it with the beef bones, carrots, celery root and onion in 3 litres of water for about 3 hours until tender.
Remove the tripe, slice it into thin strips and strain the broth back into the pot.
Return the tripe to the broth and season with salt.
Whisk the sour cream with the egg yolks and crushed garlic, temper with hot broth and stir into the soup off the heat.
Add the vinegar, adjust the seasoning and serve with extra garlic, hot peppers and sour cream on the side.

name: Bean Sour Soup with Smoked Pork Knuckle
description: Hearty white bean ciorbă with a smoked ham hock, soured with borș and scented with thyme and lovage.
instructions: Soak the beans overnight, drain and boil them in fresh water for 10 minutes, then drain again.
Simmer the beans with the smoked knuckle in 3 litres of water for about 1 hour until the beans are nearly tender.
Add the diced onion, carrots and bell pepper and cook for 20 minutes more.
Pull the meat off the bone, chop it and return it to the pot with the tomato paste and thyme.
Pour in the borș, boil for 10 minutes, season with salt and finish with chopped lovage.

name: Romanian Vegetable Sour Soup (Ciorbă de Legume)
description: Light, garden-fresh ciorbă packed with seasonal vegetables and soured with borș and lovage.
instructions: Dice the onion, carrots, celery root, bell pepper and potatoes.
Sweat the onion and carrots in oil for 5 minutes, then add 2.5 litres of water and the remaining root vegetables.
Simmer for 15 minutes, then add the potatoes, green beans and zucchini and cook for another 15 minutes.
Stir in the grated tomatoes and the borș and boil for 10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and finish with plenty of chopped lovage.

name: Greek-Style Chicken Sour Soup (Ciorbă à la Grec)
description: Silky chicken and rice soup finished with a sour cream, egg and lemon liaison the Romanian way.
instructions: Simmer the chicken thighs with the carrots, onion and parsley root in 2.5 litres of salted water for 35 minutes.
Remove the chicken, shred the meat and return it to the pot.
Add the rice and cook for 15 minutes until tender.
Whisk the sour cream with the egg yolks and lemon juice, temper with hot soup and stir in off the heat.
Season with salt and white pepper and sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving.

name: Sorrel Sour Soup (Ciorbă de Ștevie)
description: Springtime ciorbă of tangy sorrel leaves, rice and green onions, enriched with egg and sour cream.
instructions: Wash the sorrel thoroughly and chop it roughly along with the green onions.
Sweat the chopped green onions and diced carrots in oil for 4 minutes, then add 2 litres of water.
Add the rice and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the sorrel and the borș and boil for 5 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the sour cream, temper with hot soup and stir in off the heat.
Season with salt and finish with chopped dill.

name: Chicken Soup with Semolina Dumplings
description: Clear golden chicken broth with fluffy semolina dumplings, the classic Romanian supă cu găluște.
instructions: Cover the chicken pieces with 3 litres of cold water, bring to a boil and skim off the foam.
Add the whole carrots, parsnip, celery root and onion and simmer gently for 1 hour.
Strain the broth, dice the carrots and shred some of the chicken back into it.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt, fold in the semolina and let the batter rest for 10 minutes.
Drop teaspoons of batter into the barely simmering broth, cover and cook for 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Season with salt and serve sprinkled with parsley.

name: Potato Sour Soup with Smoked Bacon
description: Rustic Transylvanian ciorbă de cartofi with smoky bacon, sweet peppers and a sharp borș finish.
instructions: Dice the smoked bacon and render it in a large pot until golden.
Add the chopped onion, carrots and bell pepper and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in 2.5 litres of water, add the cubed potatoes and thyme and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the grated tomatoes and the borș and boil for 10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and stir in the chopped lovage before serving.

name: Danube Fish Sour Soup (Ciorbă de Pește)
description: Fisherman's carp ciorbă with tomatoes, peppers and borș, served with garlic sauce and hot chili.
instructions: Clean the carp and cut it into thick steaks; season with salt and set aside.
Simmer the diced onion, carrots, bell pepper and tomatoes in 2.5 litres of water for 20 minutes.
Add the borș and bring back to a rolling boil.
Slide in the fish pieces and simmer gently for 12 minutes without stirring.
Season with salt and lovage, and serve with crushed garlic mixed with a little broth and sliced chili on the side.

name: Lettuce Soup with Smoked Bacon (Ciorbă de Salată)
description: Transylvanian lettuce soup with crisp bacon, a garlicky sour cream base and ribbons of egg.
instructions: Fry the diced smoked bacon until crisp, add the chopped onion and soften for 3 minutes.
Stir in the flour, cook for 1 minute, then whisk in 1.5 litres of water and bring to a simmer.
Tear the lettuce into large pieces and add it to the pot with the crushed garlic; simmer for 5 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the sour cream, temper with hot soup and stir in off the heat.
Add the vinegar, season with salt and pepper and serve warm with chopped dill.

name: Zucchini Sour Soup with Sour Cream
description: Summery ciorbă de dovlecei with tender zucchini, rice, fresh dill and a swirl of sour cream.
instructions: Sweat the diced onion and carrots in oil for 5 minutes.
Add 2 litres of water and the rice and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the cubed zucchini and grated tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes until just tender.
Pour in the borș and boil for 5 minutes.
Stir the sour cream into a ladle of hot soup, return it to the pot and season with salt.
Finish with chopped dill and serve.

name: Pumpkin Cream Soup with Croutons
description: Velvety roasted pumpkin soup with a hint of nutmeg, topped with crunchy croutons and toasted seeds.
instructions: Roast the pumpkin cubes with a drizzle of oil at 200°C for 25 minutes until caramelised.
Soften the chopped onion and carrot in butter in a large pot for 5 minutes.
Add the roasted pumpkin, diced potato and vegetable broth and simmer for 15 minutes.
Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and nutmeg and season with salt and pepper.
Serve topped with croutons and toasted pumpkin seeds.

name: Kohlrabi Soup with Dill (Supă de Gulii)
description: Gentle, creamy kohlrabi and potato soup brightened with fresh dill, a Transylvanian favourite.
instructions: Peel and dice the kohlrabi, potatoes and carrot; chop the onion.
Melt the butter, soften the onion for 3 minutes, then add the vegetables and cook for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle over the flour, stir for 1 minute and gradually add the vegetable broth.
Simmer for 20 minutes until the kohlrabi is tender.
Stir in the sour cream, season with salt and pepper and finish with plenty of chopped dill.

name: Peasant Pork Sour Soup (Ciorbă Țărănească de Porc)
description: Chunky pork ciorbă loaded with potatoes, green beans, peppers and tomatoes, soured with borș.
instructions: Brown the pork cubes in oil in a large pot, then add 3 litres of water and simmer for 40 minutes, skimming the foam.
Add the diced onion, carrots, celery root and bell pepper and cook for 15 minutes.
Add the cubed potatoes and green beans and simmer for 15 minutes more.
Stir in the grated tomatoes and the borș and boil for 10 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and finish with chopped lovage; serve with sour cream.

name: Nettle Soup with Garlic (Supă de Urzici)
description: Vibrant green spring soup of young nettles, rice and garlic, lifted with lemon and a spoon of sour cream.
instructions: Wearing gloves, wash the nettles and blanch them in boiling water for 2 minutes; drain and chop.
Soften the chopped onion and green onions in oil for 4 minutes.
Add the rice and vegetable broth and simmer for 12 minutes.
Stir in the nettles and crushed garlic and cook for 5 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper and lemon juice and serve with a spoon of sour cream.

name: Lamb Sour Soup with Tarragon (Ciorbă de Miel)
description: Easter-style lamb ciorbă with spring onions, tarragon and a sour cream and egg finish.
instructions: Cover the lamb with 3 litres of cold water, bring to a boil and skim, then simmer for 50 minutes.
Add the diced carrots, parsley root and chopped green onions and cook for 15 minutes.
Add the rice and simmer for 15 minutes until tender.
Pour in the borș and boil for 5 minutes.
Whisk the egg yolks with the sour cream, temper with hot soup and stir in off the heat.
Season with salt and finish with chopped tarragon and lovage.

name: Solyanka
description: Bold Russian sweet-and-sour soup with smoked sausage, ham, pickles, olives and a lemon-sour cream topping.
instructions: Fry the sliced onion in oil for 5 minutes, add the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the diced smoked sausage and ham and brown lightly.
Pour in the beef broth, add the diced pickles and bay leaf and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the sliced olives and capers and cook for 5 minutes.
Season with pepper and a little pickle brine, then serve with a lemon slice and a spoon of sour cream.

name: Hungarian Goulash Soup (Gulyásleves)
description: Deep paprika-red beef soup with potatoes, peppers and caraway, somewhere between a stew and a broth.
instructions: Brown the beef cubes in oil in a heavy pot, then remove and set aside.
Soften the chopped onions in the same pot for 8 minutes, take off the heat and stir in the paprika and caraway.
Return the beef, add the garlic, tomatoes and beef broth and simmer covered for 1 hour.
Add the cubed potatoes, carrots and bell pepper and cook for 25 minutes until tender.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with crusty bread.

name: Minestrone
description: Classic Italian vegetable soup with beans, pasta and tomatoes, finished with basil and Parmesan.
instructions: Soften the diced onion, carrots and celery in olive oil for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and zucchini and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the drained beans and the pasta and cook until the pasta is al dente.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in torn basil and serve with grated Parmesan.

name: French Onion Soup
description: Deeply caramelised onions in rich beef broth, topped with toasted baguette and bubbling melted cheese.
instructions: Slice the onions thinly and cook them slowly in butter for 40 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden.
Sprinkle over the flour, cook for 1 minute, then deglaze with the white wine.
Add the beef broth, thyme and bay leaf and simmer for 20 minutes; season with salt and pepper.
Toast the baguette slices and ladle the soup into ovenproof bowls.
Top each bowl with toast and grated cheese and grill until golden and bubbling.

name: Green Lentil and Smoked Sausage Soup
description: Hearty, smoky lentil soup with kielbasa, root vegetables and a splash of red wine vinegar.
instructions: Brown the sliced smoked sausage in olive oil, then remove and set aside.
Soften the diced onion, carrots and celery in the same pot for 8 minutes; add the garlic.
Add the rinsed lentils, crushed tomatoes, bay leaf and vegetable broth and simmer for 30 minutes.
Return the sausage and cook for 10 minutes until the lentils are tender.
Season with salt, pepper and red wine vinegar and serve.

name: Spanish Chickpea and Spinach Soup
description: Smoky paprika-spiced chickpea soup with wilted spinach, tomatoes and a squeeze of lemon.
instructions: Soften the chopped onion in olive oil for 6 minutes, then add the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika.
Add the crushed tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the vegetable broth and the drained chickpeas and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the spinach and let it wilt for 2 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper and lemon juice and serve drizzled with olive oil.

name: Potato Leek Soup
description: Smooth, buttery French-style soup of leeks and potatoes finished with cream and chives.
instructions: Slice the leeks thinly and rinse well; peel and dice the potatoes.
Melt the butter and sweat the leeks gently for 10 minutes without colouring.
Add the potatoes and vegetable broth and simmer for 20 minutes until soft.
Blend until smooth, stir in the cream and season with salt and white pepper.
Serve sprinkled with chopped chives.

name: Thai Butternut Squash and Coconut Soup
description: Silky butternut squash soup with red curry paste, coconut milk, ginger and lime.
instructions: Peel and cube the butternut squash; chop the onion, garlic and ginger.
Soften the onion in oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic, ginger and curry paste and fry for 1 minute.
Add the squash and vegetable broth and simmer for 20 minutes until tender.
Blend until smooth, stir in the coconut milk and warm through.
Season with salt and lime juice and serve topped with fresh coriander.

name: Broccoli Cheddar Soup
description: Thick, cheesy American-style soup with tender broccoli florets and shredded carrot.
instructions: Melt the butter and soften the chopped onion for 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk and vegetable broth.
Add the broccoli florets and grated carrot and simmer for 15 minutes until tender.
Blend half the soup for a creamier texture, if desired, and return it to the pot.
Remove from the heat, stir in the grated cheddar until melted and season with salt, pepper and nutmeg.

name: Spanish Garlic Soup (Sopa de Ajo)
description: Castilian peasant soup of golden garlic, smoked paprika and day-old bread with a poached egg in each bowl.
instructions: Fry the sliced garlic gently in olive oil until golden, then add the diced ham.
Take off the heat, stir in the smoked paprika, then add the torn bread and toss to coat.
Pour in the chicken broth and simmer for 15 minutes until the bread breaks down.
Season with salt and pepper, then crack the eggs into the soup and poach for 3 minutes.
Serve immediately with chopped parsley.

name: Vietnamese-Style Beef Pho
description: Fragrant star anise and ginger beef broth over rice noodles with paper-thin beef, herbs and lime.
instructions: Char the halved onion and ginger in a dry pan until blackened in spots.
Simmer the beef broth with the charred onion, ginger, star anise and cinnamon for 30 minutes, then strain.
Season the broth with fish sauce and a pinch of sugar.
Cook the rice noodles according to the pack and divide between bowls.
Top with very thinly sliced raw beef and pour over the boiling broth to cook it.
Serve with bean sprouts, basil, green onions and lime wedges.

name: Miso Ramen with Pork Belly
description: Savoury miso and garlic ramen broth with springy noodles, sliced pork belly and a soft-boiled egg.
instructions: Season the pork belly, roast it at 180°C for 50 minutes until tender, then slice.
Soft-boil the eggs for 7 minutes, cool in iced water and peel.
Fry the chopped garlic and ginger in sesame oil for 1 minute, add the chicken broth and simmer for 10 minutes.
Whisk in the miso paste and soy sauce and keep hot without boiling.
Cook the ramen noodles and the bok choy according to the pack.
Divide the noodles between bowls, pour over the broth and top with pork, halved eggs, bok choy, corn and green onions.

name: Tom Yum-Style Shrimp Soup
description: Hot and sour Thai broth with juicy shrimp, mushrooms, chili, lime and fresh coriander.
instructions: Bring the chicken broth to a simmer with the sliced ginger, bruised chili and curry paste.
Add the halved mushrooms and cherry tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the shrimp and simmer for 3 minutes until pink.
Season with fish sauce, lime juice and a pinch of sugar, tasting for a hot-sour balance.
Serve topped with fresh coriander and sliced green onions.

name: Miso Soup with Tofu and Mushrooms
description: Light Japanese miso broth with silky tofu cubes, mushrooms, spinach and spring onions, ready in minutes.
instructions: Bring the vegetable broth to a gentle simmer with the sliced mushrooms and ginger.
Cook for 5 minutes, then add the spinach and cubed tofu and warm for 2 minutes.
Take off the heat and whisk the miso paste with a ladle of broth until smooth, then stir it back in.
Season with soy sauce and a few drops of sesame oil.
Serve immediately topped with sliced green onions.

name: Split Pea and Ham Soup
description: Thick, smoky yellow split pea soup slow-cooked with a ham hock, carrots and bay.
instructions: Rinse the split peas and place them in a large pot with the ham hock and 2.5 litres of water.
Bring to a boil, skim, then add the diced onion, carrots, celery, garlic, bay leaf and thyme.
Simmer for about 90 minutes, stirring now and then, until the peas have broken down.
Remove the hock, shred the meat and stir it back into the soup.
Season with salt and pepper and loosen with a little water if too thick.

name: Mushroom Barley Soup
description: Earthy brown mushroom and pearl barley soup with thyme and a savoury splash of soy sauce.
instructions: Brown the sliced mushrooms in olive oil in batches until golden, then set aside.
Soften the diced onion, carrots and celery in the same pot for 8 minutes; add the garlic and thyme.
Add the rinsed barley and vegetable broth and simmer for 35 minutes.
Return the mushrooms, add the soy sauce and cook for 10 minutes until the barley is tender.
Season with salt and pepper and serve sprinkled with parsley.

name: Tuscan White Bean and Kale Soup
description: Rustic Italian soup of cannellini beans, kale and rosemary in a tomato-tinged broth with Parmesan.
instructions: Soften the diced onion, carrots and celery in olive oil for 8 minutes.
Add the garlic and rosemary and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth, add the drained beans and simmer for 15 minutes.
Mash a few beans against the side of the pot to thicken, then stir in the chopped kale and cook for 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with grated Parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Corn Chowder with Bacon
description: Creamy American sweetcorn and potato chowder with crispy bacon bits and chives.
instructions: Fry the diced bacon until crisp, remove and set aside, leaving the fat in the pot.
Add the butter, chopped onion and celery and soften for 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour, then gradually add the chicken broth and the diced potatoes; simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the drained corn and the milk and simmer for 5 minutes more.
Stir in the cream, season with salt and pepper and serve topped with bacon and chives.

name: Creamy Cod and Potato Chowder
description: New England-style fish chowder with flaky cod, potatoes, leek and bacon in a creamy milk broth.
instructions: Fry the diced bacon until golden, then add the butter, sliced leek and chopped onion and soften for 6 minutes.
Sprinkle over the flour, stir, then add the diced potatoes, bay leaf and 500 ml of water; simmer for 15 minutes.
Pour in the milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the cod in large chunks and poach for 5 minutes until just flaking.
Stir in the cream, season with salt and pepper and serve with chopped parsley.

name: Carrot and Ginger Soup
description: Bright, sweet carrot soup with warming ginger, a touch of orange and a swirl of coconut milk.
instructions: Soften the chopped onion in olive oil for 5 minutes, then add the garlic, grated ginger and cumin.
Add the sliced carrots and vegetable broth and simmer for 25 minutes until very soft.
Blend until completely smooth.
Stir in the coconut milk and the juice of the orange and warm through.
Season with salt and pepper and serve with a drizzle of coconut milk.

name: Cauliflower Cream Soup with Parmesan
description: Luxuriously smooth cauliflower soup with garlic, nutmeg and Parmesan, low in carbs and big on comfort.
instructions: Cut the cauliflower into florets and chop the onion and garlic.
Melt the butter and sweat the onion and garlic for 5 minutes without browning.
Add the cauliflower, potato and vegetable broth and simmer for 20 minutes until tender.
Blend until silky, then stir in the cream and grated Parmesan.
Season with salt, white pepper and nutmeg and serve.

name: Zucchini and Basil Cream Soup
description: Light green zucchini soup blended with cream cheese and fresh basil for a summery, velvety bowl.
instructions: Soften the chopped onion and garlic in olive oil for 5 minutes.
Add the sliced zucchini and diced potato, pour in the vegetable broth and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the basil leaves and blend until smooth.
Whisk in the cream cheese until melted and season with salt and pepper.
Serve warm or chilled with a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Portuguese Caldo Verde
description: Portugal's beloved potato and kale soup with slices of smoky chorizo and good olive oil.
instructions: Soften the chopped onion and garlic in olive oil for 5 minutes.
Add the diced potatoes and vegetable broth and simmer for 20 minutes until soft.
Blend the soup until smooth and return it to the pot.
Fry the sliced chorizo in a pan until crisp at the edges.
Stir the finely shredded kale into the soup and cook for 5 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper and serve topped with chorizo and a drizzle of olive oil.

name: Moroccan Harira
description: Warmly spiced Moroccan soup of lamb, chickpeas, lentils and tomatoes with fresh coriander and lemon.
instructions: Brown the diced lamb in olive oil, then add the chopped onion and celery and soften for 5 minutes.
Stir in the turmeric, cinnamon, ginger powder and pepper and cook for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes, lentils and 2 litres of water and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add the drained chickpeas and half the chopped herbs and cook for 15 minutes.
Whisk the flour with a little cold water, stir it in and simmer for 5 minutes to thicken.
Season with salt and lemon juice and serve with the remaining coriander and parsley.

name: Coconut Red Lentil Dal Soup
description: Creamy Indian-spiced red lentil soup with coconut milk, turmeric and garam masala.
instructions: Fry the chopped onion in oil for 6 minutes, then add the garlic, grated ginger, turmeric and cumin.
Add the rinsed red lentils, crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the coconut milk and garam masala and cook for 5 minutes more.
Season with salt and lime juice.
Serve topped with fresh coriander and a little chili if you like heat.

name: Ukrainian Borscht
description: Ruby-red beetroot and beef soup with cabbage, potatoes and garlic, served with sour cream and dill.
instructions: Simmer the beef in 2.5 litres of water with a bay leaf for 1 hour, skimming, then dice the meat and return it to the broth.
Grate the beetroot and carrots and fry them with the chopped onion in oil for 8 minutes; stir in the tomato paste and vinegar.
Add the diced potatoes to the broth and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the shredded cabbage and the beetroot mixture and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the crushed garlic, season with salt and pepper and rest for 10 minutes.
Serve with sour cream and chopped dill.

name: Mexican Chicken Tortilla Soup
description: Smoky tomato and chili chicken soup topped with crunchy tortilla strips, avocado and lime.
instructions: Soften the chopped onion in oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic, chopped chili and cumin and fry for 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes and chicken broth and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the chicken breast and poach for 15 minutes, then shred it and return to the pot with the drained corn and beans.
Cut the tortillas into strips and fry them in oil until crisp.
Season the soup with salt and lime juice and serve topped with tortilla strips, diced avocado and coriander.

name: Italian Wedding Soup
description: Little Parmesan meatballs, orzo and spinach in a light chicken broth, an Italian-American classic.
instructions: Mix the minced turkey with the breadcrumbs, grated Parmesan, egg, half the garlic, salt and pepper and roll into small meatballs.
Soften the chopped onion and diced carrots in olive oil for 6 minutes; add the remaining garlic.
Pour in the chicken broth, bring to a simmer and drop in the meatballs; cook for 10 minutes.
Add the orzo and cook for 8 minutes until tender.
Stir in the spinach until wilted, season with salt and pepper and serve with extra Parmesan.
